Genetics of follicular lymphoma and othe.domain: Genetics of follicular lymphoma and other indolent B-cell lymphomas (FL; marginal zone/MALT; lymphoplasmacytic/Waldenström) — mechanism and calibration numbers for a cell-level / agent-based simulation

key_facts.fact: t(14;18)(q32;q21) BCL2::IGH is the FL hallmark but its prevalence is population- and stage-dependent, not universal. Asian FL cohorts are markedly lower, and localized FL is often negative.
key_facts.numbers: ~85% of FL overall (Western 80-90%); 47-60% in Chinese/Asian cohorts (47% in a 131-case WGS series); absent in ~15% of stage III/IV and ~50% of stage I/II FL; grade 3A/B FL 18-38%
key_facts.source: Brisou, Nadel & Roulland 2021, HemaSphere (PMC8171372); Ren 2025, Cell Reports Medicine (PMID 40780199)

key_facts.fact: The translocation is a V(D)J recombination error in bone-marrow pre-B cells: RAG-mediated breaks at IGH J segments (14q32) are misjoined to BCL2 (18q21), placing BCL2 under IGH enhancer control, giving constitutive BCL2 in cells that should downregulate it in the germinal centre.
key_facts.numbers: Occurs at the pre-B stage, i.e. before any antigen exposure; the initiating hit precedes GC entry
key_facts.source: Brisou 2021 HemaSphere (PMC8171372); Sterrenberg 2022, Trends in Cancer (PMC9248772); Tsujimoto 1985 Science (background)

key_facts.fact: t(14;18)-positive B cells circulate in a large fraction of healthy adults, with strongly age-dependent prevalence — undetectable in children, plateauing after age 50.
key_facts.numbers: 46% of 715 healthy individuals (327/715) overall; 0% under age 10; rising to 66% by age 50; mean frequency 18-26 x 10^-6 in those >=40 vs 7-9 x 10^-6 in younger; 4% (31/715) carried >1 positive cell per 25,000 PBMNC
key_facts.source: Schüler 2009, International Journal of Cancer (PMID 19030176, PMC4216731)

key_facts.fact: Clone size, not mere presence, is the discriminating variable. FL patients carry the same lesion at ~4 orders of magnitude higher burden than healthy carriers.
key_facts.numbers: Healthy median ~1 positive cell per 10^6 B cells; stage III/IV FL patients median ~9,200 positive cells per 10^6 PBMNC (~1%)
key_facts.source: Schüler 2009 Int J Cancer (PMID 19030176); Brisou 2021 HemaSphere (PMC8171372)

key_facts.fact: In a prospective cohort, high circulating t(14;18) frequency years before diagnosis predicted FL, and prediagnostic blood clones were molecularly identical to the later tumour.
key_facts.numbers: EPIC cohort, 520,000 enrolled; 100 incident FL vs 218 controls; frequency >10^-4 gave OR 23.17 (95% CI 9.1-) for subsequent FL up to 15 years later; ~20% of future-FL cases exceeded that threshold; identical clone confirmed up to 10 years pre-diagnosis
key_facts.source: Roulland 2014, Journal of Clinical Oncology (PMID 24687831); Brisou 2021 HemaSphere (PMC8171372)

key_facts.fact: The carrier cell in healthy people is not a quiescent naive B cell but an expanded, germinal-centre-experienced 'FL-like cell' with AID activity; BCL2-overexpressing cells need multiple GC re-entries before acquiring the FL developmental arrest.
key_facts.numbers: >70% of healthy individuals carry such cells at ~10^-6; progression requires iterative GC transits over decades
key_facts.source: Roulland 2006, Journal of Experimental Medicine (PMID 17043145); Sungalee 2014, J Clin Invest (PMID 25384217)

key_facts.fact: Necessary-but-not-sufficient, quantified: roughly half of healthy adults carry the lesion while FL incidence is ~2.4 per 100,000 per year, implying a per-carrier annual conversion probability of order 10^-5 to 10^-6.
key_facts.numbers: carrier prevalence 46-70%; US age-adjusted FL incidence 2.4/100,000/yr (SEER 2019-2023); derived per-carrier annual conversion ~5 x 10^-6
key_facts.source: SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Follicular Lymphoma (seer.cancer.gov/statfacts/html/follicular.html); ratio is my own arithmetic

key_facts.fact: FL is described as fundamentally epigenetic because essentially every tumour carries a chromatin-modifier lesion, and most carry two or more — a near-obligate second class of hit alongside BCL2.
key_facts.numbers: chromatin-modifier mutation in 96% of FL tumours; >=2 such mutations in 76%
key_facts.source: Green 2015, PNAS (PMID 25713363, PMC4364211)

key_facts.fact: Per-gene chromatin-modifier frequencies from targeted sequencing of 113 FL tumours (1,716-gene panel, mostly treatment-naive).
key_facts.numbers: KMT2D/MLL2 60.0%; CREBBP 52.4%; EP300 19.0%; EZH2 17.0%; MEF2B 7.6%; ARID1A 5.7%; any SWI/SNF component 30.5%; histone (linker/core) gene mutations 43.8%, co-occurring in 17.1%
key_facts.source: Krysiak 2017, Blood (PMID 28064239, PMC5270390)

key_facts.fact: Larger/deeper series give higher CREBBP and KMT2D estimates than the Krysiak panel; use ranges, not point values. Reported KMT2D reaches 80-90% and CREBBP 60-90% depending on cohort and assay.
key_facts.numbers: CREBBP 60-70% (review); KMT2D up to 80% FL; systemic-FL cutaneous involvement series: CREBBP 90%, KMT2D 90%, EP300 30%; ARID1A ~11% FL; HIST1H1C/E ~44% FL
key_facts.source: Collin 2025, Histopathology (PMID 39468961); Mondello 2022, Frontiers in Genetics (PMC8883034); Combalia 2026, HemaSphere (PMID 42256548)

key_facts.fact: EZH2 gain-of-function is always heterozygous and biochemically cooperative: Y641 mutants are poor at H3K27me0→me1 but hyper-efficient at me2→me3, so hyper-trimethylation requires the wild-type allele (or EZH1) alongside.
key_facts.numbers: EZH2 GOF in ~25% of FL (17% in Krysiak); tazemetostat ORR 69% in EZH2-mutant vs 35% in EZH2-wild-type FL
key_facts.source: Sneeringer 2010, PNAS (PMID 21078963); Collin 2025, Histopathology (PMID 39468961)

key_facts.fact: TNFRSF14/HVEM and EPHA7 are the two recurrent microenvironment-facing tumour suppressors. HVEM loss disrupts the inhibitory HVEM-BTLA interaction, driving cell-autonomous proliferation plus stromal activation and TFH recruitment; EPHA7 is the 6q-deletion target and acts via a secreted splice variant.
key_facts.numbers: HVEM/TNFRSF14 mutated in 28% of 141 FL (35% of those homozygous; 65% missense, 32.5% nonsense); ~31% of FL are HVEM protein-negative by IHC; EPHA7 inactivated in 72% of FL
key_facts.source: Boice 2016, Cell (PMID 27693350, PMC5221752); Oricchio 2011, Cell (PMID 22036564)

key_facts.fact: CREBBP KAT-domain mutation is an early, precursor-stage event — detectable in prediagnostic blood years ahead of FL and specific to people who go on to develop it, unlike the BCL2 translocation itself.
key_facts.numbers: CREBBP KAT mutations in 14/48 (29%) of prediagnostic FL subjects vs 0/13 healthy BCL2-rearranged and 0/20 healthy controls (p=0.03, p=0.007); median lead time 5.8 years
key_facts.source: Schroers-Martin 2023, Cancer Discovery (PMID 36939219, PMC10239329)

key_facts.fact: CREBBP loss causes focal enhancer H3K27ac depletion at CIITA/MHC-II loci, left unopposed by BCL6/SMRT/HDAC3; the consequence is reduced surface MHC class II, weaker autologous T-cell stimulation and fewer tumour-infiltrating CD4 T cells. MHC-II deletion phenocopies it; CD4 depletion mimics the benefit to the tumour; HDAC3 inhibition reverses it.
key_facts.numbers: CREBBP mutated in ~52-70% of FL; effect is a graded reduction in MHC-II transcript and protein, with reduced CD4 helper and CD8 memory T-cell frequencies
key_facts.source: Green 2015, PNAS (PMID 25713363); Jiang 2017, Cancer Discovery (PMID 27733359); Hashwah 2017, PNAS (PMID 28831000)

key_facts.fact: MALT lymphoma is driven by NF-kB-activating translocations whose frequency is site-specific; API2(BIRC3)-MALT1 works by cleaving NIK, giving constitutive non-canonical NF-kB and hence antigen independence. Marginal-zone disease is otherwise an antigen-driven, chronic-stimulation model. Waldenström is dominated by MYD88 L265P.
key_facts.numbers: t(11;18) API2-MALT1: lung 40%, stomach 20-25%, intestinal 33%, ocular adnexa 10%; t(1;14) BCL10-IGH 1-2%; t(3;14) FOXP1-IGH thyroid 7-56%. Gastric MALT H. pylori-positive ~80% (20.5% negative, 95% CI 17.0-24.6); eradication alone gives CR 70-80% if Hp-positive vs 15-30% if Hp-negative; t(11;18) present in 47% (stage IE) and 68% (>=IIE) of eradication non-responders but only 3% of responders. WM: MYD88 L265P 80-95%, CXCR4 WHIM-like 30-40% (mostly C-terminal nonsense/frameshift, commonest S338X). SMZL: KLF2 50%, NOTCH2 25%, KMT2D 25%, del(7q) 27%
key_facts.source: Rodríguez-Sevilla & Salar 2021, Cancers (PMC8750177); Matysiak-Budnik 2023, Cancers (PMC10417821); Lv 2025, Clin Transl Gastroenterol (PMID 39450888); Růžičková 2026, IJMS (PMC13299230); Parker 2026, Blood Advances (PMID 42200578)

mechanisms: FL initiation is a two-compartment, two-epoch process. Epoch 1: RAG-mediated BCL2::IGH misjoining in a bone-marrow pre-B cell — antigen-independent, before any GC. Epoch 2: the resulting BCL2-high cell survives GC selection it should not survive, exits as a memory-like cell, and re-enters germinal centres repeatedly over decades, each transit exposing it to AID-driven somatic hypermutation and a fresh chance at a cooperating hit (Roulland 2006 JEM; Sungalee 2014 JCI). This is why FL is best modelled as recurrent excursions through a mutator compartment, not one-shot accumulation.

BCL2 deregulation is permissive, not proliferative. It removes apoptosis as the GC quality-control filter; it does not itself increase division rate. In an ABM this is a change to a death hazard, not to a birth rate.

Mutation order is non-random and is the main structural constraint. BCL2 translocation is earliest; CREBBP (specifically KAT-domain) is the next committed lesion, present in prediagnostic blood a median 5.8 years before diagnosis; KMT2D and TNFRSF14 are later/subclonal events (Green 2013 Blood; Green 2015 PNAS; Schroers-Martin 2023 Cancer Discovery). Model as an ordered DAG, not an unordered hit-accumulation.

The chromatin-modifier lesions converge on one functional module: the 'GC-exit / immune-recognition' program. CREBBP/EP300 (H3K27 acetylation at enhancers), KMT2D (H3K4me1/2 at enhancers), TET2 (5hmC, required for CREBBP-dependent acetylation) act at enhancers; EZH2 and ARID1A act at promoters. All of them reduce MHC class II, CD40 and interferon responsiveness (Mondello 2022 Front Genet). One shared output variable can represent several distinct genotypes.

CREBBP-loss immune escape is mechanistically a de-repression failure, not a deletion. Enhancers are counter-regulated by BCL6/SMRT/HDAC3; without CREBBP acetyltransferase activity, deacetylation is unopposed and CIITA/MHC-II stays off. This makes it pharmacologically reversible (HDAC3 inhibition restores MHC-II and T-cell killing), which is an actionable perturbation to include in a sim (Jiang 2017 Cancer Discov; Mondello et al.).

EZH2 Y641 is a substrate-preference switch requiring enzymatic cooperation with the wild-type allele: mutant PRC2 cannot efficiently do me0→me1 but is hyper-efficient at me2→me3 (Sneeringer 2010 PNAS). A single-parameter 'gain of EZH2 activity' will mis-model this; it needs two sequential reactions with different catalysts.

TNFRSF14/HVEM loss is a microenvironment-coupling lesion: it breaks the HVEM-BTLA inhibitory ligation between tumour B cell and TFH/stroma, simultaneously raising B-cell proliferation and recruiting TFH and activating lymphoid stroma (Boice 2016 Cell). It is a cell-cell interaction rule, not a cell-intrinsic parameter.

EPHA7 acts as an extrinsic (secreted) tumour suppressor — a soluble splice variant that blocks oncogenic Eph signalling in neighbouring cells (Oricchio 2011 Cell). Loss therefore has a diffusible, neighbourhood-scale effect, distinct from the cell-autonomous lesions.

Marginal-zone/MALT lymphomagenesis is antigen-addiction: chronic H. pylori-driven (or autoantigen-driven) T-cell-dependent stimulation supplies the proliferation signal. API2(BIRC3)-MALT1 from t(11;18) cleaves NIK and activates non-canonical NF-kB cell-autonomously, which is exactly why those cases stop responding to antigen removal. This gives a clean, testable binary switch: antigen-dependent vs antigen-independent growth.

Waldenström is a constitutive-innate-signalling disease: MYD88 L265P allows myddosome assembly (MYD88-IRAK1/4-BTK-HCK) without TLR/IL-1R ligand, giving ligand-independent NF-kB. CXCR4 C-terminal truncation (S338X) removes the receptor's internalisation/desensitisation, giving sustained AKT/ERK and marrow retention — hence BTK-inhibitor resistance.
modellable: Initiation rate and carrier pool: seed t(14;18)+ cells with an age-dependent process calibrated to zero prevalence under age 10, ~66% prevalence by age 50, plateau thereafter; steady-state clone frequency mean 7-9 x 10^-6 of PBMNC under 40 and 18-26 x 10^-6 at >=40. (Schüler 2009)

Calibration target for the full progression pipeline: per-carrier annual conversion to overt FL of order 5 x 10^-6 (carrier prevalence 46-70% against FL incidence 2.4 per 100,000 per year). Any simulation whose carriers convert faster than ~1e-5/yr is wrong.

Risk threshold as a state variable: blood clone frequency >10^-4 confers OR 23.2 for FL within 15 years; ~20% of eventual FL patients cross that threshold prediagnostically. Use 10^-4 as a discrete 'committed precursor' state boundary.
Terminal burden: overt stage III/IV FL corresponds to median 9,200 t(14;18)+ cells per 10^6 PBMNC (~0.9%). Gives a stop condition ~4 logs above the healthy carrier state.

Latency: identical prediagnostic blood clones detected up to 10-15 years before diagnosis; CREBBP KAT hit median 5.8 years before diagnosis. Use decades for GC-recycling epoch, ~6 years for the committed-precursor-to-diagnosis interval.

Per-agent genotype sampler for a synthetic FL cohort (draw with these marginals, then enforce constraints): KMT2D 0.60-0.85, CREBBP 0.52-0.70, EP300 0.19, EZH2 GOF 0.17-0.25, ARID1A 0.06-0.11, TNFRSF14 0.28, EPHA7 loss/6q 0.72, any SWI/SNF 0.31, histone/linker-histone 0.44. Constraints: >=1 chromatin modifier in 96% of agents, >=2 in 76%; CREBBP and EP300 largely mutually exclusive; EZH2 mutations heterozygous only (never homozygous).
Ordering rule (DAG edges): BCL2::IGH -> CREBBP(KAT) -> {KMT2D, TNFRSF14, EZH2, EP300}. TNFRSF14 and KMT2D should be allowed as subclonal/late; CREBBP should be clonal in the founder when present.

MHC class II as a continuous per-agent surface variable: CREBBP-mutant agents get a graded reduction (transcript and protein), which reduces (a) probability of productive CD4 T-cell contact, (b) T-cell proliferation induced per contact, and (c) local CD4-helper and CD8-memory densities. MHC-II = 0 phenocopies CREBBP loss; CD4 T-cell removal abolishes the fitness difference — both are validation checks the model should reproduce.

Reversibility perturbation: HDAC3 inhibition restores enhancer H3K27ac, MHC-II and T-cell killing preferentially in CREBBP-mutant agents. Implement as a switch that resets the MHC-II variable and re-couples the CD4 killing term, with larger effect in CREBBP-mutant than wild-type agents.

EZH2 as two sequential reactions: reaction A (me0->me1) catalysed efficiently only by WT EZH2/EZH1; reaction B (me1->me2->me3) catalysed hyper-efficiently by Y641 mutant. Requires both alleles present. Drug response asymmetry to reproduce: response rate 69% mutant vs 35% wild-type under EZH2 inhibition.

TNFRSF14/EPHA7 as interaction rules, not intrinsic rates: HVEM-null agents lose an inhibitory contact term with BTLA+ TFH and gain a TFH-recruitment and stromal-activation term. EPHA7-null agents stop secreting a diffusible suppressor, so the effect radius should be neighbourhood-scale, not single-cell.

MALT/MZL antigen-dependence switch: agents carry a binary 'antigen-dependent' flag. Antigen removal (eradication) drives extinction with probability 0.70-0.80 for antigen-dependent, H. pylori-positive gastric agents; 0.15-0.30 for antigen-negative; ~0.03 for t(11;18)/API2-MALT1-positive (constitutive NF-kB) agents. Site-specific t(11;18) prevalence: lung 0.40, stomach 0.20-0.25, intestine 0.33, ocular adnexa 0.10.

MALT NF-kB pathway occupancy: in one Hp-negative gastric series, MALT1 translocation 39%, plus TNFAIP3 23%, CARD11 9%, MAP3K14 9%, with NF-kB pathway hit in 86% of cases overall and mutations mutually exclusive with MALT1 translocation — a good mutual-exclusivity constraint for a pathway-level model.

WM agents: MYD88 L265P in 0.80-0.95 (constitutive myddosome -> ligand-independent NF-kB, so no TLR-ligand input term needed); CXCR4 truncation in 0.30-0.40, implemented as loss of receptor internalisation -> reduced marrow egress rate + sustained AKT/ERK + BTK-inhibitor resistance flag. SMZL agents: KLF2 0.50, NOTCH2 0.25, KMT2D 0.25, del(7q) 0.27.

Spatial/compartment note: FL involves bone marrow in ~70% of cases, and high blood t(14;18) frequency correlates with high marrow frequency — so blood, lymph node/GC, and marrow should be three connected compartments with exchange, not one well-mixed pool. (Dessauge 2025, Blood Advances, PMC12274835; Brisou 2021)
open_questions: What is the actual number of germinal-centre re-entries required before a BCL2+ cell reaches FL-associated developmental arrest? Sungalee 2014 shows 'multiple' but does not give a distribution — this is a free parameter you will have to fit or sensitivity-scan.

Why do >99.99% of t(14;18) carriers never convert? Is the bottleneck stochastic (waiting for CREBBP), immunological (CD4 surveillance clearing precursors), or niche-limited (no available GC/marrow niche)? These three make different, testable predictions in an ABM.

What fraction of the healthy-carrier pool already carries a second hit? Schroers-Martin found 0/13 healthy BCL2-rearranged individuals with CREBBP KAT mutations, but n=13 is far too small to bound the rate.

Is the t(14;18)-negative half of localized/Asian FL a different disease with a different initiating hit, or the same pathway with an alternative apoptosis-block? It shares chromatin-modifier mutations, which argues for partial overlap.

Quantitatively, how much MHC-II reduction is needed to escape CD4 killing? Published data are qualitative ('reduced'); a threshold or dose-response would be the single most useful missing number for coupling the epigenetic and immune modules.
Does the KMT2D-driven exhausted-CD8 phenotype and the CREBBP-driven CD4 depletion compose additively or synergistically in the ~40-50% of tumours carrying both?
For MALT, what sets the ~20-30% of H. pylori-negative gastric cases that still respond to eradication? A cross-reactive or unidentified antigen would need explicit representation.
Genetics of follicular lymphoma and othe.caveats:
"ASSAY DEPENDENCE IS THE BIGGEST TRAP IN THE t(14;18) NUMBERS. Reported healthy-carrier prevalence ranges from 46% (Schüler 2009, 715 individuals) to >70% (Brisou/Roulland 2021 review) purely because of PCR sensitivity, the amount of DNA screened, and whether the assay covers only the major breakpoint region (MBR) or also mcr/other breakpoints. Do not treat 46% and 70% as a real biological discrepancy; treat carrier prevalence as a lower bound that rises with assay depth.

MUTATION FREQUENCIES VARY WIDELY BY COHORT AND METHOD. Krysiak 2017 (KMT2D 60%, CREBBP 52%) used a 1,716-gene panel on 113 mostly treatment-naive tumours; reviews quote KMT2D up to 80-90% and CREBBP 60-90% from series with different purity, depth, and tumour-cell enrichment (Green 2015 sequenced purified tumour cells, which raises detected frequencies). Use ranges in the model and run sensitivity analyses; a point estimate here is false precision.

ETHNIC/GEOGRAPHIC HETEROGENEITY IS REAL AND LARGE for t(14;18): 80-90% in Western series vs 47-60% in Chinese cohorts. If you calibrate to Western data and validate against Asian data (or vice versa) the model will look broken when it is not.

DERIVED ARITHMETIC: the ~5 x 10^-6 per-carrier annual conversion probability is my own calculation from carrier prevalence and SEER incidence, not a published figure. It ignores competing mortality, the age structure of both quantities, and the fact that carrier prevalence itself rises with age. Treat it as an order-of-magnitude sanity check only.

SOME MECHANISM EVIDENCE IS MOUSE/CELL-LINE, NOT HUMAN. The MHC-II-phenocopies-CREBBP-loss and CD4-depletion-rescues-engraftment results (Hashwah 2017 PNAS) are murine and MYC-driven; the HDAC3-inhibition rescue (Jiang 2017) is largely cell-line and xenograft. The human evidence for the CREBBP→MHC-II→CD4 axis is correlative (Green 2015: reduced MHC-II, reduced T-cell stimulation ex vivo, reduced CD4/CD8 infiltrate). The direction is well supported; the magnitude in human tumours is not.

SOME PUBLICATION YEARS IN THIS BRIEFING ARE 2025-2026 PREPRINT-STAGE OR RECENT PRIMARY WORK (Parker 2026 Blood Advances for SMZL; Ren 2025 Cell Rep Med; Combalia 2026 HemaSphere). These are single-cohort numbers and have not been independently replicated; the 1970s-2010s numbers (t(14;18), MYD88, t(11;18)) are far more settled.

MALT ERADICATION RESPONSE RATES ARE DRIFTING DOWNWARD over time (early series ~90% regression; recent series 50-60% all stages) as the H. pylori-negative fraction grows. Use the modern 70-80% figure for Hp-positive disease specifically, not a historical all-comers rate.

I could not source a clean published breakdown of MBR vs mcr breakpoint proportions, or a threshold value for how much MHC-II loss is required for immune escape. Both are flagged as open questions rather than asserted."

Genetics of aggressive B-cell lymphoma:.domain: Genetics of aggressive B-cell lymphoma: DLBCL cell-of-origin and genetic subtypes (Schmitz/LymphGen; Chapuy/DLBclass), MYC-rearranged high-grade B-cell lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma — with frequencies, signalling mechanisms and survival for cell-level model calibration.

key_facts.fact: Gene-expression cell-of-origin splits DLBCL into germinal-centre-B-cell-like, activated-B-cell-like and unclassified. ABC has clearly inferior R-CHOP outcome, independent of IPI and MYC/BCL2 co-expression.
key_facts.numbers: Lymph2Cx on 344 uniformly R-CHOP-treated de novo DLBCL, 335 assignable: GCB 189/335 (56%), ABC 108/335 (32%), unclassified 38/335 (11%). ABC-vs-GCB multivariable HR: time-to-progression 2.2 (1.5-3.4, p<.001), PFS 1.9 (1.3-2.7), disease-specific survival 2.0 (1.3-3.2), OS 1.7 (1.1-2.5, p=.01). In intermediate-IPI patients 5-yr TTP 53% (ABC) vs 74% (GCB).
key_facts.source: Scott DW et al., J Clin Oncol 2015; PMID 26240231, PMCID PMC4554747

key_facts.fact: Authoritative review-level cell-of-origin proportions and outcome gap, plus the double-expressor and overall cure denominators a simulation should reproduce.
key_facts.numbers: GCB ~60%, ABC ~25-30%, unclassifiable ~10-15%. 5-yr PFS after R-CHOP: ABC ~40-50% vs GCB ~75%. >60% of all DLBCL cured with R-CHOP. Double-expressor (MYC+BCL2 protein, no rearrangement) ~30% of DLBCL. Large B-cell lymphomas ~30% of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, ~150,000 new cases/year worldwide.
key_facts.source: Sehn LH & Salles G, N Engl J Med 2021;384:842-858; PMID 33657296, PMCID PMC8377611

key_facts.fact: Schmitz's original four genetic subtypes: MCD (MYD88 L265P + CD79B), BN2 (BCL6 fusion + NOTCH2), N1 (NOTCH1), EZB (EZH2 + BCL2 translocation). Survival differs sharply within each cell-of-origin class.
key_facts.numbers: 574 DLBCL; 44.8% assigned to genetically 'pure' subtypes: MCD n=71, BN2 n=98, N1 n=19, EZB n=69, other n=317. Predicted 5-yr OS after R-CHOP: MCD 26%, N1 36%, BN2 65%, EZB 68%. Within MCD, 42% carried both MYD88 L265P and CD79B; 82% carried at least one; 76% had HLA-A/B/C mutation or deletion; 30% CD58 truncation. In BN2, 73% NOTCH2 mutation/amplification.
key_facts.source: Schmitz R et al., N Engl J Med 2018;378:1396-1407; PMID 29641966, PMCID PMC6010183

key_facts.fact: LymphGen expanded the scheme to seven subtypes by adding ST2 and A53 and made assignment probabilistic per-patient, but roughly a third of cases still fall outside any subtype.
key_facts.numbers: NCI cohort n=574: classified 329/574 = 63.1% (47.6% core, 9.8% extended, 5.7% genetically composite); 36.9% remained 'Other'. Subtype prevalence in that cohort: BN2 16.1%, MCD 13.9%, EZB 13.2%, A53 6.6%, ST2 4.7%, N1 2.8%. Real-world panel cohorts give similar-to-shifted ranges: MCD 18-25%, BN2 6-15%, EZB 3-13%, ST2 7-10%, A53 0-15%, N1 0-2.5%, Other 39-42%.
key_facts.source: Wright GW et al., Cancer Cell 2020;37:551-568; PMID 32289277, PMCID PMC8459709; real-world ranges from Blood Adv 2026 Korean cohort (PMID 41544233) and Haematologica 2024 400-gene panel validation

key_facts.fact: ST2 is defined by SGK1 and TET2 mutations with additional PI3K/GPCR and JAK-STAT lesions; A53 by TP53 inactivation on the most aneuploid genomic background. EZB further splits by MYC status.
key_facts.numbers: ST2 genes: SGK1, TET2, plus P2RY8, GNA13, SOCS1, DUSP2, NFKBIA. A53 genes: TP53 mutation+deletion, TP53BP1, B2M, focal p73 and ING1 deletions; highest aneuploidy of all subtypes. EZB subdivides into DHIT+/MYC+ and DHIT-/MYC-; EZB-MYC+ survival significantly worse than EZB-MYC-.
key_facts.source: Wright GW et al., Cancer Cell 2020; PMID 32289277, PMCID PMC8459709

key_facts.fact: Chapuy's independent clustering of 304 DLBCLs gave six clusters C0-C5 with distinct drivers, cell-of-origin skew and outcomes; C0 is a driver-poor residual group.
key_facts.numbers: n=304: C0=12, C1=56, C2=64, C3=55, C4=51, C5=64. C1: BCL6 structural variants + NOTCH2/BCL10/TNFAIP3/FAS, ~96% ABC. C2: biallelic TP53 inactivation + 17p loss, CDKN2A and RB1 loss, both ABC and GCB. C3: BCL2 mutation + t(14;18), KMT2D/CREBBP/EZH2, 95% GCB (38/40). C4: histone gene, CD83/CD58/CD70, RHOA/GNA13/SGK1, CARD11/NFKBIE/NFKBIA mutations, primarily GCB. C5: near-uniform 18q gain, CD79B 48% (29/60), MYD88 50% (30/60), ~96% ABC. Favourable: C0, C1, C4. Unfavourable: C3, C5. C2 shows steady continuing progression.
key_facts.source: Chapuy B et al., Nat Med 2018;24:679-690; PMID 29713087, PMCID PMC6613387

key_facts.fact: The two schemes largely agree: applying LymphGen to Chapuy's own cohort, each genetic subtype drew predominantly from one C cluster. MCD~C5, BN2~C1, EZB~C3, A53~C2, ST2~C4; N1 has no C-cluster counterpart.
key_facts.numbers: 75% overall agreement between the two methodologies on the Harvard (Chapuy) cohort of 304. Mapping confidence: MCD/C5 and EZB/C3 highest (both ~95%+ concordant on cell-of-origin and defining lesions); N1 unmatched because it is rare (~2-3%).
key_facts.source: Wright GW et al., Cancer Cell 2020, PMID 32289277 (75% figure); the specific one-to-one mappings are consensus interpretation across Wright 2020, Chapuy 2018 and Frontiers Oncol 2022 consensus-classification review

key_facts.fact: MYD88 L265P is the single most recurrent DLBCL point mutation and drives NF-kB plus JAK-STAT3 by spontaneously nucleating an IRAK1/IRAK4 myddosome. It defines MCD/C5 with CD79B.
key_facts.numbers: MYD88 L265P in 29% of ABC DLBCL; rare or absent in GCB DLBCL and Burkitt; 9% of MALT lymphoma. Ibrutinib response in relapsed/refractory DLBCL: 37% of ABC cases overall, but 80% of tumours carrying both CD79B and MYD88 L265P.
key_facts.source: Ngo VN et al., Nature 2011;470:115-119, PMID 21179087; ibrutinib response rates from Phelan JD et al., Nature 2018;560:387-391, PMID 29925955, PMCID PMC6201842

key_facts.fact: CD79B ITAM mutations produce chronic active B-cell-receptor signalling (clustered, low-diffusion BCR) into CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 and NF-kB; CARD11 gain-of-function bypasses BTK and confers intrinsic ibrutinib resistance.
key_facts.numbers: CD79B first-ITAM tyrosine (Y196) mutated in 18% of ABC DLBCL; CD79A/CD79B ITAM mutations rare in GCB DLBCL, absent in Burkitt and MALT. Activating CARD11 coiled-coil mutations in ~10% of ABC DLBCL.
key_facts.source: Davis RE et al., Nature 2010;463:88-92; PMID 20054396, PMCID PMC2845535

key_facts.fact: TNFAIP3/A20 is the most commonly inactivated NF-kB brake in DLBCL; its loss prolongs NF-kB responses. Multiple positive and negative NF-kB regulators are mutated, mostly in ABC.
key_facts.numbers: >50% of ABC-DLBCL and a smaller fraction of GCB-DLBCL carry somatic mutations in NF-kB regulators (TNFAIP3/A20, CARD11, TRAF2, TRAF5, MAP3K7/TAK1, TNFRSF11A). A20 is most commonly affected: ~30% of patients show biallelic inactivation by mutation and/or deletion.
key_facts.source: Compagno M et al., Nature 2009;459:717-721; PMID 19412164, PMCID PMC2973325

key_facts.fact: EZH2 Tyr641 mutations are GCB-restricted change-of-function alleles that raise H3K27me3; combined with t(14;18) BCL2 they define EZB/C3, coupling a locked germinal-centre proliferative state to an apoptosis block.
key_facts.numbers: EZH2 Y641 in 21.7% of GCB DLBCL and 7.2% of follicular lymphoma; absent from ABC DLBCL. EZB is the EZH2+BCL2-translocation subtype (13.2% of the NCI cohort; C3 = 55/304 = 18% of Chapuy cohort).
key_facts.source: Morin RD et al., Nat Genet 2010;42:181-185; PMID 20081860, PMCID PMC2850970; subtype frequencies from Wright 2020 and Chapuy 2018

key_facts.fact: An unselected population-based cohort reproduces the subtype structure with real survival numbers — the best single calibration target because it is not trial-enriched.
key_facts.numbers: 928 DLBCL, 293-gene panel. Clusters: BCL2 176 (19.0%), MYD88 152 (16.4%), NOTCH2 143 (15.4%), SOCS1/SGK1 111 (12.0%), TET2/SGK1 98 (10.6%), unclassified/NEC 248 (26.7%). 5-yr OS all patients: MYD88 42.1%, NOTCH2 48.1%, NEC 53.6%, TET2/SGK1 60.1%, BCL2 62.5%, SOCS1/SGK1 64.9%. In R-CHOP-treated de novo subset (n=579) 5-yr OS: SOCS1/SGK1 80.0%, TET2/SGK1 69.8%, BCL2 69.5%, MYD88 62.8%, NOTCH2 58.8%.
key_facts.source: Lacy SE et al., Blood 2020;135:1759-1771; PMID 32187361, PMCID PMC7259825

key_facts.fact: MYC rearrangement occurs in ~10-11% of DLBCL, but the adverse effect is confined to double/triple-hit cases with an immunoglobulin partner, and is strongly front-loaded in the first two years.
key_facts.numbers: Lunenburg consortium: MYC-R in 264/2383 (11%) of biopsied patients (5117 screened). Adverse prognosis only with concurrent BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement AND an IG partner: HR 2.4 (95% CI 1.6-3.6, p<.001), time-dependent, concentrated within 24 months. HGBL-DH/TH is 4-8% of morphologic DLBCL. Trial data: DA-EPOCH-R + venetoclax was worse than DA-EPOCH-R alone (24-month OS 52% vs 72%); CODOX-M/IVAC-R vs DA-EPOCH-R in patients <=60: 2-yr EFS 64.1% vs 48.9%, 5-yr 61.5% vs 39.5%, OS not different.
key_facts.source: Rosenwald A et al., J Clin Oncol 2019;37:3359-3368, PMID 31498031; 4-8% from Sehn & Salles NEJM 2021, PMID 33657296; Abramson JS et al., Lancet Haematol 2026, PMID 42660130; Atallah-Yunes SA et al., Haematologica 2025, PMID 39385736

key_facts.fact: Mantle cell lymphoma is defined by t(11;14) CCND1-IGH; SOX11 separates aggressive conventional nodal MCL from the SOX11-negative, IGHV-hypermutated leukaemic non-nodal variant, which paradoxically carries more TP53 mutation.
key_facts.numbers: ~2-10% of all lymphomas; European incidence 0.45/100,000/yr (>1/100,000 Northern Europe); male:female ~3:1; median age ~70. Leukaemic non-nodal MCL: SOX11-negative (<10% cells), IGHV somatic hypermutation >3%, splenomegaly, indolent course. TP53 aberration: 10-15% of conventional MCL vs 25% of non-nodal MCL (one series: 5/7 = 71% nnMCL vs 8/56 = 14% cMCL). In 187 newly diagnosed MCL, ATM aberration 81/187 (43%) and TP53 aberration 75/187 (40%); ATM deletion predicted shorter PFS only in TP53-wild-type patients. Population 5-yr OS 58%, 10-yr 32% (2000-2020). TP53-mutant newly diagnosed MCL on targeted therapy: median OS 38.5 months; R/R TP53-mutant after CAR-T: 2-yr OS 44%.
key_facts.source: Jerkeman M et al., HemaSphere 2025 EHA-EU MCL guidelines, PMID 41132246, PMCID PMC12541557; Obr A et al., Mol Med 2025, PMID 41023839; Federmann B et al., Haematologica 2020, PMID 31296581; Zhang N et al., EClinicalMedicine 2025, PMID 40686686; Bea S et al., PNAS 2013, PMID 24145436 (ATM/CCND1/TP53/BIRC3/NOTCH1-2 driver landscape)

key_facts.fact: Burkitt lymphoma is a near-uniform MYC-IG translocation disease with a Ki-67 near 100%; that total growth fraction is exactly why short intensive cell-cycle-dependent chemotherapy cures it.
key_facts.numbers: t(8;14)(q24;q32) ~80% of BL; variants t(2;8)(p12;q24) ~15-20% and t(8;22)(q24;q11) ~5%. Ki-67 >95% (essential diagnostic criterion). EBV: ~95% in endemic sub-Saharan African BL, ~20% sporadic (Europe/USA), 20-40% immunodeficiency-associated. Mutations: MYC ~70%, ID3 50-60%, TP53 ~50%, CCND3 ~40%, SMARCA4 ~40%, TCF3 10-20%; Schmitz 2012 reported TCF3-or-ID3 lesions in 70% and CCND3 in 38% of sporadic BL. EBV-positive tumours carry markedly more AICDA-driven aberrant somatic hypermutation but fewer driver mutations. Outcomes: cure >90% in children/adolescents; adults 3-yr EFS 58%, 3-yr OS 66% (large series); LMB regimen 3-yr PFS 79%, OS 84%; CNS involvement 3-yr OS 55%.
key_facts.source: Anagnostopoulos I et al., Cancers 2026, PMID 41749833, PMCID PMC12938643; Schmitz R et al., Nature 2012;490:116-120, PMID 22885699; Grande BM et al., Blood 2019, PMID 30617194; Rajendra A et al., Blood Cancer J 2025, PMID 40087298; Dlouhy I et al., Cancers 2025, PMID 40941011

mechanisms: Chronic active BCR signalling (ABC/MCD): CD79B ITAM Y196 mutation removes LYN-mediated negative feedback and blocks receptor internalisation, so BCR forms clustered, low-diffusion microdomains that sustain SYK -> BTK -> PKCbeta -> assembly of the CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 (CBM) signalosome -> IKK -> constitutive NF-kB. Antigen-independent but antigen-mimicking; distinct from tonic PI3K-only signalling.

MYD88 L265P: single amino acid change in the TIR domain lets MYD88 spontaneously oligomerise and nucleate a myddosome containing IRAK1 and IRAK4 without ligand. Output is dual: IRAK4 kinase activity -> IRAK1 phosphorylation -> NF-kB, plus JAK kinase -> STAT3 with autocrine IL-6/IL-10 secretion. This is a self-reinforcing loop, so a model needs positive feedback, not a constant.

My-T-BCR supercomplex: in MCD, MYD88 L265P, TLR9 and the BCR co-assemble on endolysosomes together with mTORC1. This physically couples the two NF-kB inputs and licenses mTOR signalling from the same platform. It explains why CD79B+MYD88 double-mutant tumours respond to ibrutinib at 80% while ABC overall responds at 37%, and why BTK plus mTOR inhibition is synergistic. Model implication: MYD88 and CD79B are not independent additive NF-kB inputs, they are cooperative.

CARD11 gain-of-function (coiled-coil domain, ~10% ABC) activates the CBM complex downstream of BTK, so it produces NF-kB output that is epistatic to and resistant to BTK inhibition. In a model this is a node that bypasses the drug target.

TNFAIP3/A20 loss: A20 is a ubiquitin-editing enzyme that terminates NF-kB by deubiquitinating RIP1/NEMO. Biallelic inactivation (~30%) removes the shut-off arm, converting a transient pulse into a prolonged response. This is a gene-dose effect (mutation and/or deletion of both alleles), so it is naturally modelled as a 2-allele brake rather than a binary switch.

EZH2 Y641 is change-of-function, not loss-of-function: mutant EZH2 has poor activity on unmethylated H3K27 but high processivity converting me2 to me3, so it must act in trans with a wild-type allele. Net effect is elevated H3K27me3 repressing CDKN1A, PRDM1/BLIMP1 and IRF4, locking cells in a proliferative germinal-centre/dark-zone program and blocking plasma-cell exit. Combined with t(14;18) BCL2 (apoptosis block) this is the EZB/C3 two-hit logic: proliferate and do not die.

NOTCH pathway: BN2/C1 carries NOTCH2 activating mutations or SPEN (NOTCH antagonist) inactivation in ~50%, with BCL6 translocation in ~72% of those, driving a marginal-zone-like differentiation program. N1 carries NOTCH1 PEST-domain truncations that stabilise the intracellular domain. NOTCH1 mutation is independently adverse; NOTCH2 mutation is not.

A53/C2: biallelic TP53 inactivation plus 17p loss, with CDKN2A and RB1 deletion, produces the most aneuploid genomes and an immune-cold, chromosomally unstable state. Mechanistically this is a mutator/selection phenotype rather than a signalling phenotype — model it as an elevated per-division chromosomal missegregation rate plus loss of the damage checkpoint.

MYC-IG translocation places MYC under immunoglobulin enhancer control, giving constitutive supraphysiological MYC. MYC alone raises proliferation but also primes apoptosis (via ARF-p53 and BIM), which is why single-hit MYC-R is not strongly adverse. Adding a BCL2 rearrangement removes the apoptotic counterweight: that is the mechanistic basis of double-hit, and why the adverse effect requires an IG partner (highest expression).

Mantle cell lymphoma: t(11;14) puts CCND1 under IGH enhancer control -> cyclin D1 overexpression -> CDK4/6-mediated RB1 phosphorylation -> G1/S override. This alone is insufficient (it exists in healthy people's B cells); secondary hits are needed. SOX11 is a transcription factor that blocks terminal B-cell differentiation (represses PRDM1/BLIMP1) and promotes PAX5 and angiogenesis, defining aggressive nodal MCL. SOX11-negative, IGHV-mutated leukaemic non-nodal MCL is indolent at diagnosis but acquires TP53 lesions at higher frequency, giving a two-phase natural history.

Burkitt lymphoma: TCF3 (E2A) activating mutations or loss of its inhibitor ID3 (together ~70% of sporadic BL) increase TCF3 transcriptional output, which augments tonic BCR signalling and activates PI3K-AKT for survival; CCND3 stabilising mutations drive G1/S. So BL uses tonic BCR-PI3K, not chronic active BCR-NF-kB — the opposite wiring from ABC-DLBCL, which is why BTK inhibitors are not the BL strategy.

EBV in endemic Burkitt: EBV positivity is associated with a genome-wide increase in aberrant somatic hypermutation, implicating AICDA activity, yet EBV-positive tumours carry significantly FEWER driver mutations, especially in apoptosis genes — the virus appears to substitute for some host genetic lesions.
modellable: Cell-of-origin sampling priors for a virtual DLBCL cohort: GCB 0.56, ABC 0.32, unclassified 0.11 (Lymph2Cx, n=335). Alternative review-level prior: GCB 0.60, ABC 0.275, unclassified 0.125.

Genetic subtype priors (LymphGen, NCI n=574): BN2 0.161, MCD 0.139, EZB 0.132, A53 0.066, ST2 0.047, N1 0.028, composite 0.057, Other 0.369. Note ~37% unassigned — a model must include an explicit 'no defined subtype' compartment, not force every agent into a class.

Alternative population-based subtype priors with matched survival (Lacy HMRN, n=928): BCL2 0.190, MYD88 0.164, NOTCH2 0.154, SOCS1/SGK1 0.120, TET2/SGK1 0.106, NEC 0.267. Use these when calibrating to unselected incidence rather than trial cohorts.

Outcome calibration targets, 5-yr OS after R-CHOP by genetic subtype: MCD 0.26, N1 0.36, BN2 0.65, EZB 0.68 (Schmitz). Population equivalents (Lacy, R-CHOP de novo): MYD88 0.628, NOTCH2 0.588, TET2/SGK1 0.698, BCL2 0.695, SOCS1/SGK1 0.800. Overall DLBCL cure fraction >0.60.

Mutation co-occurrence rules for generating in silico genotypes (conditional, not independent): P(MYD88 L265P | ABC) = 0.29; P(CD79B ITAM | ABC) = 0.18; within MCD, P(both MYD88 and CD79B) = 0.42 and P(at least one) = 0.82; P(CARD11 GOF | ABC) = 0.10; P(A20 biallelic loss | DLBCL) = 0.30; P(any NF-kB regulator mutation | ABC) > 0.50; P(EZH2 Y641 | GCB) = 0.217; P(NOTCH2 alteration | BN2) = 0.73.

NF-kB as a multi-input node with one brake: three alternative activating inputs (MYD88-myddosome, CD79B-BCR-CBM, CARD11-GOF) converging on IKK, and a dose-dependent A20 shut-off arm with 2 allele copies. Cooperativity term required between MYD88 and CD79B (My-T-BCR supercomplex): their joint effect is super-additive, evidenced by 80% vs 37% ibrutinib response.

Drug-target epistasis rule for a BTK-inhibitor arm: agents with CARD11 GOF are resistant regardless of upstream genotype; agents with MYD88+CD79B are maximally sensitive (response 0.80); ABC overall 0.37. mTOR inhibition acts on the same supercomplex, so model BTK+mTOR as synergistic, not additive.

Proliferation parameters: Burkitt growth fraction ~1.0 (Ki-67 > 0.95), doubling time on the order of 24-48 h — set almost every agent cycling, which makes a cell-cycle-phase-specific cytotoxic kill nearly saturating and reproduces >0.90 cure in children. DLBCL Ki-67 is heterogeneous (typically 0.4-0.9) and the dark-zone-signature GCB subset has 5-yr OS 0.55 vs 0.82 for DZ-negative GCB — a usable proliferation-to-outcome coupling.

MYC/BCL2 double-hit module: prevalence of MYC-R = 0.11 of DLBCL; HGBL-DH/TH = 0.04-0.08 of morphologic DLBCL; double-expressor (protein only) = 0.30. Implement MYC as raising both division rate and apoptotic priming, and BCL2 rearrangement as lowering the apoptotic threshold; adverse phenotype should emerge only when both are present with an IG partner (target HR 2.4), and should decay after 24 months.

Time-dependent hazard, not proportional hazard: the double-hit adverse effect is concentrated in the first 24 months and attenuates thereafter. Any survival module fitted to these data needs a non-constant hazard or it will misfit the tail.

Mantle cell lymphoma module: t(11;14) in essentially all cases as the founder event (cyclin D1 -> CDK4/6 -> RB1); SOX11 as a binary differentiation-block switch splitting agents into conventional nodal (SOX11+, IGHV unmutated, aggressive) versus leukaemic non-nodal (SOX11-, IGHV SHM >3%, indolent, spleen/blood-tropic). Secondary-hit rates: TP53 aberration 0.10-0.15 in cMCL vs 0.25 in nnMCL (up to 0.40 in unselected newly diagnosed cohorts); ATM aberration 0.43. Calibrate population survival to 5-yr OS 0.58, 10-yr 0.32; TP53-mutant median OS 38.5 months.
ATM/TP53 interaction rule for MCL: ATM deletion shortens PFS only in TP53-wild-type agents — an explicit conditional-epistasis rule, not an additive risk score.

Burkitt module: MYC-IG translocation in ~1.0 of agents (t(8;14) 0.80, t(2;8) 0.15-0.20, t(8;22) 0.05); secondary hit rates ID3 0.50-0.60, TCF3 0.10-0.20, TP53 0.50, CCND3 0.40, SMARCA4 0.40. EBV branch: endemic P(EBV+) = 0.95, sporadic 0.20, immunodeficiency 0.20-0.40; EBV+ agents get a higher genome-wide AICDA-driven mutation rate but FEWER apoptosis-pathway drivers — model as increased background mutation rate with reduced driver requirement.

Age/epidemiology inputs: endemic BL peak 6-8 yrs; sporadic BL median 10 yrs with secondary peaks at 40 and 75; immunodeficiency-associated median 40-45 yrs; male:female 2-4:1. MCL median age ~70, male:female ~3:1, incidence 0.45/100,000/yr. Large B-cell lymphoma ~30% of NHL, ~150,000 cases/yr worldwide.

Cross-scheme mapping for validating a classifier built inside the simulation: expect ~75% agreement between LymphGen-style and Chapuy-style clustering on the same genomes, with MCD<->C5, BN2<->C1, EZB<->C3, A53<->C2, ST2<->C4 and N1 unmatched. A simulated classifier that agrees at ~100% is overfitted; ~75% is the empirical ceiling.

Burkitt therapy-response calibration: children/adolescents cure >0.90; adults 3-yr EFS 0.58, 3-yr OS 0.66; LMB-regimen 3-yr PFS 0.79 / OS 0.84; CNS involvement drops 3-yr OS to 0.55. The paediatric/adult gap is toxicity-limited dose intensity, so model dose tolerance as an age-dependent constraint on delivered intensity, not as differing tumour biology.
open_questions: Chapuy et al. reported cluster outcomes as Kaplan-Meier curves and hazard ratios, not as explicit 5-year OS percentages; I could not source per-cluster 5-yr OS numbers for C0-C5 from the primary paper. If you need them for calibration, the Lacy HMRN 5-yr OS figures are the better-sourced substitute.

Wright et al. 2020 likewise gives no explicit 5-yr PFS/OS percentages per LymphGen subtype in text; the Schmitz 2018 'predicted 5-yr OS' figures (26/36/65/68%) are model-predicted, not raw observed, and come from the earlier 4-subtype scheme. ST2 and A53 have no equivalently clean published 5-yr OS number that I could source.

Reported LymphGen subtype frequencies vary substantially between cohorts (MCD 13.9% in the NCI cohort vs 25.2% in a Korean cohort vs 18.0% in a real-world panel cohort; A53 6.6% vs 14.6% vs 0%). Whether this is genuine population genetics, panel/assay coverage, or classifier thresholding is unresolved — do not treat any single set of priors as universal.

The exact split between t(2;8) and t(8;22) in Burkitt is inconsistent across sources; the review I used gives t(2;8) 15-20% and t(8;22) 5%, but other literature reverses the ordering. Treat the two variant translocations as jointly ~20% and do not rely on the split.

The frequency of the leukaemic non-nodal MCL variant as a proportion of all MCL was not stated in the guideline or the studies I could reach (one series had 8/66 = 12%, which is a referral-biased single cohort). Also unsourced here: the exact proportion of MCL that is SOX11-positive, and the proportion that is cyclin D1-negative with CCND2/CCND3 rearrangement.

DLBclass (the 2024+ refinement of the Chapuy clustering) and the newer '2-S' classifier are now in use alongside LymphGen and reportedly show high concordance, but I did not source their cluster definitions, frequencies or outcomes. If the simulation is meant to be current as of 2026, that is the main gap.

Whether the genetic subtypes represent discrete states or positions on continuous axes is unsettled; ~37% 'Other' under LymphGen and 26.7% NEC under the HMRN clustering both argue against a clean discrete-state model. A mixture or continuous-latent-space representation may fit the data better than hard classes.
Genetics of aggressive B-cell lymphoma:.caveats: Survival numbers come from different eras, populations and treatment regimens and are not interchangeable. Schmitz's 26/36/65/68% are model-PREDICTED 5-year OS from a 2018 four-subtype scheme; Lacy's are observed 5-year OS in an unselected UK population; Scott's are R-CHOP trial-quality but cell-of-origin only. Cohort composition drives large apparent differences (Lacy's all-patient MYD88 5-yr OS is 42.1% but 62.8% in the R-CHOP-treated de novo subset — the same biology, a different denominator). Do not pool them. Frequencies are similarly denominator-sensitive: 'percent of DLBCL' versus 'percent of ABC-DLBCL' versus 'percent within a subtype' differ by several fold (e.g. MYD88 L265P is 29% of ABC but ~8-10% of all DLBCL). Several numbers here are single-cohort or single-review values with no replication cited (nnMCL TP53 71%, the t(2;8)/t(8;22) split, the Korean LymphGen frequencies) — flagged in open_questions. The 75% cross-scheme agreement figure comes from applying LymphGen to Chapuy's cohort, so it is not a fully independent comparison. Full texts of Nature, Lancet, Wiley and ASH-hosted journals were not directly reachable; abstract-level and PMC-hosted extraction was used, so a small number of within-paper figures (per-cluster Kaplan-Meier percentages in particular) could not be verified against the source tables. Nothing here is clinical guidance; the treatment numbers are included only as calibration targets.

Taxonomy and epidemiology of non-Hodgkin.domain: Taxonomy and epidemiology of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL): WHO-HAEM5 (2022) vs ICC (2022) classification, subtype frequency, US/global incidence and mortality, subtype-specific survival and cure fraction, and quantified risk factors — assembled for calibration of a cell-level / agent-based lymphoma simulation.

key_facts.fact: Two competing 2022 classifications coexist. WHO-HAEM5 is hierarchical (families/classes) and abolishes 'provisional entity'; ICC retains provisional entities. Both descend from REAL/WHO4R and agree on most diagnostic criteria.
key_facts.source: Alaggio 2022 Leukemia (PMID 35732829, PMC9214472); Campo 2022 Blood (PMID 35653592, PMC9479027)

key_facts.fact: Concrete WHO5/ICC divergences that change entity counts: B-PLL, NLPHL naming, double-hit definitions, effusion lymphoma, FL grading, follicle-centre and testicular FL, immune-privileged-site LBCL grouping.
key_facts.numbers: 8 named divergences: (1) WHO5 deletes B-PLL into 'splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli'; ICC keeps B-PLL. (2) ICC renames NLPHL to nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma; WHO5 keeps it in Hodgkin. (3) WHO5 = 'DLBCL/HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements' only; ICC adds provisional 'HGBL with MYC and BCL6'. (4) WHO5 new 'fluid overload-associated LBCL'; ICC provisional 'HHV8-/EBV-negative primary effusion-based lymphoma'. (5) FL grading optional in WHO5, retained (1/2/3A/3B) in ICC. (6) ICC provisional 'BCL2-R-negative CD23+ follicle centre lymphoma'; WHO5 calls it FL with predominantly diffuse pattern. (7) ICC distinct 'testicular FL'; not an entity in WHO5. (8) WHO5 groups primary LBCL of immune-privileged sites (CNS/testis/vitreoretina); ICC lists separately.
key_facts.source: Falini & Martelli 2023, Blood Cancer J (PMID 36460764, PMC9883170); confirmed in Lancet B-NHL review 2024 (PMID 38614113, PMC12261310)
