key_facts.fact: CURABILITY — Burkitt lymphoma is curable in adults with non-dose-intensive DA-EPOCH-R, including HIV-positive patients; risk-adapted low-risk arm had no failures.
key_facts.numbers: n=113 adults, 22 centres, median age 49 yr, 25% HIV+, 87% high-risk. Median follow-up 58.7 months: EFS 84.5%, OS 87.0%. Low-risk EFS 100%; high-risk EFS 82.1%.
key_facts.source: Roschewski M et al. 2020, J Clin Oncol 38:2519-2529 (PMID 32453640, PMC7392744)

key_facts.fact: CURABILITY — follicular lymphoma: the 'incurable' label is now contestable. 15-year SWOG S0016 cure modelling shows a real cured fraction and a decaying relapse hazard, but ~20% fail early with poor survival.
key_facts.numbers: n=531 advanced-stage FL, median follow-up 15.5 yr. 15-yr OS 70%; 15-yr PFS 40% (CHOP-RIT 47% vs R-CHOP 34%, P=.004). Mixture cure model estimate: cure rate 42%. Relapse rate falls from 6.8%/yr (yr 0-5) to 0.6%/yr (yr 15-20). POD24 (progression within 24 mo of R-CHOP) occurs in 19% and gives 5-yr OS 50% vs 90% (HR 6.44). SEER FL 5-yr relative survival 89%.
key_facts.source: SWOG S0016 15-yr follow-up 2026 (PMID 41746629, PMC12947078); Casulo C et al. 2015 J Clin Oncol (PMID 26124482, PMC4879714); ACS/SEER 2015-2021

key_facts.fact: CURABILITY — mantle cell lymphoma remains 'generally incurable' by the authors' own wording, but survival has transformed; there is control, not a demonstrated cure fraction.
key_facts.numbers: Pooled 6 randomised phase III trials, n=2,541, enrolled 1996-2020. Age <=65 yr: median OS 4.9 yr (5-yr OS 49%) in 1996-2000 -> 13.8 yr (73%) in 2004-2014 -> not reached (84%) in 2016-2020. Age >65 / transplant-ineligible: median OS 3.8 -> 4.8 yr (5-yr OS 40-49%). Historic UK registry 5-yr relative survival 31.4% (2004-2014).
key_facts.source: Pooled analysis of six randomized phase III MCL trials, 2026 (PMID 41163573, PMC13136794); HMRN (PMC4453686)

key_facts.fact: CURABILITY — extranodal marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma is the one NHL curable by removing the antigen rather than killing cells: H. pylori eradication alone induces durable remission, and the failures are genetically defined.
key_facts.numbers: Systematic review, 32 studies, n=1,408 early-stage gastric MALT: remission 77.5% (95% CI 75.3-79.7). Stage I 78.4% vs stage II1 55.6% (P=.0003); submucosa-confined 82.2% vs deeper 54.5%; distal 91.8% vs proximal stomach 75.7%; API2-MALT1 [t(11;18)] negative 78% vs positive 22.2% (P=.0001). Asian 84.1% vs Western 73.8%. UK extranodal MZL 5-yr relative survival 87.9%.
key_facts.source: Zullo A et al. 2010, Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol (PMID 19631287); HMRN (PMC4453686)

key_facts.fact: NOT CURABLE — CLL/SLL and lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenstrom are controlled indefinitely, not cured, with standard therapy; long median survivals but no plateau at background mortality.
key_facts.numbers: CLL, Swedish population-based 2010-2021, n=7,234, median age 71: median OS 9.7 yr (95% CI 9.3-10.2). WM: median OS 126.7 months (Spanish multicentre, n=577 IgM gammopathies) and 202.8 months (Torino cohort, n=166). Acalabrutinib in WM at 63.7-mo follow-up: 66-mo PFS 83.6% treatment-naive, 52.0% relapsed/refractory — responses, not plateaus.
key_facts.source: Swedish MM/CLL infection cohort 2026 (PMID 42540882); SAL-TO IgM gammopathy study 2026 (PMID 41855507); ACE-WM-001 5-yr update (PMID 41985004)

key_facts.fact: CURABILITY — mature T/NK entities: only ALK-positive ALCL is reliably curable; PTCL-NOS, AITL, ENKTL and especially ATLL are not. Most deaths are early, and salvage is nearly futile.
key_facts.numbers: International T-Cell Lymphoma Project (n=1,153 reviewed): subtype mix PTCL-NOS 25.9%, AITL 18.5%, NK/T 10.4%, ATLL 9.6%. 5-yr OS: ALK+ ALCL 70%, ALK- ALCL 49%, PTCL-NOS/AITL/NKTCL 32%, ATLL 14%. Prospective 10-yr follow-up (n=735): ORR 68%, 5-yr OS 49%, 10-yr OS 40%; conditional on being alive at 5 yr, 84% reach 10 yr, but 67% of deaths in yr 5-10 are still lymphoma. After first-line failure (n=937): 47% primary refractory, 21% relapsed, median OS 5.8 months.
key_facts.source: Vose J et al. 2008, J Clin Oncol 26:4124-4130 (PMID 18626005); ITCLP 10-yr follow-up (PMC11931637); Bellei M et al. 2018 Haematologica (PMID 29599200, PMC6029527)

key_facts.fact: Quantified risk factors, all expressed as relative risks usable as hazard multipliers: immunosuppression dominates, followed by specific chronic-antigen/viral exposures.
key_facts.numbers: HIV (US HIV/AIDS Cancer Match, n=448,258, 1996-2012): NHL SIR 11.5 (11.1-11.9). Solid-organ transplant (US SRTR linkage, n=175,732): NHL SIR 7.54 (7.17-7.93); by organ lung 7.79, liver 7.77, heart 7.79, kidney 6.05; risk peaks in yr 1, dips, re-plateaus at 4-5 yr. Autoimmune (InterLymph, n=29,423): Sjogren OR 6.5 for NHL and OR 996 (216-4596) for parotid MZL; SLE OR 2.7. HCV (InterLymph, 4,784 cases/6,269 controls): OR 1.78 (1.40-2.25). HTLV-1: lifetime ATL risk 6-7% men, 2-3% women (Japan), latency 20-30 yr, ~60 ATL cases/100,000 carriers/yr.
key_facts.source: Hernandez-Ramirez 2017 Lancet HIV (PMID 28803888, PMC5669995); Engels 2011 JAMA (PMID 22045767, PMC3310893); Ekstrom Smedby 2008 Blood (PMID 18263783); de Sanjose 2008 Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol (PMID 18387498); Iwanaga 2012 Front Microbiol (PMID 22973265, PMC3437524)

mechanisms: DEFENSIBLE CURABILITY TABLE (entity | curable today? | key number | source). Burkitt lymphoma | YES | adult DA-EPOCH-R EFS 84.5%/OS 87.0% at 58.7 mo; low-risk EFS 100% | Roschewski 2020 JCO. DLBCL | YES | 5-yr RS 65%; EFS24 achievers have SMR 1.18 (ns) vs general population | Maurer 2014 JCO. ALK+ anaplastic large cell lymphoma | YES | 5-yr OS 70% | Vose 2008 JCO. Early-stage gastric MALT/EMZL | YES, by antigen withdrawal | 77.5% remission on H. pylori eradication alone; 22.2% if t(11;18)+ | Zullo 2010. Localised (stage I-II) FL | PROBABLY | involved-site RT 24-30 Gy potentially curative; SEER localized 5-yr RS 97% | Lancet 2024 primer; SEER. Advanced FL | PARTIALLY — newly arguable | cure fraction 42% by mixture cure model at 15 yr; relapse hazard 6.8%/yr -> 0.6%/yr | SWOG S0016 2026. Mantle cell lymphoma | NO (control only) | 'generally incurable'; <=65 yr 5-yr OS 84% in 2016-2020 but no demonstrated plateau at background mortality | pooled 6 RCTs 2026. CLL/SLL | NO | median OS 9.7 yr, population-based | Swedish registry 2026. Lymphoplasmacytic/Waldenstrom | NO | median OS 126.7-202.8 months | SAL-TO 2026. PTCL-NOS / AITL / ENKTL | NO for most | 5-yr OS 32%, 10-yr OS 40% overall; 47% primary refractory | ITCLP. ATLL (HTLV-1) | NO | 5-yr OS 14% | Vose 2008.

Cell-of-origin and mutational engine: most B-NHL arise from germinal-centre or post-GC B cells, where AID-driven somatic hypermutation and class-switch recombination create physiological double-strand breaks. Translocation partners are the immunoglobulin loci — t(14;18) BCL2-IGH in FL, t(8;14) MYC-IGH in Burkitt, t(11;14) CCND1-IGH in MCL. This makes lymphomagenesis a byproduct of a normal, high-throughput, error-prone cellular program, not a stochastic background mutation process.

Antigen-dependence as a therapeutic axis unique to lymphoma: MALT lymphoma clones initially depend on chronic antigenic stimulation (H. pylori in stomach, HCV in splenic MZL, Sjogren autoantigen in parotid MZL). Removing the antigen removes the growth signal and the tumour regresses. Acquisition of t(11;18)/API2-MALT1 confers constitutive NF-kB activation and antigen independence — a discrete, modellable switch that drops remission from 78% to 22%.

Immunosurveillance failure as the second axis: EBV-transformed B cells are normally held in check by EBV-specific cytotoxic T cells. HIV or pharmacological immunosuppression removes that control, producing EBV+ DLBCL and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. This gives a relative-risk multiplier of ~7.5-11.5x and, importantly, is partly reversible — reducing immunosuppression can regress PTLD, meaning the effector-cell compartment must be explicit in any cell-level model.

Proliferative-fraction paradox governing curability: entities with near-total cycling fractions (Burkitt, Ki-67 up to 100%) are the most chemocurable; indolent entities with low cycling fractions (FL, CLL, MZL, WM) harbour a quiescent reservoir that cytotoxic therapy cannot reach, which is the mechanistic reason their survival curves lack a plateau. MCL sits between, with Ki-67 >30% marking the high-risk, aggressive-behaviour subset (MIPI-c).

Histologic transformation couples the indolent and aggressive compartments: FL transforms to DLBCL and CLL undergoes Richter transformation. WHO-HAEM5 formalises this by adding a section on 'transformations of indolent B-cell lymphomas' that ICC does not have — meaning a two-state (indolent -> aggressive) model is now taxonomically sanctioned.
modellable: Virtual-cohort demographics: draw age from the SEER NHL age distribution (<20 1.6%, 20-34 3.6%, 35-44 4.8%, 45-54 9.5%, 55-64 20.0%, 65-74 28.7%, 75-84 23.0%, >84 8.8%), median 68 yr; sex ratio M:F 1.31 (GLOBOCAN 2024) or age-standardised 1.39 (HMRN). Baseline hazard 18.7 new NHL/100,000/yr (US age-adjusted).

Subtype mixture weights for the cohort. Two defensible parameterisations, which must be labelled: (a) B-NHL denominator (Lancet 2024): DLBCL 0.30-0.40, FL 0.25, MZL 0.05-0.15, MCL 0.05-0.07; (b) unselected registry, NHL denominator excluding CLL/LPL (HMRN): DLBCL 0.478, MZL 0.198, FL 0.186, T/NK 0.062, MCL 0.050, Burkitt 0.021. Sub-partition MZL as EMZL 0.67 / SMZL 0.20 / NMZL <0.10; MCL as nodal SOX11+ 0.80-0.90 / leukemic non-nodal 0.10-0.20; PTCL as PTCL-NOS 0.259 / AITL 0.185 / NK-T 0.104 / ATLL 0.096.

Mixture cure model as the survival kernel: S(t) = p + (1-p)*S_u(t), where p is the cured fraction and S_u is uncured-patient survival. Fitted p values to use directly: advanced FL p = 0.42 (log-normal mixture, S0016); all-NHL by AJCC stage p = 0.91 / 0.85 / 0.81 / 0.74 for I/II/III/IV (SEER 2006-2015, ages 40-79). Assume cured individuals die at background population rate.

FL relapse-hazard schedule (directly implementable as a time-varying rate): 6.8%/yr in years 0-5, declining to 0.6%/yr in years 15-20. 15-yr PFS 0.40, 15-yr OS 0.70. Add a POD24 subpopulation of 19% with a death hazard ratio of 6.44 and 5-yr OS 0.50 (vs 0.90 for the rest). FL spontaneous regression occurs in 10-20% untreated.

DLBCL landmark rule: after 24 months event-free, set the excess lymphoma hazard to ~0 (SMR 1.18, P=0.25). Use this rather than a continuous hazard for DLBCL survivorship. Baseline 5-yr relative survival 0.65; by SEER stage localized 0.74 / regional 0.74 / distant 0.58. About 30% of new DLBCL are dual MYC/BCL2 protein 'double-expressor' with intermediate outcome.

MALT antigen-withdrawal rule: on antigen removal, set net clone growth rate to <=0 with probability 0.775 overall; condition it on modelled covariates — stage I 0.784 vs stage II1 0.556, submucosal 0.822 vs deeper 0.545, distal 0.918 vs proximal 0.757, t(11;18)-negative 0.78 vs t(11;18)-positive 0.222. H. pylori itself is eradicable in 91% first-line, 98.3% cumulative ITT.

Proliferative fraction (Ki-67) as a per-cell cycling probability: Burkitt up to 1.00; MCL threshold at 0.30 separating standard from high-risk (MIPI-c); FL/CLL/MZL low. Couple cycling fraction to cytotoxic kill probability to reproduce the observed curable/incurable split.

Immunosuppression as a time-varying hazard multiplier on lymphomagenesis: HIV x11.5; solid-organ transplant x7.54 overall (lung 7.79, liver 7.77, heart 7.79, kidney 6.05), with a documented shape — peak in year 1 post-transplant, fall, then re-plateau from years 4-5. Autoimmune: Sjogren x6.5 (x996 for parotid-site MZL), SLE x2.7. HCV x1.78.

HTLV-1 -> ATLL as an explicit two-stage latency process: infection in childhood, 20-30 yr latency, then conversion at ~60-138 per 100,000 carriers/yr, giving lifetime risk 6-7% (men) and 2-3% (women). Geography changes the mixture drastically: ATLL is 51-59% of all NHL in endemic Kyushu vs 7.5% of lymphomas nationwide in Japan — a clean test case for a geography-parameterised cohort.

PTCL treatment-failure module: first-line ORR 0.68; 47% primary refractory, 21% later relapse; median OS after failure 5.8 months (3-yr OS 21% refractory, 28% relapsed). Overall 5-yr OS 0.49, 10-yr 0.40; conditional survival 5->10 yr is 0.84, so the hazard is heavily front-loaded and should be modelled as a decaying, not constant, rate.

Global scaling for burden calculations: 562,793 incident NHL and 234,903 NHL deaths worldwide in 2024; US share 79,320 incident and 19,970 deaths — i.e. the US carries ~14% of global incidence but ~8.5% of global deaths, a ~1.7x mortality-to-incidence gap that can be used to calibrate a treatment-access parameter.
open_questions: Is the 42% FL 'cure' from S0016 true clonal eradication, or lifelong subclinical disease with a hazard that has fallen below detection? No MRD or ctDNA data accompany the 15-year cure-model estimate, so a simulation cannot yet distinguish 'zero clonogenic cells' from 'a dormant reservoir with rate ~0.6%/yr'.

The SEER stage-IV all-NHL cure fraction of 74% is implausibly high as biological cure and almost certainly reflects cause-of-death misattribution plus indolent-histology mixing. No published stage-and-subtype-stratified cure fractions exist for NHL. This is the single largest quantitative gap for the curability table.

No published crosswalk quantifies how many mature lymphoma cases get reclassified between WHO-HAEM5 and ICC. Such a study exists for B-ALL (unclassifiable fell from 41.9% under WHO-HAEM4R to 15.9% WHO-HAEM5 and 11.9% ICC, PMID 41886641) but not for mature B/T entities — so cohort composition under the two 2022 systems cannot be reconciled numerically.

Do CAR-T and bispecific antibodies create a genuine cure fraction in relapsed/refractory DLBCL and FL, or only extend remission? Mixture-cure modelling of ZUMA-7 is contested and the health-technology-assessment literature explicitly flags this as unresolved (PMID 40930226, PMID 40775201).

What mechanism converts an antigen-dependent MALT clone to antigen-independent? t(11;18)/API2-MALT1 explains part of it (remission drops to 22.2%) but not the ~22% of t(11;18)-negative non-responders.

Are the near-normal survival curves now seen in MCL (5-yr OS 84% in 2016-2020) the start of a plateau or merely a shifted curve? Follow-up is too short to fit a cure model, and the trial authors still describe MCL as generally incurable.
Taxonomy and epidemiology of non-Hodgkin.caveats:
DENOMINATOR TRAP — the single biggest source of error in NHL frequency tables. SEER's "NHL" is ICD-10 C82-C86 + C96 and EXCLUDES CLL (C91.1) and multiple myeloma; HMRN's lymphoma report likewise counts CLL/SLL and lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with the leukaemias/plasma cell neoplasms, so my derived HMRN percentages (DLBCL 47.8%, etc.) are shares of lymphoma-excluding-CLL/LPL, not of all mature lymphoid neoplasms. Series that fold CLL/SLL back in typically drop DLBCL to ~30% and insert CLL/SLL at ~15-20%. Always state the denominator before quoting a subtype fraction.

"CURE" HAS THREE DISTINCT MEANINGS HERE, and they must not be mixed: (1) statistical/registry cure fraction = the modelled proportion whose mortality returns to the age/sex-matched background rate; it is inferred from mixture cure models on cause-specific or relative survival and, for indolent lymphoma, systematically overstates biological cure because patients living with disease who die of other causes are read as cured; (2) landmark cure, e.g. DLBCL EFS24, which is an empirical observation (SMR 1.18, ns) rather than a model fit and is the most defensible single cure claim in NHL; (3) long remission / control, e.g. CLL on BTK inhibitors or MCL after transplant, where median survival is long but no plateau at background mortality has been demonstrated. The SWOG S0016 FL figure of 42% is type (1) and is a genuinely new claim (2026) that overturns decades of teaching — treat it as strong but singular evidence, from one trial, in a fitter-than-average trial population, with CHOP-RIT (a regimen no longer used) outperforming R-CHOP.

VINTAGE. The HMRN survival figures are 2004-2014 and predate BTK inhibitors, venetoclax, CAR-T, bispecifics and brentuximab-CHP. HMRN MCL 5-yr relative survival of 31.4% and PTCL-NOS 19.7% are historically accurate but no longer describe current practice; use the 2026 pooled MCL trial analysis and the ITCLP prospective cohort instead. Conversely, the Vose 2008 PTCL subtype distribution is from 22 referral centres, not a population, and geography dominates it (ATLL 9.6% overall but 51-59% of NHL in endemic Kyushu).

RELATIVE SURVIVAL is not cause-specific survival and not overall survival; comparing a relative-survival figure (SEER, HMRN) with an overall-survival figure (trials) across subtypes will produce spurious differences, especially in the elderly where NHL median age is 68.

GLOBOCAN figures are modelled estimates, not registry counts, in most low- and middle-income countries; the global 562,793/234,903 split should be treated as an order-of-magnitude anchor rather than a measurement.

The lifetime-ATLL-risk figures (6-7% men, 2-3% women) derive from Japanese studies of the 1980s-2000s and are extrapolated cumulative risks, not prospective cohort measurements; Caribbean and South American estimates differ (e.g. ~4% in both sexes in Jamaican modelling) and the male excess is not universal.

I could not source a subtype-specific cure fraction (as opposed to relative survival) for DLBCL, MCL, MZL, CLL or PTCL from population data; those rows in the curability table rest on survival-curve shape plus expert wording in the primary papers, not on a fitted cure parameter. That is the main place where the table is argued rather than measured.

Normal germinal centre (GC) biology, GC.domain: Normal germinal centre (GC) biology, GC quantitative dynamics, and the mapping of non-Hodgkin lymphoma entities onto their normal counterpart cells — briefing for building a cell-level / agent-based lymphoma simulation.

key_facts.fact: GC dark zone and light zone occupy roughly equal volumes, and the ratios of T cells, macrophages, proliferating and apoptotic cells stay constant across the established response despite enormous variation in GC size.
key_facts.numbers: 3,457 GC sections analysed; DZ ≈ LZ in size; minimum cell loss rate estimated at 3% per hour
key_facts.source: Wittenbrink N et al. 2011, J Immunol 187:6185 (PMID 22102720)

key_facts.fact: GC B cells are among the fastest-cycling mammalian cells; the full cell cycle in the GC takes 6-8 hours, so multiple rounds of division are possible even during a short light-zone dwell.
key_facts.numbers: cell cycle 6-8 h; ~3-7% of GC B cells are cMyc+ light-zone (recently selected) cells at any time
key_facts.source: Nakagawa R et al. 2021, PNAS 118:e2016425118 (PMC7812803)

key_facts.fact: Number of divisions per dark-zone visit is not fixed: it is graded by the amount of antigen a B cell captured and presented to Tfh cells in the light zone. Hypermutation scales with it.
key_facts.numbers: 1 to 6 divisions per DZ cycle; DEC-OVA-targeted cells ~50% mCherry-negative (max divisions) at 60 h vs even spread in controls
key_facts.source: Gitlin AD, Shulman Z, Nussenzweig MC 2014, Nature 509:637 (PMC4271732)

key_facts.fact: The canonical somatic hypermutation rate is ~1 mutation per 10^3 bp per cell division, but the rate is actively regulated — high-affinity cells divide more and mutate LESS per division (shortened G0/G1).
key_facts.numbers: 1 x 10^-3 per bp per division baseline; cells doing 6 divisions accumulated only 2-2.5-fold (not 6-fold) more mutation; 8 mutations / 125,628 bp in high-affinity cells over 24 h
key_facts.source: Merkenschlager J et al. 2025, Nature (PMC12058521); baseline rate also in De Silva & Klein 2015 Nat Rev Immunol (PMC4399774)

key_facts.fact: The GC is a slaughterhouse. Direct apoptosis-indicator imaging shows a small standing apoptotic fraction but very fast corpse clearance, implying massive turnover.
key_facts.numbers: 3.6-5.7% of GC B cells active-caspase-3+ at any instant; fragmentation 20.6 min after commitment (first morphological signs 12.5 min); ~46% of GC B cells lost in 5.3 h; 'up to half of all GC B cells dying every 6 h'
key_facts.source: Mayer CT et al. 2017, Science 358:eaao2602 (PMC5957278)

key_facts.fact: Death is zone-specific and mechanistically different: light-zone cells die by default unless positively selected; dark-zone cells die because AID has destroyed their immunoglobulin genes.
key_facts.numbers: 43% and 58% of apoptotic DZ cells carried non-productive Ig transcripts vs only 9% and 14% of apoptotic LZ cells
key_facts.source: Mayer CT et al. 2017, Science (PMC5957278)

key_facts.fact: Cyclic re-entry is strongly asymmetric: bulk flow DZ->LZ, with only a minority of LZ cells positively selected to return; the rest die or exit as memory/plasma cells.
key_facts.numbers: ~50% of DZ cells transition to LZ over ~4 h; <10% of LZ cells return to DZ over 6 h; 10-30% of LZ arrivals are positively selected; typical selected cell divides ~2x per LZ-DZ cycle
key_facts.source: Mesin L, Ersching J, Victora GD 2016, Immunity 45:471 (PMC5123673); Victora GD et al. 2010, Cell 143:592 (PMC3035939)

key_facts.fact: Measured GC spatial/motility parameters from two-photon imaging, fitted to an agent-based model: GC treated as a sphere; B cells move as a persistent random walk; FDC contacts are brief.
key_facts.numbers: GC radius R = 160 µm; B-cell motility coefficient 21.4 ± 4.2 µm^2/min (WT) vs 8.5 ± 3.5 in Cxcl13-/-; persistence time 1.24 min; ~8% inter-zonal migration per hour; B-FDC contacts mostly <=5 min, mean 2-3 min
key_facts.source: Figge MT et al. 2008, J Exp Med 205:3019 (PMC2605235)

key_facts.fact: Individual GCs are polyclonal at seeding and lose diversity at wildly different rates; efficient affinity maturation does not require homogenising selection, so many clones mature in parallel.
key_facts.numbers: tens to >100 distinct B-cell clones seed each GC (chicken gamma globulin immunisation)
key_facts.source: Tas JMJ et al. 2016, Science 351:1048 (PMC4938154)

key_facts.fact: A lymphoid organ runs many asynchronous GCs; individual GC lifetimes are variable, and new GCs keep forming well past the peak of the response.
key_facts.numbers: 10-16 GCs per popliteal lymph node (NP-OVA); hundreds per spleen (SRBC); fitted individual GC lifetime ~12.5-17.5 days; new GCs form until at least day 12; overall GC response ~3 weeks
key_facts.source: Arulraj T, Binder SC, Meyer-Hermann M 2021, Cells 10:1736 (PMC8306527); Arulraj et al. 2021 Front Immunol 12:705240

key_facts.fact: Textbook correction with modelling consequences: class switch recombination happens mostly BEFORE germinal centre entry, not during the GC reaction. IgM-dominated GCs exist.
key_facts.numbers: vast majority of CSR events precede onset of SHM by BCR phylogeny; only a small percentage of GC B cells show germline (switch) transcripts
key_facts.source: Roco JA et al. 2019, Immunity 51:337 (PMC6914312)

key_facts.fact: AID mutagenesis is genome-wide, not Ig-restricted. Deep sequencing of GC B cells found hundreds of off-target genes; susceptibility is predicted by RNA Pol II / Spt5 stalling density.
key_facts.numbers: 275 AID target genes identified (including 30 of 35 previously known); >1,500 genomic regions sequenced; high-density PolII/Spt5 found in only 2.3% of genes
key_facts.source: Álvarez-Prado ÁF et al. 2018, J Exp Med 215:761 (PMC5839764); commentary Reynaud & Weill 2018 JEM (PMC5839771)

key_facts.fact: t(14;18) BCL2-IGH is a V(D)J (RAG) accident in bone-marrow pre-B cells, not a GC accident — but it only becomes lymphoma after GC-dependent second hits. It is common in healthy people.
key_facts.numbers: t(14;18) in 85% of follicular lymphoma and ~30% of GCB-DLBCL; detectable at ~1 per 10^6 B cells in up to 70% of healthy adults; >10^-4 frequency flags elevated FL risk (seen in 20% of pre-FL cases)
key_facts.source: Mossadegh-Keller N et al. 2021, Front Immunol 12:683597 (PMC8323519); Brisou G, Nadel B, Roulland S 2021, HemaSphere 5:e563 (PMC8171372)

key_facts.fact: Burkitt lymphoma cleanly separates the two AID mechanisms: EBV+/endemic MYC breakpoints sit in/near rearranged V(D)J (somatic hypermutation), sporadic breakpoints sit in IGH switch/constant regions (class switch recombination).
key_facts.numbers: t(8;14) IGH::MYC ~80% of cases; t(2;8) IGK::MYC or t(8;22) IGL::MYC ~15-20%; Ki-67 proliferation index typically >95%
key_facts.source: Anagnostopoulos I et al. 2026, Cancers 18 (PMC12938643); O'Connor E et al. 2026, Transl Oncol (PMC12686623)

key_facts.fact: The T-cell side follows the same logic: nodal TFH-cell lymphoma (angioimmunoblastic type) was defined by gene-expression profiling as arising from the T follicular helper cell, the GC's selecting T cell.
key_facts.numbers: TFH origin established 2007; diagnostic requires >=2 of PD1, ICOS, CXCL13, CD10, BCL6; DUSP22 rearrangement in 20-30% of ALK-negative ALCL; TET2/DNMT3A mutations often shared with clonal haematopoiesis
key_facts.source: Bisig B, Savage KJ, de Leval L 2023, Haematologica 108:3227 (PMC10690915); Alaggio R et al. 2022, Leukemia 36:1720 (PMC9214472)

mechanisms: GC ANATOMY AND CYCLIC RE-ENTRY. A GC polarises ~7 days after antigen into a dark zone (DZ, CXCR4-hi CD83-lo CD86-lo, chemoattracted by CXCL12 from reticular cells) and a light zone (LZ, CXCR4-lo CD83-hi CD86-hi, held by CXCL13 from follicular dendritic cells). Centroblasts are the large, proliferating, AID-high DZ cells; centrocytes are the smaller, non-dividing LZ cells that test their newly mutated BCR. Cyclic re-entry: DZ proliferation + SHM -> migrate to LZ -> capture antigen from FDC immune complexes -> present peptide-MHCII to Tfh -> the ~10-30% that win return to the DZ and divide 1-6 more times. Mesin/Victora: a typical selected cell initiates one cycle in the LZ, migrates to the DZ in S phase, and divides ~2x per full cycle.

SELECTION IS A COMPETITION FOR T-CELL HELP, NOT FOR ANTIGEN PER SE. Victora 2010 showed T-cell help, not direct antigen competition, is the limiting factor: a B cell's fate is set by the density of peptide-MHCII it displays, which is proportional to antigen captured from FDCs. Winning cells transiently express MYC (repressed by BCL6 in the steady state), activate mTORC1, and are licensed for a number of DZ divisions proportional to help received. Cyclin D3 then drives 'inertial' cycling in the DZ, away from the licensing signal (Pae et al. 2021 JEM, PMC7754672) — and a Burkitt-associated CCND3 T283A gain-of-function knock-in produces larger GCs, more DZ proliferation, and clonal lymphoproliferation in old mice, a direct normal-biology-to-lymphoma link.

FDCs are the antigen library: they retain native, unprocessed antigen as immune complexes via CR1/CR2 and FcgammaRIIb, and cycle it through non-degradative endosomes so it stays available for weeks. They also make CXCL13, defining the LZ. Tfh cells (BCL6+, CXCR5-hi, PD-1-hi, ICOS+, IL-21+, CD40L+) are numerically limiting relative to GC B cells; GC-resident Tfh are a distinct CD90-neg/lo subset that stops proliferating after differentiation (Yeh et al. 2022 Immunity, PMC8842852).

AID BIOCHEMISTRY. AID (AICDA) deaminates cytosine to uracil on single-stranded DNA exposed by transcription, preferentially at WRCH/WRCY hotspots. Downstream processing decides the outcome: replication over U gives C>T/G>A transitions; UNG excision gives an abasic site read by translesion polymerases (transversions); MSH2/MSH6 recruitment of Pol-eta spreads mutation to A/T. In IgV genes this is SHM. In the repetitive switch (S) regions, dense deamination plus UNG/APE1 produces staggered double-strand breaks that classical NHEJ joins — that is CSR. AID requires transcription and is favoured by RNA Pol II stalling (Spt5, DOT1L/H3K79me2-3 modulate this), which is exactly why the off-target set is enriched in highly transcribed, stalled genes such as BCL6, MYC, PIM1, PAX5, RHOH, BTG2 (aberrant SHM).

WHY THE GC IS THE ORIGIN OF MOST B-CELL LYMPHOMAS — four compounding reasons. (1) AID makes programmed DNA lesions, including frank double-strand breaks in switch regions, at high rate; its targeting is imperfect (275 off-target genes in mouse GC B cells). (2) These lesions occur in cells cycling every 6-8 h, so a break has little time for repair and a mutant clone amplifies fast. (3) The GC transcriptional programme actively tolerates damage: BCL6 represses TP53, ATR, CHEK1 and CDKN1A, so GC B cells do not arrest or die in response to the damage AID inflicts. (4) The default fate is apoptosis, imposing intense selection for any lesion that confers survival or T-cell-help independence (BCL2 translocation, CD40/NF-kB-activating mutations, EZH2/CREBBP/KMT2D epigenetic lesions that freeze the GC state). The GC is therefore a somatic Darwinian reactor with a mutator switched on — exactly the conditions for oncogenesis.

TRANSLOCATIONS FROM FAILED CSR (AID, in or around the GC): sporadic/immunodeficiency Burkitt t(8;14) IGH::MYC with breakpoints in Smu/Sgamma switch regions; most primary IGH translocations of multiple myeloma — t(4;14) NSD2/MMSET-FGFR3, t(14;16) MAF, t(14;20) MAFB, and a subset of t(11;14) CCND1 — which map to switch regions; BCL6 translocations in DLBCL (BCL6 is itself an AID target and can join IGH switch regions or many non-Ig partners); IGL::MYC and IGK::MYC. TRANSLOCATIONS FROM FAILED SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION: endemic/EBV+ Burkitt t(8;14) with breakpoints in or adjacent to rearranged V(D)J; aberrant SHM point mutations in PIM1, PAX5, MYC, RHOH, BCL6 5' region in DLBCL/PCNSL. TRANSLOCATIONS FROM FAILED V(D)J RECOMBINATION (RAG, bone marrow precursor B cells, before any GC): t(14;18) BCL2::IGH of follicular lymphoma and ~30% of GCB-DLBCL, with the IGH breakpoint at JH; t(11;14) CCND1::IGH of mantle cell lymphoma, classically at the DJ junction in a pre-B cell. Key modelling point: the founding lesion and the transforming lesions can occur in different compartments and decades apart.

B-CELL COUNTERPART MAP. Germinal centre B cell — Burkitt lymphoma (dark-zone-like, MYC-driven), follicular lymphoma and GCB-DLBCL (light-zone-like, BCL2/EZH2/CREBBP/KMT2D), high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (isotype-switched t(14;18)+ GC B cell; Varano et al. 2025 Blood Cancer Discov, PMC12209767), nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (LP cells are GC B cells), classic Hodgkin lymphoma (a 'crippled' GC B cell that has lost a functional BCR yet escaped apoptosis). Post-GC / activated B cell — ABC-DLBCL (activated B / plasmablastic or memory-derived, MYD88 L265P + CD79B, NF-kB-dependent), primary CNS lymphoma (late GC-exit, IgM+ memory-related), plasmablastic lymphoma, primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (thymic B cell). Memory B cell — CLL/SLL (IGHV-mutated = post-GC memory-like; IGHV-unmutated = pre/less GC-experienced), hairy cell leukaemia (late-activated memory B cell). Marginal zone B cell — extranodal MALT, nodal and splenic marginal zone lymphomas (t(11;18) API2::MALT1 and t(14;18) IGH::MALT1 are not AID V(D)J/CSR-classic Ig-oncogene juxtapositions in the same sense; MALT is chronic-antigen driven, e.g. H. pylori); EBV-driven immunoblastic/immunosuppression-related lymphoma also maps to tonsillar MZ B cells (Torgbor et al. 2025 J Virol, PMC12363164). Naive / mantle zone B cell — mantle cell lymphoma (t(11;14), mostly IGHV-unmutated; a leukaemic non-nodal subtype is IGHV-mutated and more GC-experienced). Plasma cell — multiple myeloma, plasmacytoma, lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenstrom (post-GC B cell with plasmacytic differentiation, MYD88 L265P).

T-CELL AND NK COUNTERPART MAP (WHO-HAEM5 / ICC 2022). T follicular helper cell — nodal TFH-cell lymphoma, angioimmunoblastic type (AITL), follicular type and NOS; these are the direct T-cell counterpart of the GC selector cell and characteristically carry TET2, DNMT3A, IDH2 R172 and RHOA G17V mutations, with TET2/DNMT3A often arising earlier as clonal haematopoiesis. Activated cytotoxic T cell — ALK+ and ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK- ALCL: DUSP22 rearrangement 20-30%, JAK1/STAT3 mutations 20-30%, TP53 mutations 23%). Th1/TBX21 vs Th2/GATA3 mature CD4 T cell — the two transcriptional subgroups of PTCL-NOS. Skin-resident memory CD4 T cell — mycosis fungoides / Sezary syndrome. Intraepithelial T cell — enteropathy-associated and monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma. Gamma-delta T cell — hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma. Effector-memory cytotoxic CD8 — T-LGL leukaemia. Regulatory/CD4 T cell — adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma (HTLV-1). NK cell — extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type (EBV+).
modellable: Cell-cycle clock: GC B cell full cycle 6-8 h (Nakagawa 2021). Draw divisions-per-DZ-visit from 1-6, monotonically increasing in captured-antigen/pMHCII signal (Gitlin 2014). Implement DZ cycling as 'inertial' — once licensed, the cell completes its programmed divisions without further Tfh input (cyclin D3-dependent).

Mutation operator: apply SHM at 1e-3 per bp per division over a ~350 bp IgV target (~0.35 mutations per V region per division, i.e. ~1 mutation per V-region per ~3 divisions, or ~1 per 1000 bp per division). Optional refinement: make the per-division rate DECREASE with affinity (Merkenschlager 2025) — implement as rate ∝ 1/(1+k·affinity) while divisions ∝ affinity.

Mutation outcome distribution: use a rule where the large majority of IgV mutations are neutral or deleterious, a minority affinity-enhancing, and a defined fraction are BCR-crippling (frameshift/stop). Calibrate the crippling fraction against the observation that 43-58% of apoptotic DZ cells carry non-productive Ig transcripts vs 9-14% in the LZ (Mayer 2017).

Death process: two distinct death rules. (a) DZ death = AID-induced BCR destruction, applied at mutation time. (b) LZ death = default apoptosis unless positively selected within the dwell window. Global calibration target: 3.6-5.7% of GC B cells apoptotic at any instant with a 20.6 min corpse-clearance time, i.e. ~46% of the GC B cell pool lost every ~5-6 h. NOTE the tension with Wittenbrink's lower bound of 3% loss per hour — treat 3%/h to 50%/6h as the plausible envelope and run sensitivity analysis over it.

Zone transition rates: P(DZ -> LZ) such that ~50% of DZ cells transition over ~4 h (hazard ~0.17/h); P(LZ -> DZ) < 10% over 6 h (hazard ~0.017/h). Alternatively drive this mechanistically with CXCR4/CXCL12 vs CXCR5/CXCL13 gradients on a lattice.

Selection probability: 10-30% of cells arriving in the LZ are positively selected per cycle; the remainder die or exit as memory/plasma cells. Make selection a rank-order competition for a limited number of Tfh cells rather than an absolute affinity threshold.

Spatial layout: sphere of radius ~160 µm (volume ~1.7e7 µm^3), split into equal DZ and LZ halves (Wittenbrink: DZ ≈ LZ). Cell diameter ~10 µm implies a packing upper bound of order 1e4-3e4 B cells; treat absolute GC B-cell number as a poorly constrained free parameter in the 1e3-1e4 range and fit it.

Motility: persistent random walk with motility coefficient 21.4 µm^2/min and persistence time 1.24 min (Figge 2008); mean instantaneous speed ~6 µm/min. B-FDC contacts: mean 2-3 min, mostly <=5 min. B-Tfh conjugates are short-lived (order minutes) but the productive help signal integrates over repeated contacts.

Seeding and clonality: seed each GC with tens to >100 distinct founder clones (Tas 2016); a workable influx rule is ~2 seeder cells/hour for the first ~96 h (Arulraj 2021). Founder-cell affinity distribution and antigen dose are the two parameters that most strongly control GC lifetime.

Organ-level scaling: 10-16 GCs per popliteal lymph node (NP-OVA) or hundreds per spleen (SRBC), initiated asynchronously; individual GC lifetime ~12.5-17.5 days with substantial variance; whole response ~3 weeks. Model GCs as independent agents with staggered start times and antigen depleting exponentially (A(t) = A0·e^-kt).

Antigen: FDCs hold a finite pool of immune-complexed native antigen (e.g. 3000 'antigen portions' per GC in Meyer-Hermann-family models) that depletes and is recycled; declining antigen is the main driver of GC shutdown.

CSR timing rule: perform class switching mostly at GC entry / pre-GC activation, not stochastically throughout the GC (Roco 2019). Allow a small residual in-GC CSR rate. This matters for modelling switch-region-mediated translocations, which should therefore be dated to the pre-GC/early-GC window.

Oncogenic-lesion module: (a) V(D)J-derived founder lesion, applied once at B-cell genesis with low probability — calibrate to ~1 t(14;18)+ cell per 1e6 circulating B cells in ~70% of healthy adults; (b) AID off-target lesion, applied per division to a set of ~275 susceptible loci, with per-locus rate scaled by transcription/Pol II stalling; (c) CSR-associated DSB translocation, applied only during switching. Emergent quantity to fit: only a tiny fraction of t(14;18)+ carriers ever develop FL, so require multiple cooperating hits (CREBBP KAT-domain mutation detectable a median 5.8 years pre-diagnosis).

Lesion frequency targets for calibration: t(14;18) 85% of FL, ~30% of GCB-DLBCL; KMT2D inactivating mutations 70-90% of FL, up to 30% of DLBCL; CREBBP 50-70% of FL, ~25% of DLBCL; EZH2 gain-of-function 10-30% of FL/GCB-DLBCL; 95% of FL carry >=1 chromatin-modifier mutation; MYC::IG in ~100% of Burkitt (t(8;14) ~80%, IGK/IGL ~15-20%); Ki-67 >95% in Burkitt.

Zone-of-origin assignment for simulated tumours: Burkitt = dark-zone programme (high proliferation, MYC-on, low NF-kB); FL and GCB-DLBCL = light-zone programme (BCL2-on, blocked exit, dependent on Tfh/CD40 signals); ABC-DLBCL = activated/plasmablastic exit state with chronic-active BCR/NF-kB and blocked PRDM1-driven plasma-cell differentiation.
open_questions: Absolute GC B-cell number is not well established in the literature. Published figures range from ~1e3 to ~1e5 and are usually model assumptions rather than direct counts; the 160 µm radius (Figge 2008) is itself a modelling idealisation fitted to imaging.

The Tfh:GC-B ratio inside the GC is repeatedly asserted to be small and limiting but I could not find a clean primary quantification; treat any specific ratio you use as a free parameter and state it as such.

Reconciling the death rate: Wittenbrink 2011 gives a MINIMUM loss of 3%/h; Mayer 2017 infers ~50% loss per 6 h (~11%/h). Whether the true turnover is nearer 3%/h or 10%/h changes total GC throughput by 3-4x and therefore changes the expected number of AID-induced lesions per GC per day by the same factor.

How much CSR really occurs inside the GC (Roco 2019 says very little) is still debated, and it directly determines when switch-region-mediated translocations such as sporadic Burkitt t(8;14) and myeloma t(4;14) can be generated.

The identity and dynamics of the t(14;18)+ 'FL-like' premalignant cell — whether it recirculates through many GCs over years, and how many GC transits it takes to accumulate CREBBP/KMT2D hits — is unresolved and is exactly what a cell-level simulation could address.

The 'cell of origin' language is a transcriptional-resemblance claim, not proof of the transformed cell's actual developmental stage; lymphomas can adopt a GC-like programme without the founding lesion having occurred in a GC (t(14;18) is the clearest example).

Human vs mouse: nearly all quantitative GC dynamics above are from mouse immunisation models. Human GC parameters (tonsil, lymph-node fine-needle aspirate) are far less constrained, and human GCs are generally larger and longer-lived.

Tumour microenvironment and immune evasi.domain: Tumour microenvironment and immune evasion in follicular lymphoma (FL): niche dependence, T follicular helper / stromal / macrophage / Treg / exhausted-CD8 biology, antigen-presentation loss, spatial architecture, and oxygenation — assembled for a cell-level (agent-based) simulation builder.

key_facts.fact: Two gene-expression signatures from tumour-infiltrating immune cells, not tumour B cells, split FL patients into survival quartiles independently of clinical prognostic variables — the founding evidence that FL outcome is microenvironment-determined.
key_facts.numbers: 191 untreated biopsies (95 training / 96 test); test-set quartile median survival 13.6, 11.1, 10.8, 3.9 years; survival-predictor score = (2.71 x IR-2 average) - (2.36 x IR-1 average); high score = poor outcome
key_facts.source: Dave SS et al., NEJM 2004;351:2159-69, PMID 15548776 (score formula and gene lists from NEJM full text)

key_facts.fact: Immune-response-1 (favourable) contains T-cell and some macrophage genes; immune-response-2 (adverse) contains macrophage/dendritic-cell genes. IR-1 is not a simple T-cell-count surrogate: many standard T-cell genes did not predict survival.
key_facts.numbers: IR-1: CD7, CD8B1, ITK, LEF1, STAT4, ACTN1, TNFSF13B(BAFF). IR-2: TLR5, FCGR1A, SEPT10, LGMN, C3AR1. Non-predictive T-cell genes: CD2, CD4, LAT, TRIM, SH2D1A
key_facts.source: Dave SS et al., NEJM 2004, PMID 15548776

key_facts.fact: Purified FL B cells undergo rapid spontaneous apoptosis ex vivo despite constitutive BCL2, driven by caspase-8/-3 and loss of BCL-xL and c-FLIP-L; feeder/stromal contact rescues them. This is the direct reason FL is hard to culture.
key_facts.numbers: CD32(CDw32)-transfected fibroblast feeders reduced apoptosis from 67% to 16% (p=0.001) and raised viability +114%; FDC-line coculture blocks caspase-8/-3 and restores c-FLIP-L via CD54(ICAM-1), CD106(VCAM-1), CD40; no proliferation induced
key_facts.source: Buske C et al., Leukemia 1997, PMID 9369419; Goval JJ et al., Haematologica 2008, PMID 18556415; Ghia P et al., Blood 1998, PMID 9414291

key_facts.fact: Tfh cells in FL secrete IL-4 at levels far above normal tonsil Tfh, creating an IL-4/STAT6 axis; phospho-STAT6-positive lymphoma B cells localise next to PD-1+ Tfh in situ. CD40L and IL-21 co-signal from the same cells.
key_facts.numbers: 677 non-redundant genes define the FL B-cell/non-B interface across 26 functional networks; CD10+ Tfh subset is IL-4-hi / IFN-gamma-lo / TNF-alpha-hi and is amplified specifically in FL; FL-Tfh are IL-21-hi, IL-17-lo
key_facts.source: Pangault C et al., Leukemia 2010, PMID 20944673; Ame-Thomas P et al., Blood 2015, PMID 25733581

key_facts.fact: A recurrent tumour-intrinsic mutation makes FL B cells hypersensitive to Tfh-derived IL-4, i.e. the niche dependence is genetically reinforced rather than incidental.
key_facts.numbers: STAT6 DNA-binding-domain mutations in 13% of FL (33/258); gain-of-function, upregulating CCL17, CCL22, FCER2/CD23 and PARP14 in a feed-forward loop
key_facts.source: Mentz M et al., Leukemia 2022, PMID 35851155

key_facts.fact: IL-4-high FL Tfh cells, not the FL B cells themselves, induce CXCL12 overexpression in lymphoid stromal precursors; CXCL12 then drives FL B-cell activation, migration and adhesion. This is a two-step, T-cell-mediated stromal conversion.
key_facts.numbers: CXCL12 overexpression confirmed in situ in FL-infiltrated lymph node and bone marrow stroma; CXCL12-driven FL B-cell responses antagonised by BTK and PI3K inhibitors

key_facts.fact: FL B cells preferentially contact CD49a+ fibroblastic reticular cells and reprogram human lymphoid stroma in situ downstream of TNF and TGF-beta, raising CCL19 and CCL21. Three human lymphoid stromal subsets were defined (CD49a+ precursor, FRC, FDC).
key_facts.numbers: Tonsil-derived reference: 3 LSC subsets by flow/imaging/RNA-seq; FL-associated changes measured in situ
key_facts.source: Mourcin F et al., Immunity 2021;54(8):1788-1806, PMID 34166622

key_facts.fact: Tumour-associated macrophage content predicts FL survival, but the sign of the effect flips with therapy — CD163-high is adverse with R-CVP and favourable with R-CHOP. Any simulation must make macrophage effect therapy-conditional.
key_facts.numbers: Farinha: >15 vs <15 CD68+/hpf, median OS 5.0 vs 16.3 years (n=99, p<0.001). Kridel: BCCA R-CVP CD163-high 5-yr PFS 38% vs 72% (n=186); PRIMA R-CHOP CD163-high 5-yr PFS 60% vs 44% (n=395)
key_facts.source: Farinha P et al., Blood 2005;106:2169-74, PMID 15933054; Kridel R et al., Clin Cancer Res 2015, PMID 25869385

key_facts.fact: High total FOXP3+ Treg content predicts better FL survival, while effector-Treg density inside neoplastic follicles rises with stage and correlates inversely with intrafollicular CD8 infiltration — compartment matters more than total count.
key_facts.numbers: Carreras: median Treg 10.5%; >10% / 5-10% / <5% gave 5-yr OS 80% / 74% / 50% (p=0.001, n=97). Inoue: intrafollicular FOXP3+CTLA-4+ eTreg 12/mm2 (duodenal FL) vs 78 (limited-stage) vs 109 (advanced); CD8 TIL 1827 vs 1150 vs 1188/mm2; eTreg-CD8 r=-0.267
key_facts.source: Carreras J et al., Blood 2006;108:2957-64, PMID 16825494; Inoue H et al., Br J Haematol 2020, PMID 32383789

key_facts.fact: PD-1 level splits FL T cells into two opposite populations: PD-1-high intrafollicular Tfh that help the tumour, and PD-1-low interfollicular exhausted TIM-3+ cells that predict poor survival. LAG-3 (not PD-1 alone) marks true exhaustion; TIGIT marks suppressive Tregs plus exhausted effectors.
key_facts.numbers: PD-1-low CD4 and CD8 counts correlated with reduced OS (p=0.007 and 0.04, n=32); PD-1+LAG-3+ cells show reduced cytokine/granule output and LAG-3 correlates with poor outcome; TIGIT+ T cells adverse in n=82 by mass cytometry; FL flow atlas (n=91 FL vs 43 hyperplasia) finds Treg subsets TIGIT+CTLA4+ and PD1+TIGIT+CTLA4+TIM3+
key_facts.source: Yang ZZ et al., Blood Cancer J 2015, PMID 25700246; Oncotarget 2017, PMID 28977875; Clin Cancer Res 2020, PMID 32631956; El Daker S et al., Haematologica 2025, PMID 39911114

key_facts.fact: MHC class II loss is driven mainly by CREBBP inactivation, which is among the earliest clonal events in FL and reduces CIITA-dependent class-II transcription; the effect is reversible pharmacologically by HDAC3 inhibition.
key_facts.numbers: Chromatin-modifier mutation in 96% of FL tumours, two or more in 76%; CREBBP most enriched in the earliest inferable progenitor across 59 sequential biopsies from 22 patients; CREBBP-mutant B cells stimulate less T-cell proliferation and tumours show fewer CD4 helper and CD8 memory T cells
key_facts.source: Green MR et al., PNAS 2015;112:E1116-25, PMID 25713363; Jiang Y et al., Cancer Discov 2017;7:38-53, PMID 27733359

key_facts.fact: MHC class I loss in FL is mostly epigenetic, via silencing of the class-I transactivator NLRC5, rather than B2M mutation; B2M loss appears predominantly at histologic transformation. Frank B2M/CD58 co-inactivation is a DLBCL phenomenon.
key_facts.numbers: NLRC5 promoter hypermethylation in 30% and copy-number loss in ~6% of 172 FL tumours; aberrant cases show reduced HLA-A, TAP1, PSMB8, PSMB9; CD8 and CD137 correlate with NLRC5 (r>0.7, p<0.0001). B2M, MYC, TP53 mutations emerge at transformation. DLBCL: B2M inactivated in 29%, CD58 in 21%, aberrant HLA-I/CD58 in >60%
key_facts.source: Gunawardana J et al., EJHaem 2020, PMID 35845006; Hesius EAM et al., J Clin Pathol 2025, PMID 39890445; Challa-Malladi M et al., Cancer Cell 2011, PMID 22137796

key_facts.fact: CD47 blockade plus rituximab converts the macrophage compartment from bystander to effector, with the strongest early signal in FL — consistent with FL's macrophage-rich niche.
key_facts.numbers: Hu5F9-G4 + rituximab phase 1b, n=22 (7 FL, 15 DLBCL): overall ORR 50%, CR 36%; FL ORR 71%, CR 43%; DLBCL ORR 40%, CR 33%; 95% rituximab-refractory; 30 mg/kg gives ~100% CD47 receptor occupancy; on-target anemia
key_facts.source: Advani R et al., NEJM 2018;379:1711-21, PMID 30380386

key_facts.fact: CD3xCD20 bispecifics kill independently of MHC/peptide presentation, so they bypass the CREBBP/NLRC5 antigen-presentation defects — but escape then occurs by CD20 antigen loss and transformation instead.
key_facts.numbers: Mosunetuzumab SC pivotal R/R FL (>=2 prior lines, n=94): ORR 76.6%, CR 61.7%, median DoCR 34.6 months, median PFS 23.7 months. First-line mosunetuzumab (n=42, 88% FL): end-of-treatment ORR 100%, CR 86%, 2-yr PFS 89%; of 4 progressions, 2 were CD20 loss and 2 transformation
key_facts.source: Bartlett NL et al., Am J Hematol 2026, PMID 41862428; Lynch RC et al., J Clin Oncol 2026, PMID 42600120

key_facts.fact: Neoplastic follicles behave as immune-privileged compartments: CD8 T cells are excluded from the follicle core, those inside are exhausted along a radial gradient, and a Treg-rich band sits at the follicle boundary separating it from an effector-rich interfollicular zone.
key_facts.numbers: Imaging mass cytometry, 156 FL cores, 4.2M cells, two 39-marker panels: CD8 = 2.0% of cells at GC core vs 28.3% interfollicular; TOX+PD-1+ fraction 73.6% at GC core falling to 7.2% in T-cell zone; TFR 70% of Tregs at GC core vs <2% in T zones; CD14-high FDC per-cell intensity predicts PFS (HR 1.50 multivariate, p=0.0007) and OS (HR 1.76); VISTA+ myeloid 56% vs PD-L1+ 12%; median segmented cell area 68 um2; 50 um neighbourhood radius
key_facts.source: Elemento O, Ravichandran H, Beguelin W, Scott DW, Steidl C, Melnick AM. bioRxiv 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.06.09.731209 (PREPRINT, not peer reviewed)

key_facts.fact: Independent peer-reviewed spatial studies agree that compartment and co-localisation, not global density, carry prognostic information in FL — but cohorts are small (n=32 and n=127) and results are not yet cross-validated.
key_facts.numbers: Hagos 2022 (n=32): low interfollicular CD8+FOXP3+ density associated with relapse (p=0.0057, HR 0.42 independent of FLIPI). Tsakiroglou 2021 (n=127, 7-plex, 30 um interaction radius): Shannon entropy of cell types HR 0.19 (0.06-0.65) and of spatial interactions HR 0.39 (0.20-0.75) for OS. Mondello 2021 (n=496): absent intrafollicular CD4 predicts early failure, pooled OR 2.37 (1.48-3.79)
key_facts.source: Hagos YB et al., Hematol Oncol 2022, PMID 35451108; Tsakiroglou AM et al., Cancer Immunol Immunother 2021, PMID 33929583; Mondello P et al., Blood Cancer J 2021, PMID 34267181

mechanisms: Tfh -> B cell axis: FL-infiltrating CXCR5+ICOS+PD-1+BCL6+ Tfh deliver IL-4 (STAT6/JAK), IL-21 and membrane CD40L. IL-4/STAT6 drives CD23/FCER2, CCL17, CCL22, PARP14; CD40 ligation raises BCL-xL and c-FLIP-L and blocks the caspase-8 -> caspase-3 apoptosis that otherwise kills FL B cells ex vivo. STAT6 mutation (13%) amplifies the same axis cell-intrinsically.

Stromal conversion is Tfh-mediated and two-step: IL-4-high Tfh (not the tumour B cells) induce CXCL12 in CD49a+ stromal precursors/FRCs; FL B cells separately reprogram stroma via TNF and TGF-beta, raising CCL19/CCL21. The resulting CXCL12/CCL19/CCL21 gradients recruit and retain both tumour B cells and T cells, closing a positive-feedback loop. FL-derived extracellular vesicles extend the same polarisation to bone-marrow MSCs (Dumontet 2021 Blood, PMID 33881493).

FDC contribution: FDC networks provide contact survival signals through CD54/ICAM-1, CD106/VCAM-1 and CD40, plus complement/immune-complex antigen retention. A CD14-high activated FDC state is reported to mark the proliferative tumour niche and predict early progression (preprint evidence only).

Macrophage axis: monocytes are recruited/polarised by stromal CCL2 and tumour signals; TAMs are simultaneously (i) a protumoural M2-like compartment (adverse with chemotherapy) and (ii) the effector arm of rituximab ADCP (favourable with rituximab-based therapy). CD47-SIRPalpha is the 'don't eat me' brake on that effector arm; blockade plus rituximab restores phagocytosis.

Regulatory suppression: highly oligoclonal Tregs and Tfr accumulate; effector Tregs (FOXP3+CTLA-4+, often TIGIT+) concentrate at and inside neoplastic follicles, inversely tracking intrafollicular CD8. Treg diversity inversely correlates with CD8 TCR diversity (Liu 2015 Oncoimmunology, PMID 26155390).

CD8 exhaustion: intratumoural CD8 T cells progressively acquire PD-1, then TIM-3, LAG-3 and TIGIT. LAG-3 (with PD-1) rather than PD-1 alone marks functionally exhausted cells; IL-12 upregulates LAG-3. Dual PD-1 + LAG-3 blockade restores IFN-gamma and IL-2 ex vivo.

Antigen-presentation escape has two separable arms. Class II: CREBBP loss-of-function (earliest clonal event) depletes enhancer H3K27ac at CIITA-dependent MHC-II loci, which BCL6/SMRT/HDAC3 then represses unopposed — reversible by HDAC3 inhibition. Also CTSS mutation/amplification perturbs CD74 processing and MHC-II peptide loading (Bararia 2020 Cell Rep, PMID 32330423). Class I: NLRC5 promoter hypermethylation or copy loss lowers HLA-A, TAP1, PSMB8/9; B2M mutation is largely a transformation event.

Therapeutic consequence: checkpoint blockade and vaccines depend on intact presentation, so CREBBP/NLRC5-defective FL is predicted to resist them; CD3xCD20 bispecifics and CAR-T bypass MHC entirely, which is why their response rates in FL are high — with escape then shifting to CD20 antigen loss, transformation, or T-cell exhaustion.

Physical/spatial mechanism: the neoplastic follicle acts as a spatial barrier. Effector CD8 cells are largely confined to interfollicular zones; a Treg/Tfr-enriched rim at the follicle boundary and an exhaustion gradient peaking at the germinal-centre core constitute an architectural, not purely molecular, immune-evasion mechanism (preprint-level evidence).

Metabolic/oxygen mechanism (weaker evidence): germinal centres are relatively hypoxic in mice; FL cells grown as 3D aggregates activate a genuine hypoxia response (pimonidazole+, HIF-1A, VEGFA) with NF-kB activation, quiescence and resistance to doxorubicin, bendamustine and NK killing — a plausible but not directly demonstrated in-vivo mechanism in human lymphomatous nodes.
modellable: Cell-death / rescue rule: baseline FL B-cell apoptosis without support ~67% over days in culture, falling to ~16% with stromal contact (Buske 1997). Implement as a contact- or ligand-dependent survival hazard: apoptosis rate high by default, multiplied by ~0.24 when in contact with FDC/FRC/feeder agent, mediated by CD54/CD106/CD40 (Goval 2008).

Signalling rules: IL-4 (Tfh-secreted, diffusible) -> STAT6 phosphorylation in FL B agent -> survival + CD23/CCL17/CCL22 output; CD40L requires cell-cell contact (immunological synapse), so make it contact-only with radius ~1 cell diameter. Give a subpopulation (13%) a STAT6-mutant flag with elevated gain on the IL-4 input (Mentz 2022).

Chemokine fields to simulate: CXCL12 (stroma, IL-4-inducible), CXCL13 (FDC), CCL19/CCL21 (reprogrammed FRC), CCL2 (monocyte recruitment). Preprint ABM used 4 diffusive chemokine fields on a 100x100 grid with circular tissue radius 45 and 8 cell types.

Spatial geometry: two-compartment tissue (intrafollicular vs interfollicular). CD8 occupancy 2.0% of cells at GC core vs 28.3% interfollicular; Treg/Tfr 70% of Tregs at GC core vs <2% in T zones; exhaustion (TOX+PD-1+) 73.6% at core decaying to 7.2% at T zone — implement as a radial gradient with the boundary as a Treg barrier. Median cell area 68 um2; neighbourhood/interaction radius 30-50 um (Tsakiroglou used 30 um; preprint used 50 um).

Absolute densities for calibration: intrafollicular CD8 TIL 1150-1188/mm2 in nodal FL (1827/mm2 in indolent duodenal FL); intrafollicular effector Treg 78-109/mm2 nodal vs 12/mm2 duodenal (Inoue 2020). Treg as % of cells: median 10.5% (Carreras 2006). Macrophage threshold: 15 CD68+ cells per high-power field separates prognostic groups (Farinha 2005).

Grade-dependent structure: follicle compactness 0.46 (grade 1) -> 0.31 (grade 3A); macrophage clustering (Ripley's L) falls 32% grade 1 -> 3A; Ki-67+ B cells 7.5% -> 16.3%. Use as a proliferation-rate and architecture-disorder parameter pair (preprint, unrefereed).

Antigen-presentation state variables per tumour agent: MHC-II-low flag with prevalence tied to CREBBP mutation (chromatin-modifier mutation in 96% of FL; CREBBP among earliest); MHC-I-low flag with prevalence ~30-36% via NLRC5 hypermethylation/CNL. Rule: MHC-I-low blocks CD8 killing and checkpoint-blockade benefit but does NOT block CD3xCD20 bispecific killing.

Antigen-escape rule for T-cell engagers: seed a CD20-negative subclone at ~3% frequency with ~20% reduced proliferation (preprint ABM parameterisation); clinically, 2 of 4 progressions after first-line mosunetuzumab were CD20 loss (Lynch 2026).

Therapy response targets for validation: mosunetuzumab R/R FL ORR 76.6%, CR 61.7%, median PFS 23.7 months, median DoCR 34.6 months; first-line CR 86%, 2-yr PFS 89%; magrolimab+rituximab FL ORR 71%, CR 43%.
Outcome targets for validation: median survival by immune-signature quartile 13.6 / 11.1 / 10.8 / 3.9 years (Dave 2004); FOXP3 strata 5-yr OS 80 / 74 / 50%; CD68-high median OS 5.0 vs 16.3 years.

Oxygen/diffusion module: measured oxygen consumption rate in ex vivo naive mouse lymph node slices = 2.16 +/- 0.87 uM/s in the T-cell region (live tissue) vs 0.08 +/- 0.06 uM/s killed control; 1.6 +/- 1.0 uM/s static vs 0.30 +/- 0.28 uM/s under continuous perfusion; slices 300 um thick; T-cell zone consumes faster than B-cell/cortical regions (Anbaei 2024, Analyst, PMID 38535830). Use with an O2 diffusion coefficient to get consumption-limited penetration depth.

Hypoxia thresholds used experimentally: 1% O2 defines the 'germinal-centre-like' hypoxic condition in B-cell culture models; 21% is the artificial normoxic control; breathing 60% O2 in vivo reverses germinal-centre hypoxia and shrinks GC B, Tfh and plasmacyte frequencies (Abbott 2016). Human head-and-neck metastatic cervical NODES (not lymphoma) gave median pO2 13.9 +/- 8.0 mmHg with 29% of readings <5 mmHg pre-treatment (Gabalski 1998) — the closest available direct nodal pO2 anchor.

Vascular module: quantify tumour-to-vessel distance covering 90% of tumour (TVD90) on CD34-stained sections — lower TVD90 (denser vasculature) was an INDEPENDENT predictor of inferior OS (p=0.01) and transformation risk in 84 uniformly treated FL. Angiogenic sprouts defined as CD34+ structures <30 um2 in area, more numerous in poor-prognosis FL and surrounded by CD163+ macrophages (Farinha 2010, PMID 20713461; Clear 2010, PMID 20375314).

Composition prior: T cells reported as >87% of non-malignant immune cells in dissociated FL samples — but this is extraction-biased and should be treated as an upper bound, not a tissue truth (Radtke & Roschewski, Blood 2024, PMID 38194685). ~85% of classic FL carries t(14;18)/IGH::BCL2.
open_questions: No direct pO2 measurement exists for human lymphomatous lymph nodes. Every hypoxia claim in FL is inferential: mouse germinal-centre pimonidazole staining, CAIX in human reactive/tumour-draining node germinal centres, or FL cells grown as 3D aggregates in vitro. Whether an intact human FL follicle in vivo is hypoxic is genuinely unknown.

Direction of the vascular effect is unresolved across studies: Farinha 2010 found denser vasculature (low TVD90) adverse, whereas other microvessel-density series in FL found no FLIPI association. Whether angiogenesis in FL is a driver, a marker of high-grade disease, or a measurement artefact of counting method is unsettled.

HIF-1alpha positivity in DLBCL (~60% of cases) predicted BETTER outcome with R-CHOP (Evens 2010 JCO, PMID 20048181), which contradicts a simple 'hypoxia = aggressive' model in B-cell lymphoma and should be handled explicitly in any oxygen module.

The prognostic direction of macrophages, and of Tregs, is treatment-dependent and has reversed between cohorts. A simulation that hard-codes 'M2 macrophage = bad' or 'Treg = bad' will not reproduce the FL literature.

Whether Tfh are truly expanded in FL or merely more numerous because there are more follicles is contested: Townsend 2020 (Haematologica, PMID 31537685) found the Tfh proportion inside neoplastic follicles equal to normal germinal centres, with the apparent increase driven by follicle number, not follicle content.

The strongest spatial dataset (156 cores, 4.2M cells, VISTA-dominant myeloid checkpoint, CD14-high FDC niche, and its own agent-based model) is a June 2026 bioRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed and has not been independently replicated.

Reproducibility of immunohistochemical microenvironment quantification in FL is documented to be poor between laboratories (Lunenburg Lymphoma Biomarker Consortium, Sander 2014 Haematologica, PMID 24510338): manual scoring agreement was low-to-moderate for CD3, CD4, CD8, FOXP3 and CD68. Absolute densities from single-centre studies should be treated as soft priors.

No FL model system reproduces the intact follicle. 3D spheroid/PDLS systems (Faria 2023 JITC, PMID 37899130) recapitulate the exhausted T-cell phenotype and drug responses but not follicle architecture, FDC networks or vasculature.
Tumour microenvironment and immune evasi.caveats: Confidence grading: the Tfh/IL-4/CD40L axis, the ex-vivo culture dependence, the CREBBP-MHC-II link, the Dave signatures and the therapy response rates are strongly and repeatedly sourced (high). Checkpoint-receptor prognostics rest on single-centre cohorts of n=32-91 with no external validation (medium). All spatial architecture numbers with per-compartment percentages come from one unrefereed 2026 bioRxiv preprint (Elemento/Melnick) and must be labelled as such if used to parameterise a model. The oxygen section is the weakest: there is no human FL nodal pO2 measurement anywhere in the retrieved literature, the germinal-centre hypoxia claim is mouse pimonidazole/HypoxyProbe work (Cho 2016 Nature PMID 27501247; Abbott 2016 J Immunol PMID 27798169), the human corroboration is CAIX staining in germinal centres of breast-cancer patients' nodes (Firmino 2021, PMID 34377597), and the FL-specific hypoxia evidence is an in-vitro 3D aggregate model (Gravelle 2014 Am J Pathol, PMID 24231431) whose hypoxia signature was also detectable in FL biopsy transcriptomes. Treat oxygen as a modelled variable with wide priors, not a measured one. Two numbers I could not source and did not include: absolute cell-type fractions of a whole FL lymph node, and neoplastic follicle diameter in micrometres — both are commonly asserted but I found no citable measurement in this search. Also note the search covers Europe PMC and open web only; NEJM, Nature, Lancet, Wiley and ASH sites blocked direct fetching, so a small number of primary full texts were read via abstracts plus secondary confirmation (the Dave 2004 gene lists and score formula were confirmed from NEJM full-text text quoted in web search results, not from a fetched PDF).

Why indolent NHL (follicular lymphoma) r.domain: Why indolent NHL (follicular lymphoma) relapses and is not cured: the common progenitor cell (CPC) reservoir model, clonal phylogenetics of paired diagnosis/relapse samples, divergent vs linear evolution, reservoir location and drug tolerance, histological transformation to DLBCL, POD24; plus the parallel DLBCL cure/refractory question and ctDNA/MRD. Framed for parameterising an agent-based, cell-level simulation.

key_facts.fact: IGHV somatic-hypermutation genealogies of sequential FL/transformed-FL biopsies fit origin from a shared, less-mutated common progenitor cell rather than direct descent. A father(donor)/son(recipient) transplant pair developing FL and t-FL proved the CPC is long-lived and transmissible.
key_facts.numbers: 13 of 18 sequential FL/t-FL pairs (72%) showed a CPC-compatible tree; CPC, FL and t-FL clonotypes can coexist in one lymph node
key_facts.source: Carlotti E et al. 2009, Blood 113:3553-7, PMID 19202129

key_facts.fact: A donor and recipient both developed FL 7 years after allogeneic transplant plus donor lymphocyte infusion. The shared founder clone was recoverable in the infused donor cells, directly demonstrating a circulating, transplantable, long-lived precursor reservoir.
key_facts.numbers: Identical BCL2/IGH in 1 of 2,000 DLI cells; 15 shared exome mutations, 14 (incl. EP300, KLHL6) recovered from the DLI at ~361,723x coverage; 6 later mutations (incl. ARID1A stop) private to one FL
key_facts.source: Weigert O et al. 2012, Cancer Discovery 2:47-55, PMID 22585168, PMC4530787

key_facts.fact: Whole-genome/exome sequencing of paired FL-transformed FL showed branching, not linear, evolution in every case: a shared mutational trunk (the CPC) with independent branches. Chromatin-modifier mutations are trunk events; NF-kB/EBF1 lesions are acquired at transformation.
key_facts.numbers: 10/10 pairs branching; 8/10 'rich' CPC (high clonal semblance), 2/10 'sparse' CPC (only 4 shared nonsynonymous mutations); early = CREBBP, EZH2, KMT2D; late = EBF1 (5/32 cases), MYD88, TNFAIP3
key_facts.source: Okosun J et al. 2014, Nature Genetics 46:176-81, PMID 24362818, PMC3907271

key_facts.fact: Across serial biopsies, CREBBP mutation is the somatic event most enriched in the earliest inferable progenitor. CREBBP loss lowers MHC class II on tumour B cells and reduces T-cell stimulation, giving the CPC an immune-evasion phenotype at the founder stage.
key_facts.numbers: 59 sequential biopsies from 22 patients; chromatin-modifier mutation in 96% of FL tumours, two or more in 76%; CREBBP KAT-domain hotspot codons 1300-1700 carry 68.8% (201/292) of CREBBP mutations
key_facts.source: Green MR et al. 2015, PNAS 112:E1116-25, PMID 25713363, PMC4364211; codon data from Schroers-Martin 2023

key_facts.fact: Transformation and non-transforming early progression have opposite clonal dynamics. Transformation is dominated by clones nearly absent at diagnosis (divergent); early progression is dominated by clones already major at diagnosis (linear). Neutral drift cannot explain the transformation pattern.
key_facts.numbers: Divergent in 13/15 (87%) transformations, relapse clones <1% at diagnosis; linear in 5/6 progressions (1/6 divergent). Diagnosis-specific mutation fraction 0.175±0.105, transformation-specific 0.366±0.166. Drift simulations reproduced the pattern in 0.6% of runs (88.1% lost the mutant allele), binomial p<0.001
key_facts.source: Kridel R et al. 2016, PLoS Medicine 13:e1002197, PMID 27959929, PMC5154502

key_facts.fact: In non-transformed FL relapse specifically, evolutionary divergence is a continuum, not a binary. Paired primary/relapse samples span near-zero evolution to fully divergent, with genetic and epigenetic (methylation) divergence correlated, suggesting co-evolution from a shared ancestor.
key_facts.numbers: 33 paired primary/relapse t(14;18)+ non-transformed FL; divergence magnitude correlated across IGH SHM, driver mutations, copy number and DNA methylation. Independent cohort (n=30 patients, 94 biopsies) found divergent and linear patterns at similar frequency in relapsing and transforming FL
key_facts.source: Loeffler M et al. 2015, Leukemia 29:456-63, PMID 25027518; Bai B et al. 2024, Blood Cancer Journal 14:147, PMID 39191762, PMC11350178

key_facts.fact: FL founder lesions are detectable in blood years before diagnosis. Beyond t(14;18) alone, CREBBP KAT-domain mutations distinguish people who will develop FL from healthy t(14;18) carriers, defining the committed CPC genotype.
key_facts.numbers: CREBBP KAT mutations in 14/48 (29%) pre-FL subjects vs 0/13 t(14;18)+ and 0/20 t(14;18)- healthy controls (p=0.03, p=0.007); detectable median 5.8 y before diagnosis; tumour-derived variants found in 13/34 (38%) pre-diagnostic samples at median 5 y (range 1-9)
key_facts.source: Schroers-Martin JG et al. 2023, Cancer Discovery 13:1310-23, PMID 36939219, PMC10239329

key_facts.fact: Direct test of the lymphoma-stem-cell hypothesis: FL founder mutations were present in mature B-cell fractions but absent from sorted CD34+ haematopoietic progenitors in every patient tested. The CPC sits in the committed B-cell lineage, not in an HSC.
key_facts.numbers: 7 patients sorted (bone marrow and blood); CREBBP allele fraction 40.3% in mature CD19+/CD20+ marrow B cells, undetectable in CD34+/CD20- precursors and in T cells; KMT2D stop mutation likewise HSPC-negative in 1 patient; 5 further patients confirmed
key_facts.source: Schroers-Martin JG et al. 2023, Cancer Discovery 13:1310-23, PMID 36939219, PMC10239329

key_facts.fact: Lymph nodes that are histologically benign after FL therapy still carry the tumour's t(14;18) and CREBBP KAT-domain mutations. This is the most direct human evidence that the reservoir survives immunochemotherapy in lymphoid tissue.
key_facts.numbers: 5 of 8 paired benign/malignant excisional biopsies were post-treatment, median lead time 2.9 y (overall range 0.1-6.8 y); post-treatment hyperplasias lost most tumour mutations but retained t(14;18) + CREBBP, gaining only rare private mutations; patients later relapsed
key_facts.source: Schroers-Martin JG et al. 2023, Cancer Discovery 13:1310-23, PMID 36939219, PMC10239329

key_facts.fact: t(14;18)-positive cells in healthy people are not quiescent naive B cells but germinal-centre-experienced, memory-like (IgD-/CD27+ switched) B cells with FL-like features. High circulating frequency predicts FL up to 15 years ahead, but most carriers never progress.
key_facts.numbers: EPIC cohort: frequency >1e-4 gives OR 23.17 (95% CI 9.98-67.31) for later FL, significant up to 15 y before diagnosis; typical healthy frequencies 1e-6 to 1e-5 of CD19+ cells; fewer than 5% of t(14;18) carriers develop FL
key_facts.source: Roulland S et al. 2006, J Exp Med 203:2425-31, PMID 17043145, PMC2118129; Roulland S et al. 2014, JCO 32:1347-55, PMID 24687831

key_facts.fact: The reservoir is anatomically distributed: bone marrow, lymph node and blood. FL subclones migrate between anatomical sites, and each site holds hundreds of subclones, so a single biopsy never captures the population.
key_facts.numbers: Bone marrow involvement in 67% (35/52) of FL by 10-colour flow, median 1.2% of leukocytes (IQR 0.3-7%); PET detects only 30% (14/46). Deep IGH sequencing of flow-sorted subsets found hundreds of subclones per sample, the majority at frequency <1e-2
key_facts.source: Aren M et al. 2022, Cytometry B 104:229-236, PMID 36314855; Carlotti E et al. 2015, PLoS One 10:e0134833, PMID 26325507, PMC4556522; Odabashian M et al. 2020, Blood 135:834-844, PMID 31932843

key_facts.fact: Molecular residual disease after frontline FL therapy predicts progression, quantifying incomplete reservoir clearance. Residual-disease negativity at 1e-6 in long remission has so far had a 100% negative predictive value for relapse.
key_facts.numbers: GALLIUM (n>1000): MRD+ at mid-induction HR 3.03 (2.07-4.45), at end-of-induction HR 2.25 (1.53-3.32) for PFS; MRD+ at mid-induction 4.8% with bendamustine vs 16.0% with CHOP; during maintenance 20.7% (R-CHOP) vs 7.0% (G-CHOP). Separate cohort: 31/47 (66%) undetectable at 1e-6, none relapsed
key_facts.source: Pott C et al. 2024, JCO 42:550-561, PMID 38096461; Chauhan A et al. 2024, Clin Lymphoma Myeloma Leuk, PMID 38789312

key_facts.fact: Histological transformation to DLBCL proceeds at a roughly constant hazard without plateau, is lower in the immunochemotherapy era, and carries clearly worse survival, with early transformation worst.
key_facts.numbers: Pre-rituximab: 3%/y continuous through 15 y, 28% (170/600) cumulative at median 109 mo (Al-Tourah). Immunochemo era: ~2%/y, 10.7% at 5 y (Link). NLCS: 14.3% (379/2652) at median 6.8 y follow-up, post-transformation median OS 5 y, 5-y OS 75% vs 85%. PRIMA: HT median OS 3.8 vs 6.4 y, HR 3.9 (2.2-6.9); 58% of transformations occurred in year 1
key_facts.source: Al-Tourah AJ et al. 2008 JCO 26:5165-9, PMID 18838711; Link BK et al. 2013 JCO 31:3272-8, PMID 23897955; Wagner-Johnston ND et al. 2015 Blood 126:851-7, PMID 26105149; Sarkozy C et al. 2016 JCO 34:2575-82, PMID 27298402

key_facts.fact: POD24 is progression, relapse or treatment failure within 24 months of starting frontline immunochemotherapy. About one fifth of FL patients meet it, and it separates a population with near-normal survival from one with high lymphoma-specific mortality.
key_facts.numbers: National LymphoCare: 19% (110/588) after R-CHOP; 5-y OS 50% vs 90%; FLIPI-adjusted HR 6.44 (4.33-9.58), validation HR 19.8. Pooled 13 trials, 5,225 patients: POD24 time-dependent HR for OS 4.85, 24-month landmark HR 3.06; predictors male sex OR 1.30, PS>=2 OR 1.63, B2M>=3 mg/L OR 1.43, high FLIPI OR 3.14

key_facts.fact: DLBCL is genuinely cured in a majority. Patients event-free at 24 months have survival matching the age/sex-matched general population; the refractory minority has dismal salvage outcomes, and pre-treatment genetics partly predict which group a patient falls into.
key_facts.numbers: R-CHOP gives durable remission in >60% of advanced-stage patients. EFS24 achievers: SMR 1.18 (p=0.25), validated SMR 1.09 (p=0.71). Refractory (SCHOLAR-1, n=636): ORR 26%, CR 7%, median OS 6.3 mo, 20% alive at 2 y; 5-y cumulative refractory incidence 20%. Predicted 5-y OS by genetic subtype: MCD 26%, N1 36%, BN2 65%, EZB 68%
key_facts.source: Maurer MJ et al. 2014 JCO 32:1066-73, PMID 24550425, PMC3965261; Crump M et al. 2017 Blood 130:1800-8, PMID 28774879; Schmitz R et al. 2018 NEJM 378:1396-1407, PMID 29641966, PMC6010183; Abrisqueta P 2024 J Clin Med, PMID 38610693

key_facts.fact: ctDNA kinetics are an independent, quantitative early readout of DLBCL cure. Log-fold clearance after one or two cycles stratifies outcome, and more sensitive assays reclassify a quarter of apparently ctDNA-negative patients as still positive with worse outcomes.
key_facts.numbers: ctDNA detectable pre-therapy in 98% of 217 patients. Early molecular response (2-log drop after C1): 24-mo EFS 83% vs 50%; major molecular response (2.5-log after C2): 82% vs 46%; in salvage, EMR 100% vs 13%. Interim ctDNA+ after 2 cycles: 5-y TTP 41.7% vs 80.2% (PPV 62.5%, NPV 79.8%). PhasED-seq finds ctDNA in an extra 25% of CAPP-Seq-negative patients after 2 cycles, detection into the ppm range
key_facts.source: Kurtz DM et al. 2018 JCO 36:2845-53, PMID 30125215, PMC6161832; Roschewski M et al. 2015 Lancet Oncol 16:541-9, PMID 25842160, PMC4460610; Kurtz DM et al. 2021 Nat Biotechnol 39:1537-47, PMID 34294911, PMC8678141

mechanisms: Two-compartment architecture. A small, slowly-cycling, memory-like reservoir of t(14;18)+ / CREBBP-KAT-mutant B cells carries only the founder subset of drivers. A large, proliferating, fully-driver-loaded tumour bulk is what therapy kills. Relapse = re-expansion and re-diversification from the reservoir, not regrowth of the killed bulk. This is the single mechanistic claim the simulation should be built around.

Founder lesion order. t(14;18) BCL2-IGH arises first, as a V(D)J recombination error in a pro-B/pre-B cell in bone marrow (constitutive BCL2 = apoptosis evasion). CREBBP KAT-domain loss is acquired later, in the committed mature B-cell lineage, and adds immune evasion via reduced CIITA-dependent MHC class II. Evidence: allele-fraction ordering plus non-detection in CD34+ cells (Schroers-Martin 2023).

Germinal-centre recycling as the engine. BCL2-overexpressing memory B cells re-enter GCs repeatedly; multiple GC transits are required before FL-associated developmental arrest and constitutive AID mutator activity appear. Each re-entry is a mutation-and-selection round for the precursor pool (Sungalee 2014, J Clin Invest, PMID 25384217).

Developmental arrest, not stemness. Lineage-tree analysis of flow-sorted FL subpopulations places the oligoclonal FL population in a narrow intermediate maturation state that retains ongoing SHM but cannot differentiate further. That is a differentiation block, distinct from a self-renewing stem-cell hierarchy (Carlotti 2015).

BCR N-glycosylation dependency. Ongoing SHM inserts N-glycosylation sequons into IgV; the resulting oligomannoses engage calcium-dependent lectins on tissue macrophages, driving antigen-independent BCR signalling. Sites are conserved in >96% of subclones across diagnosis, progression and transformation, so this is a hard selective constraint the reservoir must satisfy (Odabashian 2020, Blood, PMID 31932843).

Divergence is end-point-specific. Transformation is positive selection of a near-invisible minor lineage (Kridel: rare-clone takeover in 87%); early progression is drift/expansion of an already-dominant clone (linear in 5/6). Non-transformed later relapse spans the whole continuum (Loeffler 2015). Do not model 'relapse' with one evolutionary rule.

Why the reservoir is drug-tolerant (partly inferential): (i) memory-like quiescence makes it a poor target for cycle-active cytotoxics; (ii) it lacks the full driver set, so agents aimed at bulk-tumour lesions (EZH2, later NF-kB events) miss it; (iii) BCL2 translocation does not confer venetoclax sensitivity in FL, and SETD1B loss (7% FL, 16% DLBCL) confers outright BH3-mimetic resistance (Portelinha 2024, J Exp Med, PMID 39235528); (iv) niche protection in bone marrow and lymphoid tissue; (v) CREBBP-driven MHC-II loss blunts T-cell-mediated clearance, which matters for rituximab/T-cell-engaging therapy.

Spatial heterogeneity is real and large. Simultaneous biopsies from different sites in one patient show divergent genomes; single-cell VDJ shows site-to-site divergence in most patients. A well-mixed single-compartment model will systematically underestimate reservoir diversity.

DLBCL cure/failure axis is different in kind. There, the question is whether frontline therapy achieves total eradication in one pass. Determinants are tumour-intrinsic genetics (MCD/N1 vs BN2/EZB), IPI, and above all the measured rate of ctDNA clearance during cycles 1-2 — i.e. a kill-rate parameter, not a reservoir parameter.
modellable: Reservoir size / detection floor. Healthy-carrier t(14;18)+ frequency 1e-6 to 1e-5 of CD19+ cells; FL-risk threshold >1e-4 (OR 23.2). FL bone marrow involvement in 67% of patients at median 1.2% of leukocytes (IQR 0.3-7%). Use ~1e-6 to 1e-4 of the B-cell pool as the CPC compartment size range.

Clonal diversity. Hundreds of distinct subclones per sample, the majority at frequency <1e-2 (Carlotti 2015). Seed the agent population with a long-tailed subclone frequency distribution, not a handful of clones.

Divergence probabilities as a branch rule. Transformation event: draw founder from clones at <1% frequency with probability 0.87 (13/15); early progression: draw from clones already dominant at diagnosis with probability 0.83 (5/6). Non-transformed later relapse: sample divergence uniformly across the continuum.

Trunk/branch mutation split. Shared trunk plus diagnosis-private fraction 0.175 +/- 0.105 (range 0.038-0.431) and relapse-private fraction 0.366 +/- 0.166 (range 0.063-0.664) (Kridel 2016). 'Rich' CPC in 8/10 vs 'sparse' CPC (4 shared nonsynonymous mutations) in 2/10 (Okosun 2014).

Driver acquisition order and timing. Trunk: BCL2-IGH, then CREBBP KAT, KMT2D, EZH2. Branch/late: EBF1, MYD88, TNFAIP3, TP53, B2M, CCND3, GNA13, S1PR2, P2RY8, plus CNAs (EZH2, MDM2, MYC, REL amplification; 6q loss; chr12/18 gain). CREBBP detectable median 5.8 y (range 1-9 y) before clinical diagnosis — a usable pre-clinical latency prior.

Transformation hazard. Constant ~3%/y for at least 15 y pre-rituximab (28% cumulative at ~9 y); ~2%/y in the immunochemotherapy era (10.7% at 5 y). Implement as a constant-hazard Poisson event, not a rising hazard.

POD24 as a calibration target. ~19-20% of frontline-immunochemotherapy patients progress within 24 months; their 5-y OS is 50% vs 90%. Any FL simulation should reproduce a ~20% early-failure mode with that survival split. Modern baseline stratification: FLIPI24 low-risk 24-mo event rate 10-12% vs high-risk 22-35% (Maurer 2026 JCO, PMID 41329901).

Successive-remission decay (strongest single time-series target).
