Median PFS by line: 1L 4.73 y, 2L 1.5 y, 3L 1.1 y, 4L 0.9 y, 5L 0.6 y, 6L 0.5 y; median OS from 2L 11.7 y, 3L 8.8 y, 4L 5.3 y, 5L 3.1 y, 6L 1.9 y (Batlevi 2020, Blood Cancer J, PMID 32678074, PMC7366724). Reproducing this geometric-like decay is a hard test of any reservoir + resistance model.

Therapy kill parameters from MRD. FL end-of-induction MRD positivity ~7-13% (regimen-dependent); mid-induction MRD+ 4.8% (bendamustine) vs 16.0% (CHOP); MRD+ HR for PFS 2.25 at EOI, 3.03 at mid-induction. Undetectable at 1e-6 in sustained remission had NPV 100% (31/31). Calibrate log-kill per cycle against these.

DLBCL clearance kinetics. Model log-kill directly: 2-log ctDNA drop after cycle 1 and 2.5-log after cycle 2 separate 24-mo EFS 83% vs 50% and 82% vs 46%. ctDNA detectable pre-therapy in 98%. A residual population below CAPP-Seq but above PhasED-seq sensitivity (extra 25% of 'negatives') still relapses — an explicit sub-detection-threshold survivor compartment.

GC re-entry rule. Require multiple sequential GC transits before a BCL2+ agent acquires the FL developmental-arrest phenotype and constitutive AID activity; each transit applies SHM and a selection filter (Sungalee 2014).

BCR N-glycan constraint as a fitness gate. >96% of subclones retain an N-glycosylation sequon across all disease events; N-gly-negative subclones are progressively deleted. Implement as near-lethal fitness cost for sequon loss, with rare long-lived exceptions.

Spatial compartments. Minimum three: lymph node (GC niche, macrophage lectin, TFH), bone marrow (protected niche, 67% occupancy, ~1.2% of leukocytes), peripheral blood (trafficking channel). Allow subclone migration between sites; independent divergence at separate sites is the empirical default.

DLBCL frontline outcome partition for validation: >60% durable remission; EFS24 achievers SMR 1.18 (indistinguishable from background mortality); ~20% become refractory with median OS 6.3 mo and 20% alive at 2 y. Genetic-subtype 5-y OS priors: MCD 26%, N1 36%, BN2 65%, EZB 68%.
open_questions: What is the CPC's actual cell-surface phenotype and cycling status in vivo? It is inferred from mutation genealogies and from sorted bulk fractions, never prospectively isolated and functionally validated. No one has purified a CPC and shown it reconstitutes FL. This is the biggest gap between the model and the data.

Absolute reservoir size in a treated patient in remission. Nobody has measured how many CPCs survive therapy per patient. All current numbers are frequencies in blood or marrow aspirate, not absolute counts, and the tissue-resident fraction is essentially unmeasured.

Is CPC drug tolerance primarily cell-intrinsic (quiescence, apoptotic-threshold biology, missing drug targets) or niche-mediated (marrow/lymphoid microenvironment protection)? The evidence is mostly circumstantial for both; they have very different implications for a simulation's kill rules.

What fraction of non-transformed FL relapses are truly divergent? The clean numbers are for transformation (87%) and early progression (17%). For later, non-transformed relapse only a continuum has been reported, with no agreed cut-off separating divergent from linear. Treat any single 'fraction of relapses that are divergent' figure as unreliable.

Can rare CREBBP/KMT2D-bearing HSPCs be excluded entirely? Schroers-Martin explicitly cannot exclude them, and one prior report described a CREBBP mutation in a CD34+/CD38+ marrow population in a single FL patient. The negative evidence is strong but not absolute.

Are POD24 and histological transformation the same underlying biology? Kridel's data say no (linear vs divergent), yet both are early, both are lethal, and POD24 cases in one cohort had smaller inter-biopsy genomic distances than non-POD24. A model that treats them as one failure mode will likely misfit.

Does eradicating the CPC actually cure FL? Never tested. It is the field's motivating hypothesis (Okosun, Araujo-Ayala) but no therapy has been shown to deplete the reservoir, and no trial has used CPC clearance as an endpoint.

In DLBCL, is the ~60% cured because their tumour had no reservoir-like compartment, or because frontline therapy happened to clear it? ctDNA measures the consequence, not the cause. Whether a CPC-like precursor exists in de novo DLBCL is largely unstudied outside the EZB/FL-derived subset.
Why indolent NHL (follicular lymphoma) r.caveats:
Sample sizes for the clonal phylogenetics are small: Kridel n=15 transformation + 6 progression, Okosun n=10 pairs, Carlotti n=18, Weigert n=1 donor/recipient pair. Percentages like 87% divergent rest on 13 of 15 patients. Treat them as order-of-magnitude priors, not precise parameters.

The CPC is an inferred entity throughout. Every "CPC" fact is a reconstruction from mutation genealogies in bulk tissue, plus the transplant natural experiments. No study has prospectively isolated a CPC and shown it initiates FL. The model is well-supported but is not the same class of evidence as a functional stem-cell assay.

Selection bias: patients with sequential biopsies are biopsied because something clinically changed. Cohorts are enriched for transformation and aggressive relapse, so divergence fractions from these series probably overstate divergence in the general FL population.

Era effects matter for every clinical number. Transformation is 3%/y pre-rituximab vs ~2%/y after; DLBCL genetic-subtype survival (MCD 26%, EZB 68%) predates CAR-T and bispecifics; POD24 was defined for chemoimmunotherapy and its meaning after frontline bispecific or lenalidomide-rituximab regimens is not established. Do not mix eras in one calibration.

Two clinical figures are quoted with soft sourcing and should be treated as medium confidence: the ">60% cured" DLBCL frontline figure is a review-level statement (Abrisqueta 2024) not a single-trial number, and the FL bone-marrow-involvement figure (67%, median 1.2% of leukocytes) comes from one 52-patient flow-cytometry study and varies substantially with detection method (PET found only 30%).

Kridel's drift simulation (0.6% of runs reproducing the transformation pattern) is a specific neutral-evolution null model, not a general proof that selection is required. Its assumptions should be read before reusing that number as a modelling target.

I am not a clinician and this is not clinical guidance; the numbers here are for model parameterisation.

Single-cell mechanisms of anti-CD20 anti.domain: Single-cell mechanisms of anti-CD20 antibodies, CHOP-type chemotherapy, bendamustine, antimetabolites, platinum, antibody-drug conjugates and radioimmunotherapy in non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with explicit cell-cycle dependence, immune-effector dependence, and resistance mechanisms, for parameterising a cell-level simulation.

key_facts.fact: Rituximab CDC is a mass-action, cycle-independent event whose efficiency scales linearly with surface CD20 density across CLL, PLL and MCL; complement regulators CD55/CD59 set a per-cell lysis threshold.
key_facts.numbers: Correlation CD20 level vs lysis r>=0.9, P<.0001 (n=33 CLL, 5 PLL, 6 MCL); blocking CD55+CD59 raised lysis of poor responders 5-6 fold; CD46 MFI<100, CD55 MFI 20-1200, CD59 MFI 20-250
key_facts.source: Golay J, 2001, Blood; PMID 11719378

key_facts.fact: Absolute CD20 surface density measured by calibrated-bead quantitative flow cytometry differs several-fold between B-cell malignancies; CLL is the low-density outlier. Directly usable as a per-agent receptor count.
key_facts.numbers: CD20 molecules/cell (mean, x10^3): normal B 94; CLL 65; B-PLL 129; MCL 123; splenic lymphoma with villous lymphocytes 167; hairy cell leukaemia 312
key_facts.source: Ginaldi L, 1998, J Clin Pathol; PMID 9708202

key_facts.fact: In vivo anti-CD20 B-cell depletion in mice was entirely dependent on effector-cell Fc-gamma receptors and monocytes/macrophages, and completely intact in complement-deficient animals. No T- or NK-cell requirement was demonstrable.
key_facts.numbers: 12 anti-mouse-CD20 mAbs, all 4 IgG isotypes; depletion abolished in FcR common gamma-chain-null mice; depletion fully effective in C1q-, C3- and C4-deficient mice
key_facts.source: Uchida J, 2004, J Exp Med; PMID 15210744

key_facts.fact: Human response to rituximab tracks FcgammaRIIIa affinity genotype, supporting ADCC as a dominant in vivo arm; effector-cell quality is a patient-level modifier, not a tumour-cell property.
key_facts.numbers: Follicular lymphoma n=49: FCGR3A-158 V/V (n=10) 100% response at 2 months and 90% at 12 months vs 158F carriers 67% and 51% (P=.03); BCL2-JH clearance 5/6 vs 5/17
key_facts.source: Cartron G, 2002, Blood; PMID 11806974

key_facts.fact: Obinutuzumab is a type II glycoengineered (afucosylated) IgG1: higher FcgammaRIIIa affinity, far more potent ADCC, much stronger caspase-independent direct (non-apoptotic) cell death, but REDUCED CDC versus rituximab.
key_facts.numbers: KD FcgammaRIIIa-158V/-158F: GA101 55/270 nM vs rituximab 660/2000 nM (~12x and ~7x); ADCC EC50 ~35x more potent; whole-blood B-cell depletion 10-25x more potent, 1.5-2.5x greater absolute depletion
key_facts.source: Mossner E, 2010, Blood; PMID 20194898 / PMC2881503

key_facts.fact: Obinutuzumab's greater in vitro potency does NOT translate uniformly in the clinic: clearly superior in CLL with chlorambucil, but no PFS benefit over rituximab with CHOP in first-line DLBCL.
key_facts.source: Goede V, 2014, NEJM PMID 24401022; Vitolo U, 2017, J Clin Oncol PMID 28796588

key_facts.fact: CD20-negative transformation is a documented relapse phenotype after rituximab-containing therapy and is at least partly epigenetic, since demethylating agents restore CD20 mRNA within days.
key_facts.numbers: 5 of 19 rebiopsied relapses (26%) were CD20-protein-negative (3 de novo DLBCL, 2 transformed FL); CD20 mRNA re-induced within 3 days by 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine; all 5 patients died within 1 year

key_facts.fact: Rituximab infusion causes acute, sub-lethal CD20 loss and complement exhaustion: complement component C2 is consumed and B cells re-enter blood immediately with markedly reduced CD20.
key_facts.numbers: CLL patient sera post-infusion lose C3b-opsonisation and killing capacity unless supplemented with normal serum or purified C2; CD20 loss occurs within the infusion (minutes to hours)
key_facts.source: Kennedy AD, 2004, J Immunol; PMID 14978136

key_facts.fact: Mechanistically, surface loss of the rituximab:CD20 complex is dominated by antigenic modulation (internalisation), with macrophage-mediated shaving/trogocytosis an epiphenomenon of phagocytosis; the two compete for the same complexes.
key_facts.numbers: Type II glycoengineered antibody showed a modest but significant increase in shaving vs type II wild-type IgG1; blocking phagocytosis decreased shaving and increased modulation
key_facts.source: Dahal LN, 2018, J Immunol 201:1211-1221; PMID 29997125

key_facts.fact: Of CHOP, only vincristine is strictly cycle-phase-specific (M phase, tubulin binding). Cyclophosphamide is phase-non-specific DNA crosslinking. Prednisone kills lymphoid cells transcriptionally, without requiring division.
key_facts.numbers: Vinca alkaloids act at M phase via tubulin binding; cyclophosphamide metabolites crosslink DNA and are classified phase-non-specific
key_facts.source: Mohammadgholi A / vincristine combination review, 2021, PMC8468923; classification also standard pharmacology

key_facts.fact: Doxorubicin poisons topoisomerase II, trapping cleavage complexes into protein-linked double-strand breaks; lesion formation is phase-independent but lethality is amplified by replication-fork collision, so kill is S/G2-M enriched, not M-restricted.
key_facts.numbers: Also generates DNA intercalation and free-radical damage; commonly classed phase-non-specific with S/G2-M preference
key_facts.source: unsourced - background knowledge (retrieved sources gave conflicting classification)

key_facts.fact: Glucocorticoids kill lymphoid cells by ligand-activated glucocorticoid receptor binding GREs and transactivating pro-apoptotic genes (BIM/BCL2L11 axis), driving intrinsic apoptosis in resting as well as cycling lymphocytes.
key_facts.numbers: GC-induced apoptosis requires GR protein stability (KMT2D-dependent) and chromatin opening at GREs with PU.1 eviction; response develops over hours to ~1-2 days
key_facts.source: Beck D, 2024, Nat Commun PMID 39516193; Wu Y, 2024, J Biol Chem PMID 39025450

key_facts.fact: Bendamustine is mechanistically distinct from classical alkylators: it activates base-excision repair rather than alkyltransferase repair, inhibits mitotic checkpoints and induces mitotic catastrophe, explaining incomplete cross-resistance.
key_facts.numbers: Profiled in the NCI 60-cell-line screen; activity pattern unrelated to other DNA-alkylating agents; active in disease refractory to conventional alkylators
key_facts.source: Leoni LM, 2008, Clin Cancer Res; PMID 18172283

key_facts.fact: MMAE released inside an ADC-targeted cell reaches high intracellular concentration, is retained for hours, and is membrane-permeable, so it diffuses out and kills adjacent antigen-NEGATIVE cells; MMAF does not.
key_facts.numbers: Intracellular MMAE ~500 nmol/L after brentuximab vedotin; retention half-life 15-20 h; CD30-ADC with MMAE or PBD killed CD30-negative cells in admixed CD30+/CD30- tumours, MMAF failed
key_facts.source: Okeley NM, 2010, Clin Cancer Res PMID 20086002; Li F, 2016, Cancer Res PMID 26921341

key_facts.fact: The PBD dimer SG3199 (warhead of loncastuximab tesirine) is a picomolar minor-groove interstrand crosslinker whose low-distortion adducts evade repair, persist for >1 day, and largely escape MDR efflux.
key_facts.numbers: Mean GI50 151.5 pM across human solid and haematological lines; crosslinks form rapidly and persist over 36 h; ERCC1- or HR-defective cells hypersensitive; only moderately susceptible to multidrug resistance; rat plasma half-life ~8 min
key_facts.source: Hartley JA, 2018, Sci Rep 8; PMID 29992976 / PMC6041317

mechanisms: RITUXIMAB (type I anti-CD20, IgG1). Four arms: (1) CDC - C1q binds clustered Fc in lipid rafts, C3b deposition, MAC pores, osmotic lysis in minutes; (2) ADCC - NK-cell FcgammaRIIIa engagement, perforin/granzyme; (3) ADCP - macrophage/monocyte phagocytosis, whole-cell engulfment; (4) weak direct signalling (homotypic adhesion, modest apoptosis). CELL-CYCLE: entirely cycle-INDEPENDENT. A quiescent G0 CD20+ B cell is as lysable as a mitotic one; killing depends on antigen density, complement/effector availability and antibody occupancy. IMMUNE-DEPENDENT: yes, absolutely - remove complement AND FcgammaR-bearing cells and rituximab is nearly inert.

OBINUTUZUMAB (type II, glycoengineered/afucosylated). Binds a different CD20 epitope orientation, does NOT redistribute CD20 into lipid rafts, hence LOW CDC. Compensates with (a) ~10-35x stronger ADCC/ADCP from afucosylated Fc and higher FcgammaRIIIa affinity, and (b) strong direct, caspase-INDEPENDENT, actin/lysosome-dependent non-apoptotic cell death mediated by F(ab')2 crosslinking. Also internalises/modulates less than rituximab, so surface antibody persists longer. CELL-CYCLE: cycle-independent. IMMUNE-DEPENDENT: more so than rituximab for the Fc arm, less so for the direct-death arm (which works without effectors).

CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE. Prodrug -> hepatic CYP -> 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide -> aldophosphamide -> phosphoramide mustard (active bifunctional alkylator) + acrolein. Forms N7-guanine monoadducts and interstrand crosslinks. CELL-CYCLE: phase-NON-SPECIFIC (damages DNA in any phase, including G0) but cytotoxicity is realised when the cell attempts replication - so lethality is proliferation-biased even though damage is not. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT (though low-dose cyclophosphamide depletes Tregs, an immunomodulatory side effect).

DOXORUBICIN. Topoisomerase II poison stabilising the cleavable complex -> protein-linked DNA double-strand breaks; plus DNA intercalation, histone eviction and redox/free-radical damage. CELL-CYCLE: classed phase-non-specific, but kill is strongly enhanced in S/G2-M because replication/transcription collisions convert trapped complexes into lethal DSBs, and topo IIalpha is itself cell-cycle-regulated (high in S/G2/M, low in G0). Practically: models it as 'kills any cell, but with a 2-10x higher kill probability in cycling cells'. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT, though it is a classic immunogenic-cell-death inducer (calreticulin exposure, HMGB1 release).

VINCRISTINE. Binds beta-tubulin at the vinca site, suppresses microtubule dynamics, prevents mitotic spindle assembly, activates the spindle-assembly checkpoint -> prolonged metaphase arrest -> mitotic slippage or apoptosis. CELL-CYCLE: strictly M-PHASE-SPECIFIC. A cell that never enters mitosis during drug exposure is NOT killed. This is the sharpest 'kills only dividing cells' agent in CHOP and the key discriminator for the simulation. Kill therefore depends on the fraction of cells transiting M during the drug's effective exposure window, not on peak concentration alone. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT.

PREDNISONE/PREDNISOLONE. Diffuses in, binds cytosolic glucocorticoid receptor, GR dimerises and translocates to nucleus, binds GREs, transactivates pro-apoptotic BH3-only genes (BIM/BCL2L11), represses NF-kB and IL-2/BCR survival signalling, shifts the BCL2-family rheostat to trigger BAX/BAK mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilisation. CELL-CYCLE: cycle-INDEPENDENT - kills resting/G0 lymphoid cells efficiently; this is why steroids debulk lymphoma before any cytotoxic enters. Also causes G1 arrest. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT (cell-autonomous transcriptional program). Timescale: hours to ~48 h, slower than CDC.

BENDAMUSTINE. Nitrogen-mustard alkylating group fused to a benzimidazole (purine-analogue-like) ring. Bifunctional alkylation with more extensive and more durable DNA crosslinks than chlorambucil/phosphoramide mustard; repaired via base-excision repair rather than alkyltransferase, abrogates mitotic checkpoints and drives mitotic catastrophe as well as p53-dependent apoptosis. CELL-CYCLE: phase-NON-SPECIFIC damage, with a mitotic-catastrophe component realised on division. Only partially cross-resistant with cyclophosphamide. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT, but strongly and durably T-cell (CD4) depleting, which matters if the model couples chemo to antibody effector function.

HIGH-DOSE METHOTREXATE. Competitive DHFR inhibition -> depletion of reduced folates -> thymidylate and purine synthesis blockade -> thymineless state and replication-fork collapse. Intracellular polyglutamation traps MTX and prolongs inhibition after extracellular clearance. CELL-CYCLE: S-PHASE-SPECIFIC. Non-cycling cells are spared; kill is a function of exposure duration overlapping S-phase entry. Leucovorin rescue truncates the exposure window - explicitly a schedule/duration parameter, not a peak-concentration parameter. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT. Used at >=3 g/m2 for CNS penetration.

CYTARABINE (ara-C). Phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase to ara-CTP, incorporated by DNA polymerase into elongating DNA -> chain termination, stalled forks, DSBs. CELL-CYCLE: S-PHASE-SPECIFIC and profoundly SCHEDULE-DEPENDENT: total kill scales with the time the cell is exposed while in S, so continuous/repeated dosing over >= one cell-cycle length outperforms a single bolus of the same total dose. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT.

PLATINUM SALVAGE (cisplatin in DHAP, carboplatin in ICE, oxaliplatin in GDP/DHAOx). Aquated platinum forms 1,2-intrastrand d(GpG)/d(ApG) adducts (~90%) plus a minority of interstrand crosslinks. Adduct FORMATION is entirely cycle-independent, including in G0. Adduct-to-death CONVERSION requires replication-fork encounter or transcription blockade, so measured kill is S-phase-enriched. Repaired by nucleotide excision repair (ERCC1); interstrand crosslinks need HR/Fanconi pathway. IMMUNE-INDEPENDENT. Modelling note: this is the archetype of 'damage anytime, die on division' - if the simulation carries a damage state variable, platinum and alkylators should write to it in any phase and resolve it at S/M.

POLATUZUMAB VEDOTIN. Anti-CD79b IgG1 + protease-cleavable valine-citrulline linker + MMAE, DAR ~3.5. CD79b is BCR-associated, expressed on most B-NHL, and internalises efficiently. Cathepsin B in the lysosome releases free MMAE. PAYLOAD MECHANISM: MMAE binds tubulin -> G2/M arrest -> apoptosis. CELL-CYCLE: payload is M-PHASE-SPECIFIC, so the ADC only kills cells that attempt mitosis during payload retention (~15-20 h half-life). BYSTANDER: YES - MMAE is membrane-permeable and kills adjacent antigen-negative cells. IMMUNE-DEPENDENT: no for the payload; the naked-IgG Fc arm contributes little.

BRENTUXIMAB VEDOTIN. Anti-CD30 IgG1 (cAC10) + vc linker + MMAE, DAR ~4. Same payload logic as polatuzumab: intracellular MMAE ~500 nM, retention half-life 15-20 h, M-phase-specific kill, documented bystander killing of CD30-negative cells in admixed tumours. Relevant in NHL for CD30+ peripheral T-cell lymphoma and anaplastic large-cell lymphoma; CD30 expression is far more restricted than CD20, so antigen-negative fraction and bystander radius matter more.

LONCASTUXIMAB TESIRINE. Anti-CD19 IgG1 + tesirine (SG3249) -> released PBD dimer SG3199, DAR ~2.3. PAYLOAD MECHANISM: sequence-selective covalent binding in the DNA minor groove at 5'-PuGATCPy-3', forming interstrand crosslinks that cause minimal helix distortion, so they are poorly recognised by nucleotide excision repair and persist >36 h. CELL-CYCLE: DNA damage is inflicted regardless of phase - this is the ADC to model as 'kills any cell', in contrast to the MMAE ADCs. Lethality still depends on unrepaired crosslinks blocking replication/transcription. BYSTANDER: YES (PBD is membrane-permeable, demonstrated in admixed antigen-positive/negative tumours). Poor MDR1 substrate.

RADIOIMMUNOTHERAPY - Y-90 IBRITUMOMAB TIUXETAN. Murine anti-CD20 (ibritumomab) + tiuxetan chelator + Y-90, a pure high-energy beta emitter (Emax ~2.28 MeV), tissue range up to ~5 mm, physical half-life ~2.5-2.7 days. Kills by ionising radiation: DNA double- and single-strand breaks, base damage, indirect radical damage. CELL-CYCLE: cycle-INDEPENDENT damage (G0 cells are hit), though radiosensitivity varies by phase (G2/M most sensitive, late S most resistant) and lethality often manifests as mitotic death. CROSSFIRE/BYSTANDER: the defining feature - a bound antibody kills CD20-low or CD20-NEGATIVE cells hundreds of cell diameters away, so antigen-negative escape variants are not protected. Effector-cell-independent.

RESISTANCE - ANTI-CD20. (a) Antigenic loss: CD20-negative transformation in ~26% of rebiopsied relapses after R-chemo, partly epigenetic (promoter methylation, reversible by 5-azacytidine); also MS4A1 mutations/splice variants, and loss via transformation to plasmablastic phenotype. (b) Antigenic modulation: rapid internalisation of the antibody:CD20 complex (the dominant loss route), plus FcgammaR-dependent trogocytosis/shaving by monocytes - both leave a live cell with less antigen. (c) Complement exhaustion: C2 and C1q consumption during infusion makes CDC self-limiting and dose-saturable; high tumour burden depletes complement faster. (d) Complement regulators CD46/CD55/CD59 overexpression raises the per-cell lysis threshold. (e) Effector-cell exhaustion/saturation of FcgammaRIIIa; low-affinity FCGR3A-158F genotype. (f) Intrinsic apoptotic resistance: BCL2 overexpression, NF-kB activation.

RESISTANCE - ALKYLATORS/PLATINUM (cyclophosphamide, bendamustine, cisplatin, carboplatin). Elevated glutathione and glutathione-S-transferase conjugation; MGMT/alkyltransferase (bypassed by bendamustine, which relies on BER); enhanced nucleotide excision repair (ERCC1) and Fanconi/HR crosslink repair; ALDH1 overexpression detoxifying aldophosphamide; TP53 mutation blocking damage-to-apoptosis coupling (a very common DLBCL escape); reduced platinum uptake via CTR1 downregulation and increased efflux via ATP7A/ATP7B.

RESISTANCE - VINCRISTINE, DOXORUBICIN, MMAE ADCs. Shared route: ABCB1/MDR1 P-glycoprotein efflux (vincristine, doxorubicin and free MMAE are all substrates; MMAE efflux is a documented ADC-resistance route, whereas PBD dimers are only moderately MDR-susceptible). Also tubulin isotype switching and beta-tubulin mutations for vincristine; topoisomerase IIalpha downregulation/mutation and ABCG2 for doxorubicin; for ADCs specifically, target antigen downregulation (CD30, CD79b, CD19), impaired internalisation/endosomal trafficking, and defective lysosomal proteolysis or the lysosomal transporter SLC46A3 blocking payload release.

RESISTANCE - ANTIMETABOLITES. Methotrexate: reduced folate carrier (SLC19A1) loss impairing uptake, DHFR amplification or mutation, and loss of folylpolyglutamate synthetase so the drug is not retained. Cytarabine: loss of deoxycytidine kinase (activation step), upregulation of cytidine deaminase and 5'-nucleotidase (inactivation), expanded dCTP pools competing with ara-CTP, and reduced hENT1 transport. All of these are cell-intrinsic and heritable, so they can be modelled as inherited scalar sensitivity traits.
modellable: BINARY CYCLE-SPECIFICITY FLAG (the distinction the user asked to model). 'Kills only cycling/dividing cells': vincristine (M only), MMAE payloads = polatuzumab vedotin + brentuximab vedotin (M only), methotrexate (S only), cytarabine (S only). 'Kills any cell regardless of phase': rituximab, obinutuzumab, prednisone, Y-90 ibritumomab crossfire, PBD payload = loncastuximab tesirine. 'Intermediate - damage in any phase, death realised at replication': cyclophosphamide, bendamustine, doxorubicin, cisplatin/carboplatin. Implement the intermediate class as a per-cell persistent damage counter written in any phase and evaluated at S/M entry, not as an instantaneous kill probability.

Anti-CD20 kill probability as a saturating function of receptor count. Use CD20 molecules/cell drawn from a distribution: normal B ~94,000; CLL ~65,000; MCL ~123,000; SLVL ~167,000; HCL ~312,000 (Ginaldi 1998). CDC lysis probability rises approximately LINEARLY with CD20 density (r>=0.9), so a linear-then-saturating map is empirically justified; multiply by a per-cell CD55/CD59 protection factor that can reduce lysis up to 5-6 fold.

Complement as a DEPLETABLE SHARED RESOURCE. Model a global complement pool (C2/C1q) consumed proportionally to the number of opsonised cells lysed; when depleted, CDC halts even though antibody remains bound. This produces the observed nonlinearity where high tumour burden self-protects and re-dosing without a recovery interval gives no additional CDC (Kennedy 2004).

Effector-cell compartment for ADCC/ADCP. NK cells and macrophages as agents with a finite engagement rate and refractory period; per-effector kill efficiency scaled by FcgammaRIIIa genotype (V/V ~1.0, F carrier ~0.5-0.7, calibrated to 90% vs 51% 12-month response). Obinutuzumab multiplies effector kill rate by ~10-35x relative to rituximab, and simultaneously reduces the CDC term.

Obinutuzumab as a three-term antibody: CDC_term x ~0.2-0.5, ADCC/ADCP_term x 10-35, plus a NEW effector-independent direct-death term (caspase-independent, F(ab')2-driven) absent from rituximab. This structure predicts the clinical dissociation: superior where effectors and direct death dominate (CLL11 HR 0.39) and non-superior where combined with strong chemo in DLBCL (GOYA HR 0.92).

CD20 antigen dynamics per cell. Two loss processes with different rates: (i) fast antigenic modulation/internalisation of the antibody:CD20 complex, dominant, minutes-to-hours, leaves a surviving cell with reduced CD20; (ii) FcgammaR-dependent trogocytosis/shaving on macrophage contact, slower and competing with phagocytosis. Add slow epigenetic silencing producing a heritable CD20-negative subclone; calibrate emergence so ~26% of relapses are CD20-negative, and make silencing reversible (demethylation restores mRNA in ~3 days).

MMAE bystander module. On ADC-mediated payload release, deposit a diffusible MMAE quantum into the local lattice: intracellular concentration ~500 nM in the source cell, retention half-life 15-20 h, membrane-permeable, killing antigen-negative neighbours. Contrast with a non-permeable payload (MMAF) which gives zero bystander kill - a clean control condition. Bystander radius should be a fitted diffusion length, not zero.

PBD/loncastuximab module. Payload potency mean GI50 ~150 pM (about 3 orders of magnitude more potent than typical chemo). DNA interstrand crosslinks persist >36 h with minimal helix distortion; represent as a long-lived, poorly repairable lesion whose repair rate is set by ERCC1/HR status (make ERCC1-low or HR-deficient cells hypersensitive). Poor MDR1 substrate, so exempt it from the P-gp efflux term that reduces MMAE, vincristine and doxorubicin.

Radioimmunotherapy crossfire kernel. Y-90 pure beta emitter, tissue range up to ~5 mm which is roughly 200-300 cell diameters, physical half-life ~2.5-2.7 days. Implement as a spatially convolved dose field around each bound antibody, decaying exponentially in time, that kills CD20-low and CD20-negative cells within the kernel. This is the only agent in the panel for which antigen-negative escape confers no local protection.

Exposure-window versus peak-concentration semantics. For vincristine and MMAE ADCs, kill probability = P(cell enters M during the effective drug window), so it is governed by cell-cycle length distribution and the drug's residence time (MMAE ~15-20 h). For cytarabine and methotrexate, kill = integral of exposure over time spent in S. For rituximab, obinutuzumab, prednisone and Y-90, kill depends on occupancy/dose, independent of phase. Encode these as three different pharmacodynamic functional forms rather than one Hill curve.

Prednisone as a cycle-independent transcriptional killer acting on G0 cells over hours to ~48 h. In an untreated-lymphoma sim with a large quiescent fraction, prednisone (and anti-CD20, and Y-90) should be the agents that debulk the resting compartment, while vincristine and MMAE ADCs only prune the proliferating fraction. Testing whether that division reproduces observed CHOP kinetics is a good validation target.

Heritable resistance traits as per-cell scalars, mutating at division: P-gp/ABCB1 level (scales vincristine, doxorubicin, MMAE efflux; not PBD), glutathione/GST and ERCC1 (alkylators, platinum), MGMT (classical alkylators but not bendamustine, giving the incomplete cross-resistance the model should reproduce), TP53 status (uncouples DNA damage from apoptosis for all DNA-damaging agents), deoxycytidine kinase (cytarabine), reduced folate carrier and FPGS (methotrexate), CD20/CD79b/CD19/CD30 surface count (antibody and ADC targeting).

Bendamustine parameterised as partially non-cross-resistant with cyclophosphamide: same phase-non-specific crosslinking term, but a different repair-pathway dependency (base-excision repair rather than alkyltransferase) plus an added mitotic-catastrophe term on the next division. This makes bendamustine effective in a virtual population selected for classical-alkylator resistance, which is the observed clinical behaviour.
open_questions: The frequency of CD20 loss at relapse is poorly pinned down. The best single sourced figure here is 5/19 (26%) rebiopsied relapses (Hiraga 2009, n small, single centre, pre-modern era). Published estimates elsewhere range widely (roughly 10-60%) depending on whether flow, IHC or mRNA is used and whether partial downregulation counts. Do not hard-code a single rate; run it as a swept parameter.

Quantitative magnitude and half-life of trogocytosis-mediated CD20 loss in patients (percent antigen removed per macrophage encounter, recovery time constant) was not retrievable from abstracts. Dahal 2018 establishes that internalisation dominates over shaving but does not supply rates. This is a genuine gap for a spatial model with macrophage agents.

Whether PBD-dimer ADCs truly kill non-dividing/quiescent cells was NOT directly demonstrated in the sources retrieved. The inference rests on the lesion being a persistent, NER-evading DNA crosslink formed independently of phase. A modeller should treat 'PBD kills G0 cells' as a hypothesis to test rather than an established parameter.

Doxorubicin's cycle classification is inconsistent across sources (phase-non-specific vs S/G2-M-preferential vs described as an M-phase blocker). Because topoisomerase IIalpha expression is itself cycle-regulated, the effective phase dependence may be an emergent property rather than a fixed drug property. Worth modelling both ways.

No source was found giving absolute CD79b, CD19 or CD30 copy numbers per cell, which are needed to parameterise ADC payload delivery the way CD20 density parameterises CDC. Polson 2009 identifies the targets but the abstract does not carry copy numbers.

FcgammaR genotype effects are contested: Cartron 2002 found a strong effect in single-agent rituximab in follicular lymphoma (n=49), but Strefford 2021 (Blood Advances, GALLIUM/GOYA analysis) reported NO association between FcgammaR genotype and response when antibody is given with chemotherapy. Effector-genotype effects may be washed out by chemotherapy, which is itself a modellable interaction.

Free-MMAE concentrations achieved in the tumour interstitium (as opposed to intracellularly) and the effective bystander diffusion radius in tissue were not quantified in the retrieved sources - only that bystander killing occurs. The radius is therefore a fitted, not measured, parameter.
Single-cell mechanisms of anti-CD20 anti.caveats:
"1) 'Cell-cycle-specific vs not' is a continuum, not a dichotomy, and the retrieved literature is not always careful about it. Only vincristine, the auristatin (MMAE) payloads, methotrexate and cytarabine are genuinely phase-restricted. Alkylators, anthracyclines and platinum inflict damage in ANY phase including G0 but frequently require replication to convert that damage into death - so a naive 'kills any cell' flag will over-kill the quiescent compartment. Recommend a three-state model (phase-restricted / phase-agnostic-lethal / damage-now-die-on-division).

2) Effector-dependence evidence for anti-CD20 is strongest in mouse (Uchida 2004, complement dispensable, monocytes essential) and inferential in humans (Cartron 2002 FCGR3A, n=49, and contradicted by Strefford 2021 in the chemo-combination setting). The relative CDC:ADCC:ADCP weighting in human lymph node tissue is genuinely unresolved; treat the three arms as separately weighted terms and fit rather than assume.

3) In vitro potency does not linearly predict clinical benefit. Obinutuzumab is 10-35x more potent than rituximab in cellular assays yet gave HR 0.39 in CLL and HR 0.92 (non-significant) in first-line DLBCL. Any simulation that outputs 'more potent antibody -> better outcome' monotonically is contradicted by GOYA and should be checked against it.

4) Antigen density values (Ginaldi 1998) are from chronic B-cell leukaemias by calibrated-bead flow, measured in 1998; DLBCL and follicular lymphoma tissue values are not covered by that source, and formalin-fixed IHC scoring is not interconvertible with molecules/cell.

5) The doxorubicin cycle-specificity entry and the classification of cyclophosphamide/vincristine/cytarabine/methotrexate rest partly on standard pharmacology rather than a single retrievable primary source; they are flagged medium/low confidence accordingly. Platinum salvage and ADC drug-to-antibody ratios (pola ~3.5, brentuximab ~4, loncastuximab ~2.3) are stated from background knowledge and were not independently sourced in this session - verify before publishing.

6) All ADC and antibody effects assume the drug physically reaches the cell. Antibody and ADC penetration into bulky nodal tissue is spatially limited (binding-site barrier), so in a spatial model antibodies and ADCs should have a much shorter effective penetration depth than small-molecule chemotherapy - whereas Y-90 crossfire deliberately bypasses this. This spatial asymmetry is probably more important to outcome than the cycle-specificity distinction in bulky disease.

7) Rituximab/obinutuzumab efficacy in the model will depend on immune effector agents that chemotherapy itself depletes (bendamustine is markedly and durably CD4-depleting; CHOP is myelosuppressive). Chemo-immunotherapy should therefore not be modelled as two independent kill terms multiplied together."

Growth kinetics, cell turnover and physi.domain: Growth kinetics, cell turnover and physical/spatial structure of lymphoma (B-cell NHL: follicular G1-2 and G3, DLBCL, mantle cell, Burkitt) — quantitative parameters for a cell-level / agent-based simulation.

key_facts.fact: Flow-cytometric Ki67 across 476 mature B-cell neoplasms separates subtypes cleanly. Note flow reads far LOWER than immunohistochemistry on the same entity; do not mix the two scales in one model.
key_facts.source: Mao X et al. 2023, Front Oncol 13:1108837 (PMID 36890821, PMC9986934)

key_facts.fact: Immunohistochemical Ki-67/MIB-1 indices — the scale used in almost all pathology reports and the one to calibrate a simulation against.
key_facts.numbers: FL grade 1-2 intrafollicular PI: median 23.3%, range 0.6-63.2% (n=129, quantitative image analysis). All-grade FL median 17.0% (n=82), significantly lower in G1-2 than G3a. DLBCL median 70%, range 25-100% (n=53). Burkitt MIB-1 mean 98.1% vs MYC-rearranged DLBCL 66.3% (p<0.0001)
key_facts.source: Kedmi M 2014 Br J Haematol (PMID 24303881); Kawaguchi 2018 Int J Clin Exp Pathol (PMID 31949713); Asker 2021 Clin Lab (PMID 34258959); Nakamura N 2002 Mod Pathol (PMID 12118116)

key_facts.fact: Mantle cell lymphoma has a validated, trial-derived Ki-67 threshold; it is the single strongest biological prognostic variable and the best-standardised proliferation cutpoint in any lymphoma.
key_facts.numbers: Ki-67 dichotomised at 30% (assessed in 508/832 patients, European MCL Network Younger + Elderly trials). An independent series found 20% also discriminant (n=56); 20%-cutoff mean survival 69.8 vs 47.9 months
key_facts.source: Hoster E 2016 J Clin Oncol (PMID 26926679); Jeong 2016 Blood Res (PMID 27382558)

key_facts.fact: The high-grade/low-grade apoptotic index result the brief asked for is real and reproducible: high-grade NHL has ~3-4x the histological apoptotic index of low-grade, and AI rises in step with proliferation.
key_facts.numbers: AI low-grade 0.59±0.44% vs high-grade 1.96±1.92%, p<0.001 (n=85). Independent FNA series: AI threshold 1.5-2.5% separates low/intermediate from higher grade (n=96, inter-observer median r=0.93)
key_facts.source: Soini Y 1999 APMIS 107:1043 (PMID 10598877); Symmans WF 2000 Acta Cytol (PMID 10740606)

key_facts.fact: Reactive germinal centres out-proliferate AND out-die low-grade lymphoma. The reactive GC is the correct kinetic baseline for a FL model, not resting lymphocyte tissue.
key_facts.numbers: In-situ end-labelling (apoptosis): reactive GC 5.0-10.0%; low-grade NHL 1.0-3.7%; high-grade NHL 4.7-13.5%. Histone-mRNA proliferation index: reactive GC 30%; low-grade 5.2-13.5%; high-grade 12.1-50.5%
key_facts.source: Kiberu SW 1996 Clin Mol Pathol 49:M268 (PMID 16696087)

key_facts.fact: Leoncini's foundational series established that apoptotic and proliferative indices are positively coupled across NHL, and that AI — not grade or BCL2 — was the only independent predictor of lethality.
key_facts.numbers: n=50 NHL; AI vs Ki-67, PC10 and mitotic index all p<0.01; AI vs overall lethality p<0.05 on multivariate; BCL2 vs survival p=0.08 (NS). Companion: turnover index TI = mitotic index + apoptotic index; ~1/3 of high-grade lymphomas fall in the low-turnover cluster (n=170)
key_facts.source: Leoncini L 1993 Am J Pathol 142:755 (PMID 7681257, PMC1886795); Spina D 1995 J Pathol (PMID 8568587)

key_facts.fact: Cell loss factor: malignant lymphoma sits at the extreme high-turnover end of all human tumours — ~93% of produced cells are lost. This is the number the brief asked to compute; CLF = 1 - Tpot/Td.
key_facts.numbers: Pooled 389 pulmonary metastases, 5 histologies. Malignant lymphoma: volume doubling time 29 d, labelling index 29%, growth fraction 90%, cell loss factor 93%. Implied Tpot = 29 x 0.07 ≈ 2 days. Comparators: adenocarcinoma CLF 71%, squamous 89%, sarcoma 68%
key_facts.source: Tubiana M 1989 Acta Oncol 28:113-21 (PMID 2650719)

key_facts.fact: Burkitt lymphoma is the fastest-doubling human tumour; growth fraction approaches unity, so almost the entire population is cycling. Classic tritiated-thymidine kinetics on African biopsies.
key_facts.numbers: Clinical doubling time ~24-26 h (widely cited as 24 h). Growth fraction ≈100% (MIB-1 98.1%). Contrast: pooled 'malignant lymphoma' clinical VDT 29 d; a primary hepatic T-cell lymphoma VDT measured at 9.6 d
key_facts.source: Iversen OH 1974 Eur J Cancer (PMID 4479620); Kearns DB 1986 Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol (PMID 3818193); Taketomi 1996 Hepatogastroenterology (PMID 8799410)

key_facts.fact: Lymphoma is NOT a set of isolated spatial masses. Measurable tumour cells circulate at diagnosis in a substantial minority of FL and a large majority of MCL.
key_facts.numbers: FL: circulating lymphoma cells by PB flow at diagnosis in 24/147 (16%); CL+ associated with more extranodal involvement (83% vs 44%, p<0.01). MCL: circulating cells by morphology 27/35 (77%), median 20% of circulating WBC, range 5-90%; PB flow-positive in 26% of 185 samples
key_facts.source: Annunzio K 2024 Hematol Oncol (PMID 38726682); Cohen PL 1998 Br J Haematol (PMID 9609526); Gu J 2004 Mod Pathol (PMID 15001994)

key_facts.fact: t(14;18)-bearing B cells circulate in healthy people, so a background 'pre-lymphoma' recirculating pool exists before any tumour. Critical for seeding assumptions in an FL model.
key_facts.numbers: 23% of 481 normal individuals PCR-positive for BCL2/IgH; ~3% of those at >1 per 10^4 cells. Seveso cohort: 34.7% positive (50/144), 4.2 (95%CI 2.9-6.2) to 12.5 (7.4-21.1) translocations per 10^6 lymphocytes, rising with dioxin exposure
key_facts.source: Summers KE 2001 J Clin Oncol (PMID 11208834); Baccarelli A 2006 Carcinogenesis (PMID 16543249); Roulland S 2004 Cancer Res (PMID 15026372)

key_facts.fact: Direct clonal-genealogy evidence: individual FL follicles are polyclonally founded by many immigrant tumour cells, and migration occurs between follicles within a node and between separate nodes.
key_facts.numbers: Single-cell micromanipulation of 3 distinct follicles in each of 3 FL cases; IgVH/IgVL genealogical trees show each follicle founded by many tumour cells. NGS of clonal IGH in pure in-situ follicular neoplasia across multiple nodes documented inter-follicular AND inter-nodal migration
key_facts.source: Oeschger S 2002 Blood 99:2192 (PMID 11877297); Kosmidis P 2017 PLoS One (PMID 28640838)

key_facts.fact: Neoplastic follicle size is measurable but site-dependent and the sign flips between gut and node — do not assume neoplastic follicles are always larger.
key_facts.numbers: Primary intestinal FL vs reactive hyperplasia (WSI, 17 vs 17): median follicle diameter 756.9 um (576.8-929.9) vs 479.7 um (337.1-607.2), p=0.001; follicle density 0.5/mm2 (0.3-0.7) vs 0.2/mm2 (0.1-0.3), p=0.004. In LYMPH NODES the opposite was found: reactive follicle areas > FL follicle areas; mantle zone up to 65.5% of total reactive follicle area and usually absent in FL
key_facts.source: Li M 2020 Diagn Pathol 15:82 (PMID 32635930, PMC7341590); Crocker J 1983 J Clin Pathol (PMID 6350370)

key_facts.fact: Germinal-centre hypoxia is physiological and cell-intrinsic, not a diffusion-limited necrotic core. GC light zones are hypoxic in a normal immunised node with no tumour present.
key_facts.numbers: GC peak size ~10,000 B cells. Mouse GC light zones hypoxic by molecular markers; 1% O2 in vitro reproduces the phenotype; breathing 60% O2 in vivo reduced GC B cells, Tfh and plasmacytes and cut antigen-specific IgG1. Chicken spleen GC mean diameter 102-108 um (range 50-175 um)
key_facts.source: Cho SH 2016 Nature 537:234 (PMID 27501247); Abbott RK 2016 J Immunol (PMID 27798169); Victora & Nussenzweig 2010 Cell; Romppanen 1981 APMIS-C (PMID 7315360)

key_facts.fact: In vivo hypoxia imaging says lymphoma is measurably LESS hypoxic than a matched solid tumour, though HIF-1a is still widely expressed. Argues against modelling a classic necrotic hypoxic core.
key_facts.numbers: 18F-FMISO PET: visually positive in 54% of primary CNS lymphoma (n=13) vs 89% of glioblastoma (n=62); tumour-to-normal ratio 1.80±0.59 vs 2.75±0.84, p<0.001. Yet HIF-1a and VEGF-A IHC-positive in 88.2% of 34 de novo DLBCL. Microvessel density significantly higher in high- vs low-grade NHL (p=0.0015)
key_facts.source: Uchinomura S 2022 Nucl Med Commun (PMID 34864812); Pangarsa EA 2022 Mol Clin Oncol (PMID 35949890); Arias V 2000 Leuk Lymphoma (PMID 11426617)

key_facts.fact: Bone marrow involvement frequency at diagnosis differs ~4-fold across subtypes; MCL is near-universal, DLBCL is the outlier low. Detection method changes the number substantially.
key_facts.numbers: DLBCL/aggressive NHL: 24% by combined BMB+PET reference standard (BMB alone 9%, PET alone 20%; n=930, prospective PETAL/OPTIMAL>60). FL: 43% by BM histology + flow combined (n=139 specimens, 91 patients); trephine biopsy has lower false-negative rate (8%) than flow (23%). MCL: 91% by trephine biopsy (39/43), 83% by aspirate (33/40)
key_facts.source: Kaddu-Mulindwa D 2021 Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging (PMID 33928400, PMC8440256); Schmidt B 2006 Leuk Lymphoma (PMID 17064998); Cohen PL 1998 Br J Haematol (PMID 9609526)

mechanisms: Proliferation and apoptosis are POSITIVELY coupled in NHL, not inversely. High-grade tumours both divide faster and die faster; net growth is the small difference between two large fluxes. A simulation that models growth as birth-minus-a-small-constant-death will get the wrong sensitivity to therapy. Leoncini 1993 (PMID 7681257) and Spina 1995 (PMID 8568587) formalise this as the 'turnover index' TI = mitotic index + apoptotic index.

Cell loss dominates. With cell loss factor ~93% for malignant lymphoma (Tubiana 1989), ~14 of every 15 cells produced never contribute to the tumour mass. Net doubling time (29 d) is an order of magnitude longer than potential doubling time (~2 d). Small perturbations in the loss fraction produce enormous changes in net growth — this is the single most important nonlinearity to get right.

BCL2 in FL blocks apoptosis rather than driving proliferation. FL grade 1-2 has BOTH a lower proliferative index and a lower apoptotic index than a reactive germinal centre (Kiberu 1996): it is an accumulation disease, not a proliferation disease. Model FL as reduced death on a near-normal GC proliferation program; model DLBCL/Burkitt as amplified proliferation with amplified death.

Follicular lymphoma is architecturally a caricature of the germinal centre and remains microenvironment-dependent. Tumour cells keep migrating out and re-seeding new follicles, yet only expand once inside a follicular niche with FDCs and Tfh (Oeschger 2002). The correct spatial abstraction is 'many small niches connected by a well-mixed circulating compartment', not 'one expanding solid sphere'.

Lymphocyte recirculation makes the lymphoma a single connected system. Naive lymphocytes enter nodes via HEVs, dwell hours, and leave via efferent lymph. Measured mouse peripheral-LN transit: naive CD4+ 12.2 h, CD8+ 21.2 h (Mandl 2012 PNAS, PMID 23071319); rat thoracic-duct lymphocytes average ~10 h residence in LN/Peyer's patch and ~2.5 h in spleen, with only ~5% of blood lymphocytes at any instant en route to a secondary lymphoid organ (Ganusov 2014 PLoS Comput Biol, PMID 24830705). Antigen-stimulated node enlargement in that model comes largely from reduced exit, not increased entry — a directly transplantable rule.

The lymph node is already a perfused, sinusoid-rich organ before the tumour arrives; the tumour does not have to build a vasculature from scratch the way a carcinoma in stroma does. Microvessel density still rises with grade (Arias 2000), and HIF-1a/VEGF-A are expressed (Pangarsa 2022), but FMISO PET shows substantially less hypoxia than glioblastoma. Meanwhile GC light zones are constitutively hypoxic in normal nodes (Cho 2016 Nature) — so any hypoxia signal you see in an FL follicle may be inherited germinal-centre physiology, not a diffusion-limited core.

Histological apoptotic index massively understates the death RATE, because apoptotic bodies are visible only for roughly 1-3 hours before phagocytosis by tingible-body macrophages. An AI of 2% therefore corresponds to a per-day death fraction on the order of 15-50%, not 2%. This correction is the bridge between the AI literature and the cell-loss-factor literature and must be applied explicitly.

Grading thresholds are proliferation thresholds in disguise. FL grading counts centroblasts per HPF; MCL prognosis pivots on Ki-67 30%; BL vs DLBCL is separated at ~98% Ki-67-positive. A cell-level model with an explicit cycling fraction can reproduce all three classification boundaries from one underlying parameter.
modellable: Cycling fraction (growth fraction) by subtype, IHC scale, as agent state probability: FL G1-2 0.17-0.23; FL G3 0.30-0.40; DLBCL 0.70 (range 0.25-1.00); MCL classical 0.10-0.30 with 0.30 as the clinically validated dichotomy; MCL blastoid >0.40; Burkitt 0.95-1.00.
Cycling fraction on the FLOW-cytometry scale if calibrating against flow data instead (do not mix): FL G1-2 0.020; FL G3 0.196; DLBCL 0.548; MCL classical 0.105; MCL blastoid 0.265; Burkitt 0.866.

Per-timestep apoptosis probability, derived: histological AI 0.006 (low grade) to 0.020 (high grade), divided by an apoptotic-body visibility window of ~2 h, gives instantaneous death rates of roughly 0.07/h (low grade) to 0.24/h (high grade) of the counted population — i.e. per-day loss fractions of order 0.15 and 0.45. Treat the visibility window as a tunable calibration parameter in [1 h, 3 h].

Cell loss factor as a direct model constraint: CLF = 1 - Tpot/Td. For nodal lymphoma set CLF = 0.93, Td = 29 d, Tpot = 2 d, growth fraction 0.90, labelling index 0.29. Reproduce these five numbers simultaneously as a validation test.

Cell cycle duration: use ~2 days as the mean human tumour cell-cycle time (Tubiana 1989) for FL/DLBCL/MCL. For Burkitt, the ~24-26 h clinical doubling with growth fraction ~1.0 and CLF near zero forces a cell cycle of ~24 h — model Burkitt as a near-lossless exponential.

Volume doubling time targets: Burkitt 1 day; pooled malignant lymphoma 29 days; an aggressive T-cell lymphoma case measured at 9.6 days; untreated FL should be modelled as net-flat-to-slowly-growing over months (median survival 8-10 y untreated), i.e. birth and death fluxes within a few percent of each other.

Follicle geometry for a spatial FL model: neoplastic follicle diameter median 757 um (range 577-930 um); reactive follicle 480 um (337-607 um); follicle number density 0.5/mm2 (neoplastic) vs 0.2/mm2 (reactive) in 2D section. Normal GC peak content ~10,000 B cells. Mantle zone contributes up to 65.5% of reactive follicle area and is typically absent in FL. Flag: in lymph node (as opposed to gut) reactive follicles were measured as LARGER than FL follicles.

Cell packing density in lymphoid tissue (DERIVED, not directly sourced): small lymphocyte diameter 6-8 um, ~70% volume packing fraction gives ~1.0-1.5 x 10^6 cells/mm3 = ~1-1.5 x 10^9 cells/cm3. A 2 cm involved node (~4 cm3) therefore holds ~4-6 x 10^9 cells; a patient with 1 kg tumour burden holds ~1 x 10^12 cells. Treat these as order-of-magnitude only.

Trafficking rule set: give every tumour agent an exit hazard from its follicle/node compartment with mean residence 10-20 h, a blood transit compartment, and a re-entry probability into any node (not just the source node). Only ~5% of blood lymphocytes per pass are routed to a secondary lymphoid organ; the rest recycle through lung/liver with sub-minute residence. Antigen/inflammation-driven node enlargement is implemented as reduced exit hazard, not increased entry.

Circulating tumour burden initialisation: FL 16% of patients have detectable circulating clone at diagnosis; MCL 77% (median 20% of circulating WBC, range 5-90%). Healthy background t(14;18)+ pool: 23-35% of people positive at 4-13 clones per 10^6 lymphocytes — a non-zero floor for any FL initiation model.

Bone marrow as a compartment with subtype-specific seeding probability at diagnosis: DLBCL 0.24; FL 0.43 (with >90% of FL marrow disease showing a paratrabecular pattern, i.e. a stromal-niche-restricted geometry, not diffuse fill); MCL 0.91. Add a 25% marrow/node histological discordance rate (Arber 2005, PMID 16327427) if modelling grade heterogeneity across sites.

Oxygen module (if included): do NOT impose a necrotic core by radius. Instead make hypoxia niche-linked — assign low pO2 to light-zone-like follicular regions constitutively (physiological GC hypoxia), scale microvessel density up with grade, and calibrate the whole-tumour hypoxic fraction against an FMISO tumour-to-normal ratio of ~1.8 (lymphoma) versus ~2.75 (glioblastoma), with 54% vs 89% of lesions scoring positive.

Validation targets a finished model should reproduce without further tuning: (1) AI/proliferation positive correlation across simulated grades; (2) high-grade AI ~3.3x low-grade AI; (3) reactive-GC apoptosis (5-10%) exceeding low-grade FL apoptosis (1-3.7%); (4) cell loss factor 0.93 at steady growth; (5) MCL survival separation at Ki-67 0.30.
open_questions: No modern, direct measurement of the apoptotic-body clearance time in human lymphoma tissue was found. Every conversion from histological apoptotic index to an actual death rate rests on an assumed 1-3 h visibility window. This is the largest single uncertainty in the whole cell-turnover chain and it is worth a dedicated literature dig or a sensitivity sweep.

The 93% cell loss factor comes from Tubiana's pooled series of PULMONARY METASTASES classified as 'malignant lymphoma', not from nodal NHL biopsies, and predates the modern WHO classification. Whether an indolent nodal FL has anything like a 93% cell loss factor is genuinely unknown; it may be much lower.

No reliable subtype-resolved volume doubling times for FL, DLBCL or MCL were found in the searchable literature. Only Burkitt (~24 h) and a pooled lymphoma figure (29 d) are citable. Modern serial-CT/PET volumetry in watch-and-wait FL cohorts would fill this gap and is likely to exist in radiology literature that these searches did not reach.

Lymph node cell packing density (cells/mm3) has no direct citation here. It is geometrically constrained to ~1-1.5 x 10^6 cells/mm3 but should be confirmed against a stereology paper before being used as a hard model constant.

Lymph node size at diagnosis was not pinned to a source. 'Bulky' is conventionally defined at a 7-10 cm largest diameter, and normal nodes are usually <10 mm short axis, but neither was verified in this pass.

Whether circulating FL cells actually re-seed and establish NEW nodal deposits, or merely circulate, is inferred from clonal genealogy (Oeschger, Kosmidis) rather than demonstrated by lineage tracing. The inference is strong but not direct. This matters: it decides whether the simulation needs a true seeding-and-establishment probability or only a mixing term.
Human lymph node transit times are extrapolated from mouse (Mandl 2012) and rat (Ganusov 2014). No human measurement was found. Scaling to human node volumes is unvalidated.

Whether lymphoma cells inside a neoplastic follicle experience the same physiological hypoxia as normal light-zone GC B cells is untested in human tissue — the Cho and Abbott hypoxia data are murine and non-neoplastic, while the human lymphoma hypoxia data (HIF-1a IHC, FMISO PET) are whole-lesion and cannot resolve follicles.
Growth kinetics, cell turnover and physi.caveats: Scale mismatch is the biggest trap here: flow-cytometric Ki67 and immunohistochemical Ki-67 differ by up to an order of magnitude on the same entity (FL grade 1-2 is 2.0% by flow, 17-23% by IHC). Pick one and stay on it. STRENGTH OF EVIDENCE — Well established (use directly): Ki-67 by subtype on both scales; the MCL 30% cutoff (prospective trial cohorts, n=508); the high-grade > low-grade apoptotic index result (multiple independent series, consistent direction and magnitude); bone marrow involvement rates; Burkitt's ~24 h doubling; the existence of circulating clonal cells in FL and MCL; healthy-donor t(14;18) carriage. Moderately supported (use with a sensitivity sweep): follicle diameters (single small studies, and the neoplastic-vs-reactive size ordering REVERSES between gut and lymph node — Li 2020 gut vs Crocker 1983 node); microvessel density by grade; the FMISO hypoxia comparison (n=13 lymphomas, and PCNSL is not a nodal lymphoma). Weak or extrapolated (flag in any write-up): the 93% cell loss factor (pooled pulmonary metastases, 1989, pre-WHO classification); all conversions from apoptotic index to per-day death rate (depend on an assumed apoptotic-body visibility window); lymph node cell packing density (geometric derivation, unsourced); lymphocyte transit times (rodent, extrapolated to human); germinal-centre hypoxia (murine, non-neoplastic). Also note the 1990s AI/turnover literature predates routine rituximab and uses the Kiel/Working Formulation, so 'high grade' there maps imperfectly onto WHO-HAEM5 entities; and the FL grading literature is itself unstable — Xue 2020 (n=433) found grade 3A behaves like grade 1-2, so treating grade as a clean proliferation ladder is defensible for G1-2 vs G3B but not for G3A. Finally, several counts differ by detection method rather than biology (FL marrow involvement is 43% by histology+flow but higher by PCR; DLBCL marrow is 9% by biopsy and 24% by biopsy+PET) — the simulation should model the biological quantity and apply a separate detection filter.

Targeted small molecules and immunomodul.domain: Targeted small molecules and immunomodulators in non-Hodgkin lymphoma (BTK inhibitors and degraders, BCL2 inhibition, EZH2 inhibition, PI3K-delta inhibitors, cereblon modulators, MALT1 inhibitors) — mechanism, cytotoxic-vs-cytostatic character, subtype dependence, response durability, and resistance, framed for agent-based / cell-level simulation.

key_facts.fact: At progression on covalent BTK inhibitors in ELEVATE-RR, emergent BTK mutations appeared in 66% of acalabrutinib-treated and 37% of ibrutinib-treated patients, C481S dominant; PLCG2 mutations were less common.
key_facts.numbers: BTK mut 31/47 (66%) acala vs 11/30 (37%) ibrutinib; median VAF 16.1% vs 15.6%; PLCG2 6% vs 20%; T474I n=9 (acala only); preexisting TP53 ~53% both arms; median follow-up 41 months
key_facts.source: Woyach JA et al. 2024, Blood. PMID 38754046, PMCID PMC11406168

key_facts.fact: BTK mutations are detectable long before clinical progression, and their prevalence depends heavily on prior treatment. Median lead time from first C481S detection to progressive disease was about 8.5 months.
key_facts.numbers: Over ~35 months without progression: BTK mut 3% treated-naive (n=238) vs 30% relapsed/refractory (n=150); at progression BTK mut 25% (TN) vs 49% (R/R); median C481S-to-PD 8.5 months (range 0–35.7)
key_facts.source: Woyach JA et al. 2023, Clin Cancer Res. PMID 37314786, PMCID PMC10425728

key_facts.fact: Ibrutinib-induced lymphocytosis is egress from nodal compartments, resolving within 8 months in most patients; a subgroup persists past 12 months. Persistent cells are quiescent, cannot be stimulated through the BCR, and are not clonally evolved.
key_facts.numbers: Resolution <8 months in majority; persistent subgroup >12 months; PFS not inferior in persistent-lymphocytosis group; persistent cells not addicted to a single survival pathway in vitro
key_facts.source: Woyach JA et al. 2014, Blood. PMID 24415539, PMCID PMC3962160

key_facts.fact: A population PK-PD model reproduces ibrutinib lymphocyte dynamics with two compartments (tissue, blood) and two drug effects — stimulated redistribution and death. Hyperlymphocytosis patients had higher tissue:blood ratio and weaker death effect.
key_facts.numbers: 94 patients, 658 ALC and 1501 PK observations; progressors had ~2-fold lower baseline tissue lymphocytes and ~3-fold lower blood lymphocytes
key_facts.source: Gallais F et al. 2021, Clin Pharmacol Ther. PMID 33539551

key_facts.fact: Ibrutinib reduces chemokine-evoked migration speed and directionality, blocks fibronectin polarisation and immunological-synapse assembly. The CCR7 (node entry) to S1PR1 (node exit) expression ratio predicted the magnitude of treatment-induced lymphocytosis.
key_facts.numbers: Migration to CCL19, CXCL12 and CXCL13 reduced in CLL cells and, marginally, in T cells; 6-month on-therapy monitoring cohort
key_facts.source: Rey-Barroso J et al. 2024, Haematologica. PMID 37381758

key_facts.fact: Pirtobrutinib (non-covalent, C481-independent) beat ibrutinib head-to-head in BTKi-naive CLL, but is markedly weaker after covalent BTKi failure — and weaker again in real-world mantle cell lymphoma than in the BRUIN trial.
key_facts.numbers: BRUIN CLL-313/314: ORR 87.0% vs 78.5% ibrutinib, PFS HR 0.57 (n=662). BRUIN CLL-321 post-cBTKi: ORR 62%, median PFS 20 months. Real-world MCL post-cBTKi: ORR 34%, CR 21%, median PFS 5.3 months, mOS 13 months (n=153)
key_facts.source: Woyach JA et al. 2026, J Clin Oncol PMID 41353787; Molica S & Allsup D 2025, Cancers PMID 41008818; Phillips T et al. 2026 preprint (multicentre retrospective, n=213)

key_facts.fact: BTK A428D confers pan-resistance to covalent inhibitors, non-covalent inhibitors and degraders by clashing with the ATP adenine ring — but carries a competitive fitness disadvantage off-drug. Venetoclax co-treatment suppressed its expansion.
key_facts.numbers: Recurrent expansion of preexisting A428D at relapse in phase I trials of zelebrudomide and bexobrutideg; crystal structure resolved; L528W is the other kinase-dead-type escape
key_facts.source: Sievers Q et al. 2026, Cancer Discovery. PMID 42484277

key_facts.fact: BTK degraders remove both kinase and scaffold function and produce deep responses after inhibitor failure, including in patients previously exposed to covalent BTKi, BCL2i and other degraders.
key_facts.numbers: BGB-16673: ORR 94.4%, n=67, median follow-up 19.8 months, RP2D 200 mg QD. Bexobrutideg/NX-5948: ORR 83.3% at 600 mg RP2D, n=42, median time to first response 1.9 months. Birletinib (LYN/BTK): ORR 84%, n=42
key_facts.source: Sharma P, Jiang H, Liu D 2026, J Hematol Oncol. PMID 42252468, PMCID PMC13242664 (ASH 2025 summary)

key_facts.fact: Venetoclax monotherapy activity in NHL is strongly subtype-dependent and generally lower than in CLL, with the highest intrinsic sensitivity in mantle cell lymphoma and Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia rather than in t(14;18) follicular lymphoma.
key_facts.numbers: Phase I (n=106): ORR MCL 75% (n=28), FL 38% (n=29), DLBCL 18% (n=34); median PFS MCL 14, FL 11, DLBCL 1 month. Long-term median DOR: FL 26.6, MCL 15.7, MZL 20.1, WM 25.3 months
key_facts.source: Davids MS et al. 2017, J Clin Oncol PMID 28095146; Davids MS et al. 2021, Clin Cancer Res PMID 34083230

key_facts.fact: Despite t(14;18) in most follicular lymphoma, venetoclax-rituximab underperformed chemoimmunotherapy in relapsed FL, and adding venetoclax to bendamustine-rituximab added toxicity without efficacy (CONTRALTO).
key_facts.numbers: Ven-R (n=52): ORR 35%, CR 17%, 18-month PFS 27%. Ven-BR (n=51): ORR 84%, CR 75%, 18-mo PFS 62%. BR (n=51): ORR 84%, CR 69%, 18-mo PFS 59%. Grade 3/4 neutropenia 59% vs 28%
key_facts.source: Zinzani PL et al., CONTRALTO, summarised with numbers in Lew TE & Seymour JF 2022, J Hematol Oncol. PMID 35659041, PMCID PMC9164485

key_facts.fact: Venetoclax response is set by apoptotic priming, not BCL2 level. In t(14;18) FL cells sensitivity tracks the BCL2:BIM ratio; roughly one-third of aggressive B-NHL carry BAX, BAK, BIM or BID defects.
key_facts.numbers: ~33% of primary aggressive B-NHL have pro-apoptotic effector defects on BH3 profiling; FL resistance emerges via increased p-ERK1/2 and p-BIM(S69), falling total BIM, and eventual near-total BIM loss
key_facts.source: Bodo J et al. 2016, Oncotarget PMID 27661108; BH3-profiling figure cited in Lew TE & Seymour JF 2022, J Hematol Oncol PMID 35659041

key_facts.fact: Tazemetostat (SAM-competitive EZH2 inhibitor) doubles response rate in EZH2-mutant versus wild-type relapsed FL, but PFS differs much less — the mutation predicts response depth more than durability.
key_facts.numbers: EZH2-mut (n=45): ORR 69%, median PFS 13.8 months, median DOR 10.9 months. EZH2-WT (n=54): ORR 35%, median PFS 11.1 months, median DOR 13.0 months. EZH2 activating mutations in ~20% of FL. Grade 3+ related AEs <=3% each
key_facts.source: Morschhauser F et al. 2020, Lancet Oncol. PMID 33035457, PMCID PMC8427481

key_facts.fact: Lenalidomide plus rituximab (R-squared) roughly triples PFS over rituximab alone in relapsed indolent NHL, with an overall survival benefit at long follow-up.
key_facts.numbers: Median PFS 39.4 vs 14.1 months, HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.34–0.62), n=358. At median 65.9 months: PFS HR 0.50 (0.38–0.66), OS HR 0.59 (0.37–0.95). Grade 3/4 neutropenia 50% vs 13%
key_facts.source: Leonard JP et al. 2019, J Clin Oncol PMID 30897038; Leonard JP et al. 2026, J Clin Oncol PMID 41990300 (5-year AUGMENT)

key_facts.fact: Lenalidomide's activity in follicular lymphoma is largely indirect. It reactivates exhausted T and NK cells, enhances rituximab-driven ADCC and lytic NK immune synapses via a cereblon-dependent mechanism, and raises circulating T/NK counts.
key_facts.numbers: Ex vivo FL patient T and NK cells; ADCC improved in both sensitive and chemo-resistant FL cells; R-squared increased circulating T and NK counts in a phase III cohort where R-chemotherapy reduced them
key_facts.source: Chiu H et al. 2019, Br J Haematol. PMID 30767211, PMCID PMC6594227

key_facts.fact: All four PI3K-delta-targeting agents lost NHL indications. Randomized safety data showed excess serious and fatal adverse events with idelalisib, and no overall-survival advantage for the class.
key_facts.numbers: Idelalisib pooled RR for serious AEs 1.86 (95% CI 1.63–2.11), fatal AEs 3.30 (1.56–7.00), death 1.35 (0.85–2.12) by 2016; withdrawn 2022 after $842M cumulative sales. Umbralisib fully withdrawn; ODAC voted against duvelisib Sept 2022. Umbralisib ORR had been 47.1% (n=208)
key_facts.source: Banerjee T, Kim MS, Haslam A, Prasad V 2023, JAMA Intern Med PMID 36939665; Fowler NH et al. 2021 J Clin Oncol PMID 33683917; FDA ODAC April 2022 / Sept 2022 (via AJMC and OncLive reporting)

mechanisms: BTK inhibitors, covalent (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib): irreversible bond to Cys481 in the BTK ATP pocket, blocking BCR->BTK->PLCG2->PKCbeta->CARD11-BCL10-MALT1->NF-kB. At the cell level the dominant effect is NOT direct killing: it is loss of chemokine-directed migration (CXCL12/CXCL13/CCL19), loss of integrin/fibronectin adhesion, and failure to assemble the immunological synapse — cells are evicted from the protective node into blood, where they starve of microenvironmental survival signals. Modest direct apoptosis on top. Cytostatic/anti-adhesive first, cytotoxic second. (Rey-Barroso 2024 Haematologica PMID 37381758; Woyach 2014 Blood PMID 24415539)

Redistribution lymphocytosis is the clinical readout of that microenvironment dependence: nodes shrink while ALC rises, because the drug decouples tissue retention from cell death. This is the single strongest piece of evidence that lymphoma cell fitness in vivo is a function of location, not just of cell-intrinsic state — an agent-based model without a node compartment cannot reproduce the drug's most characteristic behaviour. NOTCH1-mutant CLL shows blunted redistribution lymphocytosis AND impaired nodal shrinkage with worse PFS, tying the two together. (Del Poeta 2021 Haematologica PMID 32732360)

BTK C481S: substitution of the covalent anchor cysteine converts irreversible inhibitors into weak reversible ones. Downstream BCR mediators remain activatable. T474I/T474M gatekeeper mutations co-occur and add resistance; L528W is kinase-dead but retains scaffold signalling; A428D clashes with the adenine ring and defeats inhibitors AND degraders. PLCG2 gain-of-function mutations bypass BTK entirely. (Woyach 2024 Blood PMID 38754046; Sievers 2026 Cancer Discov PMID 42484277)

Pirtobrutinib: non-covalent, ATP-competitive, does not require C481; retains potency against C481S but is defeated by A428D and L528W. Sequencing matters — first-line pirtobrutinib can select mutations cross-resistant to the covalent class, and there are no clinical data on covalent BTKi after pirtobrutinib failure. (Chen B & Qian S 2026, Ann Hematol PMID 42678527)

BTK degraders (BGB-16673, NX-5948/bexobrutideg, NX-2127): PROTACs recruiting an E3 ligase to BTK, eliminating both catalytic AND scaffold function. Effect is catalytic and sub-stoichiometric, so the relevant model variable is a degradation rate versus a BTK resynthesis rate, not fractional occupancy. NX-2127 additionally degrades IKZF1/IKZF3, so it has a lenalidomide-like immune component layered on top. (Sabakhtarishvili 2025 Am J Clin Oncol PMID 39950399; Wu 2024 Br J Pharmacol PMID 39289908)

Venetoclax: BH3 mimetic occupying the BCL2 hydrophobic groove, releasing BIM/BID to activate BAX/BAK, permeabilise the mitochondrial outer membrane and trigger caspase-dependent apoptosis. Unambiguously CYTOTOXIC and fast — tumour lysis typically within 6–24 hours of dosing or dose escalation. This is the one agent in the list whose primary action is a clean single-cell kill event. (Lew & Seymour 2022 J Hematol Oncol PMID 35659041)

Why t(14;18) FL is less venetoclax-sensitive than CLL: BCL2 overexpression is necessary but not sufficient. What matters is BCL2 *dependence* — whether the cell's pro-apoptotic load is actually sequestered by BCL2 rather than by MCL1/BCL-xL, and whether BAX/BAK/BIM/BID are intact. CLL cells are highly primed and BCL2-addicted; FL cells co-express MCL1/BCL-xL and have lower BCL2:BIM ratios, and node-resident FL cells receive CD40L/BAFF/IL-4 signals that upregulate MCL1 and BCL-xL. MCL1 is a demonstrated venetoclax resistance factor in NHL, and degrading it (polatuzumab vedotin) restores sensitivity. (Bodo 2016 Oncotarget PMID 27661108; Lasater 2023 Am J Hematol PMID 36594167)

EZH2 inhibition (tazemetostat): SAM-competitive inhibition of the PRC2 catalytic subunit, lowering H3K27me3 and de-repressing genes that force germinal-centre exit and differentiation. Y646 (and A692/A677) gain-of-function mutations increase H3K27me3 processivity, creating the sensitive genotype. The action is epigenetic reprogramming, i.e. predominantly CYTOSTATIC/differentiating and SLOW — a leukemic-phase FL case took 4 months for circulating cells to become undetectable by count and 9 months by flow cytometry. Wild-type FL still responds at 35%, so EZH2 mutation is an enrichment marker, not a switch. (Morschhauser 2020 Lancet Oncol PMID 33035457; Kikuchi 2024 Int Cancer Conf J PMID 39398919; Orleni & Beumer 2024 PMID 38520556)

Lenalidomide: binds cereblon (CRBN), substrate receptor of CRL4-CRBN, and reshapes its surface to recruit IKZF1 (Ikaros) and IKZF3 (Aiolos) for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. TWO distinct arms. (a) Cell-autonomous, mainly in ABC-DLBCL: Aiolos/Ikaros are direct transcriptional repressors of interferon-stimulated genes, so their loss de-represses ISGs and drives apoptosis; IKAROS loss also downregulates SPIB. (b) Immune/indirect, dominant in FL: reactivation of exhausted T and NK cells, Th1 cytokine release, enhanced rituximab-dependent ADCC and lytic NK synapse formation. In FL the immune arm is the main one. (Hagner 2015 Blood PMID 26002965; Hagner 2022 Clin Cancer Res PMID 35583604; Solomon 2017 Exp Hematol PMID 28893618; Chiu 2019 Br J Haematol PMID 30767211)

Golcadomide (CC-99282), a CELMoD: same CRBN glue mechanism but engineered for deeper, faster, more sustained IKZF1/IKZF3 degradation than lenalidomide, plus MYC downregulation, ISG activation, immunogenic cell death, and preferential distribution to lymphoma-resident tissues. Dose-dependent Ikaros degradation depth correlates with end-of-treatment complete metabolic response with R-CHOP, and 0.4 mg gave deeper degradation than 0.2 mg. Also mixes cell-autonomous and immune effects. (Mo Z et al. 2026 Blood Cancer Discov PMID 41182271; Zheng X et al. 2026 Br J Clin Pharmacol PMID 42648738)

MALT1 inhibition (safimaltib/JNJ-67856633, CRD-1441551): blocks the paracaspase protease activity of MALT1 in the CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 signalosome, cutting chronic NF-kB downstream of BTK — hence activity in BTKi-resistant disease where MALT1 is overexpressed and bypasses BTK/CARD11. In MCL it also suppresses PI3K/AKT/mTOR and integrin signalling, reducing adhesion and migration. Critically double-edged: MALT1 is also required for regulatory T cell function, so inhibition simultaneously disables an immunosuppressive host compartment and risks autoimmunity — an explicitly microenvironment-coupled target. (Jiang VC et al. 2023 J Clin Invest PMID 36719376; Cao X et al. 2026 J Cell Commun Signal PMID 41783325)

PI3K isoform split explains the class. PI3K-delta is required for B-cell survival and migration (tumour-intrinsic). PI3K-gamma governs T-cell migration and macrophage polarisation (host). Duvelisib's dual delta/gamma inhibition works partly by remodelling T and myeloid support cells, and produced a redistribution lymphocytosis then partial remission in an ibrutinib-resistant patient whose clone carried BTK and PLCG2 mutations — i.e. benefit that was not explained by tumour-cell-intrinsic target engagement. The same immune disruption drives the class's fatal autoimmune colitis, pneumonitis, hepatotoxicity and opportunistic infections. (Chen SS et al. 2023 Clin Cancer Res PMID 37071496)

Cell-of-origin gating in DLBCL: ibrutinib monotherapy responses were 37% in ABC-DLBCL overall, but 80% in tumours carrying both CD79B and MYD88(L265P) mutations, because those cells assemble a My-T-BCR supercomplex (MYD88 + TLR9 + BCR) on endolysosomes driving NF-kB and mTOR. Genotype, not histology, defines the addicted population. Resistance can come from PIM1 point mutations that stabilise PIM1 and bypass BTK. (Phelan JD et al. 2018 Nature PMID 29925955; Kuo HP et al. 2016 Am J Cancer Res PMID 27904766)
modellable: Two-compartment node<->blood lymphocyte model, published and parameterised: tissue and circulation compartments with a drug-concentration-driven redistribution (egress) rate and a separate drug-driven death rate. Fitted on 94 patients / 658 ALC / 1501 PK observations. Patients with hyperlymphocytosis have higher baseline tissue:blood ratio and a LOWER death effect; progressors have ~2x lower baseline tissue and ~3x lower baseline blood lymphocyte counts. Directly transplantable as the BTKi module. (Gallais 2021, Clin Pharmacol Ther PMID 33539551)

Lymphocytosis timescale for validation: ALC rises within days-to-weeks of BTKi start, resolves within 8 months in the majority, persists >12 months in an identifiable subgroup. Model must reproduce a transient blood spike concurrent with nodal shrinkage. Use CCR7:S1PR1 expression ratio as the per-cell parameter governing egress propensity — it predicted lymphocytosis magnitude clinically.

Resistant-clone dynamics with an explicit lead time. Set C481S as a pre-existing minor subclone: detectable VAF ranges from 0.03% to ~16%; median 8.5 months (range 0–35.7) from first detection to clinical progression; steady-state prevalence 3% in treatment-naive vs 30% in relapsed/refractory over ~35 months on drug. Emergence rate must be conditioned on prior treatment history (number of driver mutations at baseline predicts BTK-mutant emergence: >=2 baseline drivers raises risk).

Fitness cost of resistance — a rare, quantified, directly simulable rule. BTK A428D cells are pan-resistant to inhibitors and degraders but at a COMPETITIVE DISADVANTAGE in the absence of BTK-directed drug. Implement as reduced proliferation or increased death for the mutant genotype off-drug; this predicts mutant decay during drug holidays and supports intermittent-dosing experiments in silico. Venetoclax co-treatment suppressed A428D expansion — model as an independent kill channel the mutation does not protect against.

Apoptosis as a threshold rule rather than a probability. Give each cell a BCL2:BIM ratio (plus MCL1 and BCL-xL buffers) and let venetoclax lower the effective BCL2 buffer. Cell dies when free activator BH3 exceeds the sequestration capacity. Calibrate: ~33% of aggressive B-NHL cells carry BAX/BAK/BIM/BID defects that make them unkillable by venetoclax regardless of BCL2 level. Venetoclax kill is FAST — the tumour lysis window is 6-24 hours after dose or dose escalation.

Subtype-specific venetoclax kill probabilities for calibration: MCL ORR 75% (median PFS 14 mo), FL 38% (11 mo), DLBCL 18% (1 mo), CLL ~79%. Median DOR by subtype: FL 26.6, MCL 15.7, MZL 20.1, WM 25.3 months. Achieving CR vs PR roughly triples DOR (MCL 31.5 vs 10.1; FL 37.6 vs 9.7 months) — evidence for a bimodal depth-of-response variable rather than a continuum.

Microenvironment-dependent MCL1/BCL-xL upregulation as an explicit spatial rule: node-resident cells get a survival bonus that specifically blunts venetoclax (not BTKi-mediated eviction). Supported by the observation that degrading MCL1 with polatuzumab vedotin restores venetoclax sensitivity, giving 76% response in relapsed FL (25/33) versus 29% in DLBCL (5/17).

Slow epigenetic agent timescale. Tazemetostat 800 mg BID continuous; effect is via H3K27me3 reduction and forced differentiation. Time-to-effect is months, not hours: in leukemic-phase FL, circulating lymphoma cells declined over 4 months to undetectable by count and 9 months by flow cytometry. Model as a per-division reduction in proliferative capacity plus a differentiation transition, NOT as a death rate. Genotype split: EZH2-mutant 69% respond vs wild-type 35%; mutation prevalence ~20% of FL.

Lenalidomide/CELMoD cannot be modelled as a tumour-cell-autonomous kill in FL. Minimum viable representation needs three agent types: tumour B cell, effector T/NK cell, and the anti-CD20 antibody. Rule: lenalidomide raises NK/T proliferative and cytokine capacity (cereblon-dependent), which multiplies rituximab ADCC kill probability per contact and increases lytic-synapse formation rate. Validation targets: PFS 39.4 vs 14.1 months (HR 0.46), 5.5-year OS HR 0.59, and rising circulating T/NK counts on R-squared versus falling on R-chemotherapy.

Degrader kinetics as rate rather than occupancy: BTK degraders act catalytically, so represent per-cell BTK abundance as a balance of a degradation rate constant and a resynthesis rate. NRX-0492 achieved >90% BTK degradation with sustained pharmacodynamics; a translational PK/PD model for BGB-16673 already exists (Wu 2024, Br J Pharmacol PMID 39289908) and can be lifted. Clinical anchors: BGB-16673 ORR 94.4% (n=67), NX-5948 ORR 83.3% (n=42, median time to first response 1.9 months).

Golcadomide dose-response is quantified as degradation depth: 0.4 mg gave more rapid and deeper Ikaros degradation than 0.2 mg with R-CHOP, and exposure related positively to end-of-treatment complete metabolic response. Usable as a graded target-degradation -> response coupling function.

Trial-versus-real-world discount factor. Same drug, same indication, same line: pirtobrutinib in post-covalent-BTKi MCL gave ORR 34% / median PFS 5.3 months in 153 real-world patients versus substantially better BRUIN trial numbers.
