If the simulation is calibrated on trial ORRs, expect it to overstate population effect; the Ki-67 >=50% (HR 2.31), TP53-mutant (HR 1.78) and <=12 months prior cBTKi duration (HR 1.77) covariates give a usable risk-stratification rule.

Genotype-gated response in DLBCL: ibrutinib response 37% in ABC overall but 80% in CD79B + MYD88(L265P) double-mutant. Implement as a discrete addiction flag on the agent rather than a continuous sensitivity parameter.
open_questions: Is BTK inhibition in vivo primarily cytostatic-plus-eviction, or does it also carry a substantial direct kill term? The Gallais PK-PD model needs BOTH a redistribution effect and a death effect to fit the data, so the answer is 'both', but the relative magnitude and how it varies by subtype (CLL vs MCL vs MZL vs WM) is not well quantified anywhere I found.

Nobody has published a head-to-head BH3-profiling comparison of primary FL versus primary CLL cells quantifying BCL2 dependence. The clinical inference (CLL more BCL2-addicted) is solid, but the mechanistic explanation I give — MCL1/BCL-xL co-dependence plus lower BCL2:BIM ratio plus node-derived CD40L/BAFF/IL-4 survival signals — is assembled from adjacent papers rather than one direct measurement. Treat as a hypothesis to test, not a fact to hard-code.

How much of tazemetostat's 35% response rate in EZH2 wild-type FL is tumour-intrinsic versus immune? EZH2 inhibition de-represses MHC class I/II and chemokines in other settings, and tazemetostat was combined with atezolizumab explicitly for microenvironment reprogramming (though that combination only reached ORR 16% in relapsed DLBCL). If a meaningful fraction is immune, a purely tumour-cell model will misattribute the effect.
There are no clinical data on covalent BTK inhibitors AFTER pirtobrutinib failure, so the sequencing asymmetry cannot yet be modelled with real transition probabilities.

Clinical response rates for MALT1 inhibitors (safimaltib/JNJ-67856633) in B-cell malignancies are described only qualitatively as 'preliminary antitumor activity' in the sources I could reach — I could not source hard ORR/PFS numbers. Same for most trispecific small-molecule work, which does not really exist as a distinct class; the trispecific action is in antibodies (e.g. CD20xCD3xCD28), not small molecules.
Whether the fitness cost of BTK A428D is large enough to make intermittent dosing clinically useful is untested — this is a good candidate for a pre-registered in silico experiment.

For golcadomide, the split between cell-autonomous IKZF1/3-driven ISG apoptosis and immune-mediated killing has not been quantified in patients, so the balance parameter would have to be fitted rather than assigned.
Targeted small molecules and immunomodul.caveats:
"AGENTS WHOSE EFFECT IS INDIRECT — the point most relevant to your modelling decision. Ranked by how badly a tumour-cell-only simulation would misrepresent them. (1) Lenalidomide in FL/MZL: dominantly immune. Cereblon-mediated IKZF1/3 degradation reactivates T and NK cells and amplifies rituximab ADCC; the drug's own single-agent activity in FL is modest. A cell-autonomous model of R-squared would be simply wrong. (2) Golcadomide and other CELMoDs: mixed — real cell-autonomous ISG/MYC-driven apoptosis in DLBCL, plus immunogenic cell death and T/NK effects. (3) Duvelisib and the PI3K class: PI3K-delta hits the tumour B cell, but PI3K-gamma acts on T-cell migration and macrophage polarisation; clinical benefit after BTKi failure occurred irrespective of BTK mutation status, implying host-compartment mechanism. (4) MALT1 inhibitors: tumour-intrinsic NF-kB blockade AND disabling of regulatory T cells — a target that acts on both sides of the tumour-immune interface at once. (5) BTK inhibitors: not immune-mediated in the classical sense, but ALSO not primarily a direct kill — the drug's signature clinical behaviour (nodal shrinkage with blood lymphocytosis) is a relocation phenomenon. Ibrutinib additionally normalises Treg and Tfh proportions and reduces T-cell exhaustion markers over 12 months (Medina-Gil 2025 Haematologica PMID 40079085). Only VENETOCLAX, of everything reviewed here, is a clean cell-autonomous cytotoxic you can model as a per-cell death event. Tazemetostat is cell-autonomous but cytostatic and slow.

COMPARABILITY. Response rates quoted here come from trials with wildly different populations, lines of therapy and response criteria (2007 vs Lugano IWG), and most single-agent NHL data are single-arm phase I/II. Cross-trial ORR comparisons — including the venetoclax subtype table — are indicative, not measured differences. The network meta-analyses I cite for pirtobrutinib are explicitly labelled exploratory by their own authors, with wide credible intervals.

CLL/SLL vs NHL. A large fraction of the mechanistic and resistance literature (C481S kinetics, redistribution lymphocytosis, venetoclax MRD dynamics) is CLL data. CLL is a leukemic disease with an accessible blood compartment; transferring these parameters to nodal FL, MCL or DLBCL is an assumption, not an observation. Flag it explicitly in any model that does so.

SOURCE CAVEATS. The BTK degrader clinical numbers (BGB-16673 ORR 94.4%, NX-5948 83.3%) come from an ASH 2025 conference summary, not peer-reviewed full publications — small n, short follow-up, likely to move. The real-world pirtobrutinib MCL series (Phillips 2026) is a preprint. The Sievers 2026 A428D paper and the golcadomide papers are very recent (2026) and not yet independently replicated.

WHAT I COULD NOT SOURCE. Hard efficacy numbers for MALT1 inhibitors in B-cell lymphoma. Also note there is no real 'trispecific small molecule' class in lymphoma — trispecifics are antibodies/T-cell engagers, outside the small-molecule scope you framed. Umbralisib's specific withdrawal date and the copanlisib withdrawal details came from secondary reporting (AJMC/OncLive summarising FDA ODAC), not from a primary FDA document I fetched; treat those dates as medium confidence.

I am not a clinician and none of this is treatment guidance."

T-cell redirecting therapy in non-Hodgki.domain: T-cell redirecting therapy in non-Hodgkin lymphoma: CD19 CAR-T (axi-cel, tisa-cel, liso-cel, brexu-cel) and CD20xCD3 bispecific antibodies (mosunetuzumab, glofitamab, epcoritamab) — mechanism at the cell level, outcomes with long-term follow-up, resistance, and dosing schedule rationale. Prepared for a computational biologist building a cell-level / agent-based simulation. Literature searched via Europe PMC, September 2026.

key_facts.fact: Axi-cel (CD28 costim) in refractory LBCL: at 63-month median follow-up, responses were ongoing in about one third of infused patients, and roughly half were alive when non-lymphoma deaths are censored out.
key_facts.numbers: n=101; ORR 83%, CR 58%; 31% ongoing response at median follow-up 63.1 mo; median OS 25.8 mo; 5-yr OS 42.6%; 5-yr disease-specific survival 51.0%. Polyclonal B-cell recovery in 91%.
key_facts.source: Neelapu SS et al. 2023, Blood (ZUMA-1 5-year). PMID 36821768

key_facts.fact: Tisa-cel (4-1BB costim) in relapsed/refractory LBCL at 5 years: a durable plateau exists but the overall PFS fraction is lower than axi-cel, largely reflecting lower initial response.
key_facts.numbers: n=115 infused; median follow-up 74.3 mo; 60-mo relapse-free probability among responders 61%; 60-mo PFS 28%; 60-mo OS 32% all infused, 56% in CR/PR. No secondary T-cell malignancies.
key_facts.source: Maziarz RT et al. 2026, J Clin Oncol (JULIET 5-year). PMID 41252666

key_facts.fact: Liso-cel (4-1BB, defined 1:1 CD4:CD8 dosing) in LBCL and brexu-cel (CD28) in mantle cell lymphoma give high response rates; MCL responders still show substantial late attrition from both relapse and non-relapse causes.
key_facts.numbers: Liso-cel TRANSCEND NHL 001: n=256 evaluable, ORR 73%, CR 53%; target dose 100x10^6 CAR+ cells (50x10^6 CD8 + 50x10^6 CD4); grade>=3 CRS 2%, grade>=3 NE 10%. Brexu-cel ZUMA-2: ORR 93%, CR 67%, median DOR 36.5 mo, median OS 46.5 mo; at 5 yr, relapse-related mortality 40% and non-relapse mortality 22% of responders.
key_facts.source: Abramson JS et al. 2020, Lancet (PMID 32888407); Munoz J et al. 2026 (ZUMA-2 5-year, PMID 42036693)

key_facts.fact: In follicular lymphoma, CD19 CAR-T produces the deepest and most durable remissions of any setting; after 30 months post-infusion, lymphoma progression becomes rare, which is the strongest single argument for a true plateau.
key_facts.numbers: ZUMA-5 axi-cel (median f/u 64.6 mo, n=159 iNHL): ORR 90%, CR 75%, median DOR 60.4 mo, median PFS 62.2 mo, 55% alive without subsequent therapy; 34% of FL had lymphoma progression/death. ELARA tisa-cel: CR 69.1%, ORR 86.2%. TRANSCEND FL liso-cel: ORR 95.7%, CR 73.4%, 1-yr remission 81%.
key_facts.source: Neelapu SS et al. 2025 (ZUMA-5 5-year, PMID 41100801); Fowler NH et al. 2022 Nat Med (ELARA, PMID 34921238); Britton K et al. 2025 (FDA summary TRANSCEND FL, PMID 40663365)

key_facts.fact: Is the plateau a cure? Randomised 2L data and mixture-cure modelling support a cured fraction in LBCL, but the fraction is model-dependent and competing non-relapse mortality is non-trivial. Treat 'plateau' as a cured subpopulation plus ongoing attrition, not as zero hazard.
key_facts.numbers: ZUMA-7 (2L, n=359): median f/u 47.2 mo, 4-yr OS 54.6% axi-cel vs 46.0% SOC (HR 0.73), 4-yr PFS 41.8% vs 24.4%. Mixture-cure model estimates of the axi-cel cure fraction range 24-54% depending on data cut and parametric form.
key_facts.source: Westin JR et al. 2023, NEJM (PMID 37272527); Perales MA et al. 2025 (cure-assumption validation, PMID 40930226)

key_facts.fact: Costimulatory domain sets killing style, not just persistence: CD28-zeta CAR-T form brief, acutely lethal synapses and are the better serial killers and more sensitive to low antigen density; 4-1BB-zeta form long synapses, kill cooperatively, and rely on expansion.
key_facts.numbers: CD28-zeta: near-complete target loss within 40 min, target death within ~20 min, shorter T_contact, more lethal synapses over 6 h, a single cell can hold two cytolytic synapses at once. 4-1BB-zeta: CAR/LFA-1 accumulation past 50 min, Fas-ligand-dependent chronic killing, central-memory-skewed, more CD4 expansion.
key_facts.source: Gad AZ et al. 2025, Sci Adv (PMID 39792660); Frazee CS et al. 2026 (asymmetric division, PMID 42332264)

key_facts.fact: Mosunetuzumab, fixed duration (8 cycles if CR, max 17), in 3L+ follicular lymphoma at 3 years: most complete responders stay in remission off all therapy, and B cells recover.
key_facts.numbers: n=90; median f/u 37.4 mo; CR 60.0%, ORR 77.8%; median DOR 35.9 mo; among 54 CRs, 49 still in CR at end of treatment, 30-mo remission rate 72.4%; median PFS 24.0 mo; 36-mo OS 82.4%; median time to CD19+ B-cell recovery 18.4 mo. Subcutaneous cohort: ORR 76.6%, CR 61.7%, CRS 29.8% vs 44.4% IV.
key_facts.source: Sehn LH et al. 2025, Blood Adv (PMID 39447094); Bartlett NL et al. 2026 (SC primary analysis, PMID 41862428)

key_facts.fact: Glofitamab is given as a strictly fixed 12 cycles and stopped; complete responders then remain treatment-free, with a durable tail. This is the cleanest evidence that continuous exposure is not required for durability.
key_facts.numbers: Pivotal phase 2 (n=154): IRC CR 39%, median time to CR 42 days, 78% of CRs ongoing at 12 mo, 12-mo PFS 37%, CRS 63% (grade>=3 4%). 3-year update (median f/u 37.7 mo): CR 40%, ORR 52%, median duration of CR 29.8 mo; among patients in CR at end of treatment, 2-yr PFS 57% and OS 77%, all treatment-free >=2 yr.
key_facts.source: Dickinson MJ et al. 2022, NEJM (PMID 36507690); ASH 2024 abstract 194333, 3-year follow-up of pivotal NP30179

key_facts.fact: Epcoritamab is dosed continuously until progression; its 3-year LBCL data show a similar durable-CR tail, so fixed vs continuous has not been shown to differ in durability. No head-to-head trial exists.
key_facts.numbers: EPCORE NHL-1 LBCL (median f/u 37.1 mo, 39% prior CAR-T): ORR 59%, CR 41%; median DOR 20.8 mo; median duration of CR 36.1 mo (longest ongoing >43 mo); median PFS 4.2 mo overall vs 37.3 mo in CRs; 45% MRD-negative at any point; CRS 51%. FL: ORR 82.0%, CR 62.5%.
key_facts.source: Karimi YH et al. 2026 (EPCORE NHL-1 3-year, PMID 41634395); Sinnollareddy M et al. 2026 (exposure-response, PMID 42541678)

key_facts.fact: Step-up dosing exists because CRS severity tracks the size of the first synchronous T-cell/B-cell engagement event. Priming doses deplete accessible targets and blunt the cytokine burst before the full dose; all three agents use it, plus obinutuzumab pre-treatment for glofitamab.
key_facts.numbers: Glofitamab: 1000 mg obinutuzumab 7 days prior, then 2.5/10/30 mg. Epcoritamab 2-step 0.16/0.8/48 mg; a 3-step 0.16/0.8/3/48 mg with dexamethasone and hydration further lowered CRS with unchanged PK and B-cell depletion. Mosunetuzumab IV 1/2/60 then 30 mg; SC 5/45/45 mg. Grade>=3 CRS: glofitamab 4%, epcoritamab 2.5%, mosunetuzumab ~2%.
key_facts.source: Dickinson 2022 NEJM; Sinnollareddy M et al. 2026 (PMID 42541678); Budde LE et al. 2022, Lancet Oncol (PMID 35803286)

key_facts.fact: Serial killing is quantified best for CD19xCD3 engagers: one T cell kills several targets over hours, and complete target clearance occurs at effector-to-target ratios well below 1:1 — the key quantitative difference from stoichiometric chemotherapy.
key_facts.numbers: A single T cell eliminated multiple targets within a 9-hour window; complete target elimination within 24 h at E:T as low as 1:5; killing began within minutes; EC50 10-50 pg/mL (sub-picomolar) across 86 donors, ~100,000-fold more potent per mole than rituximab. T cells stayed motile; no stable clusters formed.
key_facts.source: Hoffmann P et al. 2005, Int J Cancer (PMID 15688411); Dreier T et al. 2002, Int J Cancer (PMID 12209608)

key_facts.fact: CAR synapses are non-classical: no LFA-1 adhesion ring, multifocal Lck, faster and shorter proximal signalling, faster lytic granule delivery, and faster detachment from the dying target — the mechanistic basis of rapid debulking. In vivo, kill-and-release completes inside ~25 minutes.
key_facts.numbers: CAR-T formed fewer stable conjugates than TCR-T over 10-40 min; pLck doubled by 2 min then decayed by 10 min; synapse actin ring smaller at 20 min; once granules land, target apoptosis time is identical for CAR and TCR. Intravital bone marrow: engage, kill, detach within 25 min; not all contacts flux calcium or kill.
key_facts.source: Davenport AJ et al. 2018, PNAS (PMID 29440406); Cazaux M et al. 2019, J Exp Med (PMID 30936262)

key_facts.fact: Killing is not always binary. In B-lymphoma it is a single-hit yes/no event, but where per-contact lethality is low, death requires temporally clustered sublethal hits from several T cells — making local effector density, not just total dose, the controlling variable.
key_facts.numbers: ~3 serial sublethal hits delivered with inter-hit intervals below ~50 min discriminate death from recovery; sublethal damage (perforin pores, nuclear envelope rupture, DNA damage) is reversible; effect strongest where CTL density is high and swarming occurs.
key_facts.source: Weigelin B et al. 2021, Nat Commun (PMID 34471116); Rastogi A et al. 2020 (agent-based evaluation of killing models, PMID 33370254)

key_facts.fact: Antigen loss is a density problem, not a binary on/off: CARs need roughly an order of magnitude more surface antigen than a TCR needs pMHC, so partial CD19 downregulation is sufficient for escape. CD19-negative relapse is common in LBCL but rare in MCL and FL.
key_facts.numbers: >1000 CD19 molecules per tumour cell required for CAR efficacy vs <100 peptide-MHC for TCR-T. ~30% of LBCL relapses fall below the CD19 density threshold; CD19-negative relapse in ~30% of axi-cel LBCL responders. ZUMA-2 (MCL): 1 of 60 relapses CD19-negative; ZUMA-5 (FL): none. In ZUMA-1, 75% of patients with CD19 loss still responded.
key_facts.source: Arena G & Chiarle R 2025 (PMID 41228246); Strati P et al. 2026, ZUMA-14 (PMID 41492094); Huang J et al. 2026 (PMID 42023212)

key_facts.fact: Tumour bulk is the dominant failure predictor for both modalities, and mechanistically because lymphoma proliferation can outrun cytotoxicity: the ratio of peak effector number to tumour cell number, not the absolute dose, sets the outcome.
key_facts.numbers: PK/PD model calibrated on axi-cel: each 2-fold reduction in pre-infusion burden adds ~10% of patients progression-free at 12 months; simulated debulking cut progression risk 35%; observed HR for progression, small vs large tumour, 0.16. For CD20xCD3 bispecifics, baseline whole-body MTV >504.7 cm3 gave median PFS 1 vs 3 months (HR 5.6). Primary resistance ~50% DLBCL, ~10% MCL, 5-15% FL; secondary 40-50% DLBCL, 40% MCL, 30% FL.
key_facts.source: Pomeroy AE et al. 2026 (PMID 41143460); Wollnitza S et al. 2026 (PMID 42223630); Arena G & Chiarle R 2025 (PMID 41228246)

mechanisms: Redirected lysis is MHC-independent. A CAR scFv or a CD3-arm of a bispecific cross-links a T cell to a CD19+/CD20+ B cell, forming a cytolytic synapse that triggers perforin/granzyme release; the T cell then detaches and can re-engage. This makes the therapeutic unit a *rate* (kills per effector per unit time) rather than a *dose* (drug molecules per cell), which is the fundamental departure from chemotherapy.

CAR synapse is structurally non-classical: multifocal Lck microclusters, no discrete LFA-1 adhesion ring, smaller actin ring by 20 min, LFA-1 dispensable for cytotoxicity. Proximal (Lck, ZAP-70) and distal (ERK) signalling rise faster and decay faster than through the TCR. Net result: faster granule delivery, faster detachment, higher serial-killing throughput, but shorter and less sustained signalling — plausibly linked to poorer memory programming.

Costimulatory domain bifurcates the killing strategy. CD28-zeta: CAR molecules translocate rapidly but transiently into membrane lipid rafts, MTOC and granules mobilise fast, synapse is brief and highly lethal, product is effector-memory skewed, sensitive to low antigen density, high peak expansion, shorter persistence, higher CRS/ICANS. 4-1BB-zeta: gradual CAR and LFA-1 accumulation at lipid rafts builds a mechanically tonic, long-lived synapse, chronic FasL-dependent killing, cooperative multi-effector killing of one target, central-memory skewed, greater CD4 expansion, longer persistence, lower toxicity. Costimulatory domains also tune asymmetric first division: 4-1BB gives greater transcriptional/metabolic divergence between daughters and more persistence-prone progeny.

Density dependence, mechanistically. Tumour cell death rate scales with the local probability of effector-target encounter, so it is roughly bilinear in effector density and target density, while lymphoma growth is exponential in target number. Above a critical target:effector ratio the tumour outruns cytotoxicity even though every individual T cell is fully functional. Chemotherapy has no analogous ratio term — drug exposure is set by pharmacokinetics, not by tumour cell number. This is why the ratio of peak CAR-T to initial tumour burden predicts durable response better than the infused dose.

Bispecifics add a second density dependence: the drug is a bridge, so efficacy depends on the product of drug concentration, target antigen density AND the number/fitness of endogenous T cells in the lesion. CAR-T supplies its own effectors; bispecifics do not. This makes bispecific efficacy uniquely vulnerable to prior T-cell-depleting therapy (bendamustine within 6 months significantly shortened glofitamab PFS) and to T-cell-poor microenvironments.

Resistance pathways: (a) antigen escape — CD19 mutation/exon-2 skipping, alternative splicing, epigenetic silencing (IKZF1 knockdown lowers surface CD19), trogocytosis, and simple downregulation below the ~1000-molecule CAR threshold; lineage switch is mostly a B-ALL, not lymphoma, phenomenon; (b) T-cell-intrinsic failure — poor pre-infusion T-cell fitness, low polyfunctionality, exhaustion signatures, prior doxorubicin/bendamustine exposure, low CD8-fit fraction; (c) tumour-intrinsic — TP53 mutation, MYC/BCL2 alterations, APOBEC mutational signature, focal RHOA deletion (91% of progressors in one WGS cohort), impaired apoptotic competence; (d) microenvironment — Tregs, suppressive myeloid/monocyte-macrophage-rich and fibroblast-rich niches, PD-L1, and reduced cytotoxic activity in lymph nodes relative to bone marrow.

CRS mechanism and step-up rationale: the first large synchronous engagement event releases IFN-gamma and TNF from T cells, which activates monocytes/macrophages to produce IL-6 and IL-1, driving endothelial activation and capillary leak. Severity tracks the magnitude of that first burst, hence tumour burden. Step-up (priming) dosing deliberately caps the size of the first engagement wave — reducing accessible targets and pre-activating a limited T-cell pool — so the full dose lands on a partly depleted, partly desensitised system. Obinutuzumab pre-treatment for glofitamab does the same by depleting circulating and peripheral CD20+ cells 7 days ahead.

Trade-off between debulking and priming: CD19+ tumour is also the antigen that drives CAR-T expansion. Empirically this trade-off resolves in favour of debulking — axi-cel expansion is equal or better in patients who achieve CR to bridging therapy — so a simulation should not assume a monotone benefit of residual antigen for expansion.
modellable: Serial killing rate: one redirected T cell kills multiple targets within a 9-hour window (BiTE, in vitro). Use ~0.3-1 kills per effector per hour as an upper-bound cytolytic throughput for CD28-type effectors; scale down for 4-1BB-type.

Engagement cycle duration: CAR-T engage, kill and detach within 25 min in vivo (bone marrow). Sub-steps: T_seek (search), T_contact (conjugation), T_death (target apoptosis onset). Target death within ~20 min for CD28-zeta; >50 min and often incomplete for 4-1BB-zeta over the same interval.

Serial killing capacity (SKC) as a finite budget: model exhaustion as a linear decline in per-contact kill probability until cumulative kills reach S0, then transition the agent to an exhausted state (the ABMACT formulation). SKC ranked second only to E:T ratio in sensitivity analysis of tumour control.

Effector-to-target ratio as the top-ranked control parameter. Complete clearance is achievable at E:T as low as 1:5 with a bispecific in vitro. Note the strong discrepancy between nominal infused E:T and effective local E:T: an in vivo model dosed at 50:1 systemically fit best at a local E:T of 1:1, implying an infiltration efficiency of order 1-2%.

Antigen density thresholds: >1000 CD19 molecules per tumour cell required for CAR efficacy; <100 pMHC for a TCR. Implement per-cell antigen number as a continuous heritable trait with a sigmoid kill-probability vs density function, not a binary antigen+/antigen- flag. ~30% of LBCL relapses sit below threshold.

Multi-hit killing option: ~3 sublethal hits with inter-hit intervals <50 min are required for death where per-contact lethality is low, with damage decaying between hits. B-lymphoma killing is closer to single-hit/binary — worth implementing both modes and testing which reproduces observed dose-response.

Tumour growth: aggressive NHL doubling times from serial volume measurements; the ABMACT calibration used 0.445/day for Raji lymphoma vs 0.223/day for glioblastoma stem cells. Growth must be exponential so it can outrun cytotoxicity at high burden.

CAR-T pharmacokinetics: piecewise expansion-then-biphasic-decline with two compartments (effector and memory). Six parameters: Cmax, fold expansion, memory fraction FB, Tmax, effector decay alpha, memory decay beta. Peak expansion clinically observed days 7-17. Durable response probability is a logistic function of (peak CAR-T count / initial tumour cell number).

Debulking sensitivity: each 2-fold reduction in pre-infusion tumour burden adds ~10 percentage points to the 12-month progression-free fraction; a simulated debulking arm cut progression risk 35%. Use as a validation target.

Clinical burden thresholds for calibration: baseline whole-body MTV >504.7 cm3 predicts median PFS 1 vs 3 months for CD20xCD3 bispecifics (HR 5.6); MTV outperforms IPI for CAR-T PFS (AUC 0.68 vs 0.61). ctDNA at end of first-line therapy is ~100-fold lower than at relapse (1.5 vs 44 hGE/mL) — a natural MRD-vs-frank-relapse comparison.

Step-up dosing schedules to implement literally: glofitamab 1000 mg obinutuzumab day -7, then 2.5 / 10 / 30 mg, 12 cycles fixed. Epcoritamab 0.16 / 0.8 / 48 mg (or 3-step 0.16 / 0.8 / 3 / 48 mg), weekly C1-3, q2w C4-9, q4w C10+, continuous. Mosunetuzumab IV 1 / 2 / 60 / 30 mg, 21-day cycles, 8 cycles if CR else up to 17; SC 5 / 45 / 45 mg.

Cell doses: axi-cel and brexu-cel 2x10^6 CAR+ cells/kg; ZUMA-2 cohort 2 used 0.5x10^6/kg; liso-cel 100x10^6 CAR+ cells split as 50x10^6 CD8 + 50x10^6 CD4 (a defined-composition dose worth modelling as two agent subtypes with different kill rates and expansion).

Spatial/anatomical heterogeneity rule: CAR-T cytotoxic activity is reduced in lymph nodes relative to bone marrow, and antigen-loss variants emerged only in bone marrow in the intravital model. Circulating targets trapped CAR-T in the lungs, reducing lymphoid-organ access — a sequestration compartment worth including.

CD4 vs CD8 effector subtypes: CD8 CAR-T have shorter T_contact and higher serial killing rates; CD4 CAR-T kill more slowly (lower granzyme B) but can hold multiple simultaneous conjugates. Multi-killing conjugation state protects against activation-induced cell death — T cells conjugated to a single target apoptose faster and more often, an effect stronger in CD8.

Outcome targets for validation (long-term fractions): LBCL 3L axi-cel 5-yr OS 42.6% and 31% ongoing response; tisa-cel 60-mo PFS 28%; 2L axi-cel 4-yr PFS 41.8%, OS 54.6%; FL axi-cel median PFS 62.2 mo with progression rare after 30 months; MCL brexu-cel median DOR 36.5 mo; mosunetuzumab FL 30-month remission rate among CRs 72.4%; glofitamab CRs at end of treatment 2-yr PFS 57%; epcoritamab median PFS in CRs 37.3 mo.
open_questions: No head-to-head randomised comparison of fixed-duration vs continuous bispecific dosing exists. Glofitamab (12 fixed cycles) and epcoritamab (continuous) both show durable CR tails, but the populations and CR definitions differ. An exposure-response analysis found epcoritamab response arose during the weekly phase in 96.2% of responders and was maintained independent of cycle-4-onward exposure, which is indirect evidence that continuous dosing may be unnecessary — but it is not a randomised test.

Whether the plateau is cure. Mixture-cure model estimates of the axi-cel cure fraction span 24-54% depending on data cut and parametric family. Non-relapse mortality is substantial (22% of ZUMA-2 responders at 5 years), so 'cured of lymphoma' and 'alive' diverge. Disease-specific survival (51% at 5 yr in ZUMA-1) is the more honest quantity to model.

Serial killing rates for CAR-T against human lymphoma in vivo are essentially unmeasured. Almost all quantitative numbers come from in vitro nanowell/microscopy assays, mouse intravital imaging, or bispecific (BiTE) systems. The per-capita killing rate in a human lymph node is unknown.
Effective local E:T ratio in patients is unmeasured. Model fits imply infiltration efficiency of order 1-2% of infused cells reaching the tumour, but this is inferred, not observed.

CD20 antigen loss frequency after CD20xCD3 bispecific failure is not well quantified. Reviews list antigen loss as a mechanism, but no large biopsy series with a CD20-negative-relapse percentage comparable to the ~30% CD19-negative figure for CAR-T was found. Treat any CD20-loss frequency as low-confidence.

Whether prior CD19- or CD20-directed T-cell engagers compromise subsequent CAR-T (and vice versa) — sequencing data are retrospective. In myeloma, a >=6-month interval between T-cell-redirecting therapies improved outcomes; whether this generalises to NHL is untested.

Post-CAR-T salvage remains poor: in the DESCAR-T registry, 33% relapsed after 2L CAR-T, and despite bispecific-based salvage in 65%, median OS after relapse was only 6.5 months. What kills the tail is not well characterised mechanistically.

Whether the antigen-density kill-probability function is sigmoid, threshold-like, or continuous, and how it shifts with T-cell fitness. One review states that improved T-cell fitness lowers the required antigen density threshold — if true this couples two parameters that models usually treat as independent.
T-cell redirecting therapy in non-Hodgki.caveats: Sourcing and confidence caveats for a modeller. (1) Cross-trial comparisons are invalid as causal comparisons: ZUMA-1/JULIET/TRANSCEND enrolled different populations, and JULIET's lower PFS partly reflects a longer, more attritional bridging period rather than 4-1BB inferiority per se. One review notes that when compared within LBCL, CD28 and 4-1BB products gave similar outcomes despite the mechanistic differences. Use the mechanism facts for cell-level rules and the trial facts for population-level validation targets — do not use trial differences to infer costimulatory-domain effect sizes. (2) MAIC/indirect comparisons cited (liso-cel vs axi-cel vs tisa-cel in FL; epcoritamab vs axi-cel) are sponsor-conducted matching-adjusted analyses, not randomised evidence; directionally useful, not decisive. (3) The glofitamab 3-year numbers come from an ASH 2024 conference abstract, not a peer-reviewed full paper — lower confidence than the NEJM primary publication. (4) Most quantitative serial-killing and synapse numbers come from in vitro nanowell/live-imaging assays and mouse models, frequently in non-lymphoma systems (HER2/glioma for the CD28-vs-4-1BB synapse work, melanoma for additive cytotoxicity). Human in vivo rates are not directly measured; scale accordingly and treat these as order-of-magnitude priors. (5) The ABMACT parameter values are for CAR-NK, not CAR-T; the model structure (serial-killing budget, E:T dominance) transfers better than the numeric fits. (6) Real-world outcomes are consistently worse than trials: PFS is shorter in every real-world cohort examined, and real-world glofitamab gave ORR 46%/CR 27% vs 52%/40% in the pivotal trial. If you calibrate on trial data, expect optimism. (7) The reviewing author is not a clinician and this briefing is not clinical guidance.

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: the 2026 unmet-nee.domain: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: the 2026 unmet-need frontier (post-CAR-T DLBCL, POD24/transformed FL, TP53-mutant disease, T/NK-cell lymphomas, CNS disease, unfit patients, global access) plus ctDNA/MRD-guided therapy as the methodological frontier

key_facts.fact: Real-world French registry: one third of patients relapse after second-line CAR-T, and salvage barely works despite bispecifics being used in most of them.
key_facts.numbers: 893 patients treated with 2L axi-cel/liso-cel; 297 (33%) relapsed; median time to relapse 2.7 months, 35% of relapses <2 months; salvage ORR 39.1%, CR 27.6%; median OS after relapse 6.5 months, median PFS 3.4 months; bispecific monotherapy median OS 7.1 months. Poor-OS predictors: relapse <6 mo, ECOG>=2, CRP>=30 mg/L
key_facts.source: DESCAR-T/LYSA, HemaSphere 2026, PMID 42099680 (PMC13148476)

key_facts.fact: Even late failure after CAR-T (>3 months) is lethal; a large minority of all CAR-T failures are late, and salvage response rates are low.
key_facts.numbers: 298 late-failure LBCL patients = 39.9% of registry failures; median age 62; 76.5% got systemic therapy; ORR 22.6% (CR 18%); median OS 4.4 months; bispecifics better PFS-2 vs chemo (HR 0.350); radiotherapy 12-mo PFS-2 41.5%
key_facts.source: DESCAR-T/LYSA, Blood Advances 2026, PMID 41124667 (PMC12828827)

key_facts.fact: Bispecific salvage after CAR-T failure roughly halves mortality but is not curative; a prospective trial with a matched external control quantified the gain.
key_facts.numbers: LYSA BiCAR, n=46 treated with short-ramp-up glofitamab. Median follow-up 30.4 mo; median OS 17.3 mo; 2-yr OS 38.3%. Weighted comparison vs 133 controls: median OS 19.6 vs 7.6 months, HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.31-0.79, P=0.007)
key_facts.source: Bachy/LYSA BiCAR, J Hematol Oncol 2026, PMID 42393723

key_facts.fact: CAR-T cures a minority in the real world, and non-relapse mortality is a major competing risk that keeps accruing after 2 years.
key_facts.numbers: US Lymphoma CAR T Consortium, 275 infused, median follow-up 58 months: 5-yr PFS 29%, 5-yr OS 40%, 5-yr lymphoma-specific survival 53%, 5-yr NRM 16.2% (>half of NRM events beyond 2 years). Second malignancies 9% (24/275; 15 therapy-related myeloid). Age>=60: lower relapse, NRM OR 4.5
key_facts.source: Chihara et al., JCO 2024, PMID 39094076 (PMC11483191)

key_facts.fact: Most relapsed large B-cell lymphoma patients never reach CAR-T; attrition, not efficacy, is the dominant real-world loss.
key_facts.numbers: Flatiron 2011-2024, n=10,016 starting 1L: only 30% initiated 2L; 13% died within 12 months of 1L without any 2L. Among 'clearly fit' 2L-CAR-T-eligible patients (n=128, 2022-2024) only 25% received 2L CAR-T; 3L eligible fit (n=182) only 35.7% received CAR-T. 12-month death: 11% (ECOG 0/1), 35% (ECOG 2), 55% (ECOG>=3)
key_facts.source: Flatiron real-world LBCL treatment patterns, 2026, PMID 42234934 (PMC13449983)

key_facts.fact: POD24 follicular lymphoma remains a defined high-risk state with no standard therapy; salvage response is high but a pooled analysis found no cure signal.
key_facts.numbers: Pooled 21 trials, 1242 POD24 patients: CAR-T ORR 91.2% (95% CI 83.7-98.7), CR 75.7% (55.1-96.4, I2=94%); bispecifics ORR 81.6% (75.9-87.3), CR 65.7% (57.1-74.3); loncastuximab+R ORR 100%/CR 79.3%; tafasitamab+R2 ORR 87.5%/CR 43.2%. POD24 affects ~20% of FL; retained-histology POD24 median EFS ~9.8 months, 5-yr OS ~71%
key_facts.source: Shen et al., Blood Advances 2026, PMID 41587420; LEO Consortium, Blood Adv 2025 (9:1013)

key_facts.fact: Reconstructed-IPD benchmarking of R/R FL therapies shows CAR-T leads on 2-year durability, with a wide spread across modalities and no head-to-head data.
key_facts.numbers: 24-month landmark PFS: liso-cel 65.4% (52.0-82.4), axi-cel 62.0% (50.2-76.6), zanubrutinib+obinutuzumab 53.8% (45.2-63.9), mosunetuzumab 49.3% (39.3-61.7), epcoritamab 43.7% (31.3-61.1), obinutuzumab alone 24.7%. PFS RMST24: 19.5 / 18.6 / 16.5 / 16.2 / 14.8 / 11.9 months

key_facts.fact: Histologic transformation hits a defined minority of follicular lymphoma; evidence in relapsed transformed FL is thin and entirely non-randomized.
key_facts.numbers: HT in 10-15% of all FL patients. Scoping review: 17 studies, ~222 t-FL patients total. CAR-T trials ORR 52-83%, CR 40-58%; real-world registries ORR 82-92%, CR 64-67%. Bispecifics: epcoritamab ORR 50%/CR 44%; glofitamab ORR 55%/CR 35%
key_facts.source: Cancer Control 2026 scoping review, PMID 42265975 (PMC13254433); Indian J Hematol Blood Transfus 2025, PMID 42040670

key_facts.fact: In mantle cell lymphoma, adding ibrutinib to first-line therapy substantially blunts the TP53 penalty, changing TP53 from an absolute to a relative adverse factor.
key_facts.numbers: TRIANGLE (n=870, ages 18-65), 4.5-yr follow-up, EHA 2026 update: differential TP53 effect on OS P=0.048; TP53 risk HR ~1.9 with ibrutinib vs ~10 without; early MRD response induced. TP53 alteration, blastoid histology and high Ki-67 remain the consistent high-risk triad
key_facts.source: TRIANGLE, EHA 2026 / Lancet 2026 PIIS0140-6736(26)00362-4; Dreyling et al., Lancet Haematology 2026, PMID 42685741

key_facts.fact: MCL molecular risk is broader than TP53: several independent lesions stratify PFS in elderly patients, giving a four-factor model.
key_facts.numbers: FIL V-RBAC trial, n=132 with CAPP-Seq (146 genes): ATM mutated 41.7% (55), TP53 mutated 23.5% (31), KMT2D 23.5%, ATM deletion 24%, CDKN2A loss 22%. Independent PFS factors beyond TP53: CDKN2A loss, CD36 mutation, single-hit ATM (favorable). Trial high-risk definitions: Ki-67 >30%, blastoid variant
key_facts.source: FIL V-RBAC, Blood Advances 2026, PMID 42498280

key_facts.fact: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma survival has essentially stagnated for PTCL-NOS and AITL across two decades, while only ALCL improved materially.
key_facts.numbers: NCDB, 29,075 PTCL patients, 2004-2020. PTCL-NOS/AITL: median OS 15.5 -> 18.5 months; 5-yr OS 31.8% -> 33.5% (era 1 vs era 2). ALCL: median OS 65.5 -> 114.5 months; 5-yr OS 50.9% -> 61.2%. Finnish registry (n=915): 5-yr OS PTCL-NOS 30%, ALK-ALCL 46%, ALK+ALCL 85%, EATL 15%; no improvement in relative survival 2002-2012 vs 2013-2018
key_facts.source: Blood Cancer Journal 2026, PMID 42236669 (PMC13234100); Sci Rep 2025, PMID 40715325

key_facts.fact: Early treatment failure in PTCL is near-uniformly fatal, defining the sharpest quantitative unmet need in lymphoma.
key_facts.numbers: LEO-MER prospective cohorts, 720 systemic PTCL patients (2002-2020, followed to 2024). CHOP-based induction 70% (CHOP 36%, CHOEP 23%, CHOP+novel 11.5% incl. 5% BV-CHP); consolidative ASCT only 14%. Patients failing EFS6: 5-year subsequent OS 12%. Failing EFS24: 17%. Allo-HCT in selected R/R PTCL: 5-yr OS ~40-55%
key_facts.source: LEO-MER, Blood Advances 2026, PMID 41707114 (PMC13195623); Bone Marrow Transplant 2026, PMID 42373849

key_facts.fact: In primary CNS lymphoma a randomized phase 3 finally settled consolidation: transplant beats non-myeloablative chemoimmunotherapy, but only for patients fit enough to be randomized.
key_facts.numbers: MATRix/IELSG43: 368 enrolled, 346 (94%) started MATRix induction, only 230 (63% of enrolled) randomized. 3-yr PFS 78% (69-85) HCT-ASCT vs 51% (41-60) R-DeVIC; HR 0.43 (0.27-0.68), P=0.0003. Mean AEs/patient 14.6 vs 9.3. In elderly PCNSL, WBRT causes ventricular enlargement 14.6%/yr vs 2.9%/yr without
key_facts.source: Illerhaus et al., Lancet 2026, PMID 42486133; J Clin Neurosci 2026, PMID 41921314

key_facts.fact: ctDNA-MRD at end of first-line therapy is now prospectively validated in LBCL and outperforms PET on positive predictive value, but it is a prognostic, not yet a proven actionable, marker.
key_facts.numbers: HOVON-902, PhasED-Seq, phased variants trackable in 134/136 (99%). EOT MRD-positive 17%, negative 83%. 3-yr PFS 17% vs 85% (HR 9.8, 95% CI 5.1-19, P=9.6e-12); 3-yr OS 43% vs 92% (HR 7.7). PPV for 2-yr PFS: MRD 68% vs PET 56% (P<=0.001); NPV 89% vs 88% (P=0.71). Independent of IPI and EOT PET-CT
key_facts.source: Meriranta/HOVON-902, JCO 2025, PMID 41385760 (PMC12879184)

key_facts.fact: No completed randomized trial has yet shown that changing therapy based on ctDNA improves outcome; MRD-negativity is not an accepted surrogate for cure in lymphoma.
key_facts.numbers: ALPHA3 (cema-cel for MRD+ after 1L LBCL) interim futility 2026: MRD clearance 58.3% (7/12) vs 16.7% (2/12) observation; ctDNA median -97.7% vs +26.6%. Target n~220, accrual to 2027, interim EFS mid-2027, primary EFS mid-2028. De-escalation trials (SHORTEN-ctDNA NCT06693830, NCT06748521) still enrolling
key_facts.source: Allogene ALPHA3 interim release 2026; J Clin Med 2026 review, PMID 42513473; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06500273/NCT06693830

mechanisms: Antigen escape after CD19 CAR-T: CD19 loss/downregulation drives a large share of recurrence. First-in-human trispecific CD19/CD20/CD22 CAR (OX40 costim), point-of-care manufactured, vein-to-vein 7 days: ORR 50% overall, CR in 83% of lymphoma patients, 1-yr OS 61% (Blood Cancer Discov 2026, PMID 42446920).

T-cell fitness as the rate-limiting input, not the CAR construct: exhaustion in the apheresis product correlated with progressive disease; ongoing responses at 60 months in ZUMA-1 were associated with early CAR T-cell expansion, and protracted B-cell aplasia was NOT required for durable response (Blood 2023, PMID 36821768).

Subtype-specific clonal evolution measured by serial ctDNA: TP53-disrupted subtype drives primary refractoriness via persistence of the founding TP53 clone; MCD subtype clears baseline mutations, remits, then relapses through branched evolution; 77.1% (37/48) of progressors acquired new alterations, enriched in cell cycle, p53, PI3K/AKT and epigenetic regulators (BMC Medicine 2026, PMID 41776568).

CNS as a pharmacologic sanctuary: glofitamab detectable in CSF in only 60% of R/R PCNSL patients, CSF/plasma ratio up to 0.44%; despite this, ORR 75%, CR 50%, median PFS 15.4 months, and CSF ctDNA clearance tracked radiographic response while re-emergence preceded progression (Am J Hematol 2026, PMID 42035265). Subclinical blood-brain-barrier leakage is measurable in DLBCL patients before any CNS relapse (Tissue Barriers 2026, PMID 42400917).

Microenvironmental rewiring in transformed FL: MYC represses miR-29a/b/c, de-repressing TRAF4 and strongly activating CD40 signaling in 90% of tFL — an adaptation to reduced CD40L+ T-cell numbers in the tFL niche. Low miR-29 independently predicts shorter OS (Leukemia 2026, PMID 41714403).

Differential graft-versus-lymphoma sensitivity: with identical myeloablative conditioning, 5-yr PFS/OS were 56%/56% in PTCL vs 24%/28% in DLBCL; NRM identical (35% vs 34%) but post-transplant relapse mortality 10% vs 36% — i.e. T-cell lymphoma is immunologically controllable in a way DLBCL is not (Leuk Lymphoma 2024, PMID 39660415).

Effector-to-target and inflammatory burden as prognostic proxies: post-CAR-T relapse OS is independently worsened by CRP >=30 mg/L and ECOG >=2, consistent with a systemic inflammatory/tumour-burden axis rather than pure tumour genetics (DESCAR-T, PMID 42099680).

TP53 loss confers chemoresistance in MCL but BTK inhibition partially bypasses it (TRIANGLE), implying the p53-dependent apoptotic route and the BCR-survival route are separable targets in the same cell.

CD30-directed ADC (brentuximab) works only in the CD30-high subset of PTCL; pooled ORR 68%, CR 43%, longest median PFS 8.3 months, longest median OS 26.3 months (J Investig Med 2025, PMID 39324259) — antigen-density dependence is explicit.

EBV lytic-switch ('kick-and-kill'): nanatinostat (HDAC1/3i) induces the full EBV lytic cycle across latency types and kills at nanomolar concentrations; with valganciclovir ~40% ORR in R/R EBV-associated lymphomas (J Med Virol 2026, PMID 42517423) — a distinct, virus-state-dependent kill mechanism relevant to NK/T-cell disease.
modellable: Post-CAR-T relapse hazard is strongly front-loaded: median time to relapse 2.7 months, 35% of relapses within 2 months, but 39.9% of all failures are 'late' (>3 months). Model as a two-component (or mixture) hazard, not a single exponential.

Cure-fraction structure: 5-yr PFS 29%, 5-yr OS 40%, 5-yr lymphoma-specific survival 53%. The 13-point gap between OS and lymphoma-specific survival is non-relapse mortality (5-yr NRM 16.2%, >50% of it after 2 years). Any cell-level sim must carry a competing-risk death process independent of tumour burden.

Second-malignancy hazard as an explicit late compartment: 9% (24/275) at median 58 months, of which 15/24 therapy-related myeloid neoplasms — i.e. a stem-cell-compartment mutational process running in parallel to the lymphoma.

ctDNA MRD detection threshold and prevalence: PhasED-Seq tracks phased variants; identifiable in 99% of patients; EOT MRD-positive prevalence 17%; MRD+ vs MRD- 3-yr PFS 17% vs 85%. Use ~1 in 10^6 as the achievable per-molecule detection floor when simulating a residual-cell readout.

ctDNA kinetic rates for an intervention arm: median 97.7% reduction from baseline over the interim interval with allogeneic CAR-T versus a median 26.6% increase under observation (ALPHA3). These give directly usable per-day net growth/kill rates for a residual-disease compartment.

Vein-to-vein time as a hard delay parameter with real variance: 7 days (point-of-care trispecific), 12 days (Thailand POC), 40 days infusion delay / 49 days decision-to-infusion (Korean commercial tisa-cel). Bridging-therapy ORR before infusion 40.6%, CR 14.1%. Model disease growth during the manufacturing gap explicitly.
CNS drug penetration ratio: CSF/plasma up to 0.44% for glofitamab, detectable in only 60% of patients — a concrete compartment-transfer coefficient for a CNS sanctuary module.

Somatic lesion frequencies for an MCL virtual cohort: ATM mutation 41.7%, TP53 mutation 23.5%, KMT2D 23.5%, ATM deletion 24%, CDKN2A loss 22%; high-risk phenotype flags Ki-67 >30% and blastoid variant. TP53 hazard ratio ~10 without ibrutinib vs ~1.9 with it — a switchable resistance multiplier.

Transition rates for an FL natural-history model: POD24 in ~20% of treated FL; histologic transformation in 10-15% of all FL; POD24 with retained histology median EFS ~9.8 months and 5-yr OS ~71%, with lymphoma (not transformation) as the dominant cause of death.

PTCL absorbing-state rule: failing EFS6 -> 5-yr subsequent OS 12%; failing EFS24 -> 17%. A simple two-gate rule reproduces most of the PTCL survival curve. Baseline PTCL-NOS/AITL 5-yr OS 33.5%, ALCL 61.2%.

Attrition cascade for an access/health-system layer: 100 patients starting 1L -> 30 reach 2L -> among the fit and eligible only 25% get 2L CAR-T (35.7% at 3L); 13% die within 12 months of 1L without any 2L. Cost node: median total POC CAR-T cost USD 111,231 (Thailand) versus commercial list prices several-fold higher.

Salvage response ladder after CAR-T failure, for sequencing simulations: any salvage ORR 39.1% / CR 27.6% (median OS 6.5 mo); late-failure salvage ORR 22.6% (median OS 4.4 mo); glofitamab median OS 17.3 mo, 2-yr OS 38.3%; radiotherapy 12-mo PFS-2 41.5%.

R/R FL durability priors for a modality-comparison sim: 24-month PFS liso-cel 65.4%, axi-cel 62.0%, zanubrutinib+obinutuzumab 53.8%, mosunetuzumab 49.3%, epcoritamab 43.7%, obinutuzumab 24.7% (PFS RMST24 19.5 to 11.9 months).

Consolidation effect size in PCNSL: 3-yr PFS 78% vs 51% (HR 0.43) for HCT-ASCT vs R-DeVIC, but only 63% of enrolled patients ever reach randomization — the eligibility filter is as large as the treatment effect and should be modelled as a selection gate.

Elderly/unfit DLBCL dose-intensity parameters: R-mini-CHOP vs full R-CHOP in median-age-81 patients gave 2-yr PFS 51% vs 68% and OS 60% vs 75%; patients >=85 still did better with any anthracycline than none; rituximab alone in palliative intent improved 2-yr OS 42% vs 22%. Chemo-free ZR2: CR 65%, 2-yr PFS 67%, OS 82%.
open_questions: Is ctDNA-MRD a surrogate for cure or only a prognostic marker? As of Sept 2026 no completed randomized interventional trial has shown that modifying therapy on ctDNA status improves outcomes. ALPHA3's EFS interim is mid-2027, primary mid-2028; SHORTEN-ctDNA and NCT06748521 (de-escalation) are still enrolling. Trial-level surrogacy (change in MRD -> change in survival across trials) has not been established in lymphoma the way it has in childhood ALL or myeloma.

The MRD-positive-but-PET-negative population is now identifiable (MRD PPV 68% vs PET 56%) but the right intervention for it is unknown — consolidation CAR-T, bispecific, or nothing. This is the single most tractable simulation question in the field.

Why does the same CD19-directed pressure produce early primary refractoriness in TP53-disrupted DLBCL but late branched relapse in MCD? Cell-level models of clonal architecture under immune pressure could discriminate selection of a pre-existing resistant subclone from de novo acquisition.

Post-CAR-T, post-bispecific ('double-refractory') disease is now the fastest-growing population and has essentially no standard of care; DESCAR-T authors call explicitly for dedicated prospective trials in it.

Whether T-cell-lymphoma outcomes lag because of tumour biology (CHOP-insensitive, 30 rare subtypes, no shared surface target as clean as CD19) or because of trial infrastructure (rarity, heterogeneous R/R populations pooled together). The strong graft-versus-lymphoma effect in PTCL but not DLBCL argues the immune axis is exploitable and under-exploited. CAR-T in T-cell disease additionally has to solve fratricide (CONQUER, ASCO 2026).

Whether the TRIANGLE result generalizes: does BTK inhibition truly neutralize TP53 risk in MCL, or only defer it? The MRD-guided CARMAN trial (first-line brexu-cel for high-risk MCL) is designed to test early intensification.

How much of the survival gap in elderly/unfit DLBCL is biology versus under-treatment. The observation that patients >=85 still benefit from any anthracycline suggests substantial avoidable loss to conservative dosing, but bispecific-based non-anthracycline frontline (epcoritamab + R-miniCVP, ASCO 2026) has only short follow-up in small exploratory cohorts.

Whether point-of-care/decentralized manufacturing actually closes the access gap. A Cytotherapy 2026 analysis concluded decentralization by itself is unlikely to be the main cost driver and may lose scale efficiency — the access benefit may come from shorter vein-to-vein times and reduced logistics rather than price.
In PCNSL, whether bispecifics can substitute for or precede transplant, given a CSF/plasma ratio under 0.5% but a 75% ORR — i.e. how much CNS drug exposure is actually needed.

In transformed FL, whether the reservoir is the common progenitor cell rather than the aggressive clone, which would predict that eradicating the DLBCL-phase population without touching the FL-phase reservoir yields the observed relapse pattern.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: the 2026 unmet-nee.caveats: Several of the strongest 2026 numbers come from retrospective registries (DESCAR-T, Flatiron, NCDB, Finnish Cancer Registry) or from single-arm trials with constructed external control arms (LYSA BiCAR), not randomized comparisons — treat effect sizes as association-grade, not causal. The ALPHA3 figures are an interim futility analysis with n=12 per arm on a biomarker endpoint (MRD clearance), reported in a company press release, not a peer-reviewed efficacy readout; do not model it as a demonstrated survival benefit. The TRIANGLE TP53 subgroup result (HR ~1.9 vs ~10) reaches me via EHA 2026 conference coverage rather than the primary publication text, and is a subgroup analysis in a trial not powered for it — I have marked it medium confidence. Some POD24 figures (median EFS 9.8 months, 5-yr OS 71%, ~20% POD24 incidence) come from search-result summaries of the LEO Consortium Blood Advances 2025 paper whose abstract I could not retrieve in full; verify against the primary article before using them as calibration targets. The pooled POD24 salvage response rates carry extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 94% for CR) and pool across very different populations, so the point estimates are unreliable as simulation inputs — use the per-trial durability benchmarks (reconstructed IPD) instead. Publisher paywalls blocked direct access to Lancet, Nature, Blood and Blood Advances full texts; where those are cited I worked from Europe PMC abstracts, which occasionally truncate the final numbers. Finally, I found no authoritative 2026 consensus document that explicitly ranks the field's unsolved problems; the closest quotable statements are Dreyling et al., Lancet Haematology 2026 ("current recommendations are still largely based on age rather than biology"), the DESCAR-T conclusion ("overall prognosis and treatment efficacy remain dismal, highlighting the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies and dedicated prospective trials in this emerging double-refractory population"), the NCDB PTCL conclusion ("gains remain modest in PTCL-NOS and AITL... highlighting unmet needs for more effective therapies"), and the 2026 Am J Hematol DLBCL update ("the feasibility of using ctDNA for prospective decision-making remains a challenge" and "the optimal treatment of double hit lymphoma and triple hit lymphoma remains undefined"). The Mayo lySMART 2026 guideline separately names Richter transformation as an unmet need with survival under 24 months.
